title: STRATEGY records the 2026-08-15 staff-member directive as a ratified stakeholder amendment

The executing session commits a dated STRATEGY.md amendment that: (1) re-scopes the Phase 5 'no new roles, hosts, or platform investment' hold for this program; (2) records the directive's bearing on construct-7t0 without closing it (the formal product-vs-feature answer stays Gerald's); (3) licenses tracker writes under the existing consent tiers; (4) licenses host breadth: nanobot (HKUDS) stays the non-IDE dogfood host, goose and pi are added as probe targets, no new framework is adopted (skills + MCP is the portability seam); (5) licenses the 2.x cleanup as remove-and-rewire-to-3.x; (6) licenses defined API connectors with a hard use/build gate as an amendment to commitment 1's connector reading; (7) names consumer-app confidence (admin-app, blackstory) as a program goal; (8) states that the old 'killed ADR/RFC/PRD documentation system' decision killed internal process, not user-facing deliverable shapes. title: Composed documents were bullets by structural necessity, no prose/tables/diagrams
description: Gerald, 2026-08-13: 'These are lists are bullet points; do artifacts not have templates that give the artifacts structure and depth. I would expect to see a mix of prose, tables, visuals and handwritten diagrams. I thought construct shipped that stuff for artifacts.' Checked: STRATEGY.md already admits 'Deliverable templates remain unported... still aspiration.' ComposedClaim {section, text, from} was one sentence per claim, rendered unconditionally as a bullet regardless of what the underlying role deliverable actually contained — real, structured, multi-paragraph prose in every case checked.
acceptance_criteria: ComposedClaim supports at minimum bullet, paragraph, table, and diagram kinds; a table renders as real markdown with headers and all rows, or is dropped whole if malformed rather than rendered broken; a diagram renders as a fenced mermaid block; the support-check pass shown a table or diagram claim sees its real content, not just a caption, so an invented row or edge is caught the same way an invented sentence already is; proven end-to-end through the real compose CLI, not just at the data layer.
notes: 2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): fix landed in 48f0a027 on main (verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor), which predates this bead — same pattern as every other retroactively-filed bead this session. Benign.
close_reason:
Fixed (48f0a027). ComposedClaim carries a kind: bullet (unchanged default), paragraph, table, diagram. Table claims validated whole (headers, rows, width-consistency) and dropped rather than rendered broken; diagram claims carry mermaid source rendered in a fenced block (kernel/run/publish.ts's renderComposedClaim, beside every other record/reader view this system already draws). Composer prompt names all four kinds and warns diagrams are the easiest place to imply an unestablished relationship. Support-check pass shows a table's real rows and a diagram's real structure to the checking role, not just a caption, so an invented row or edge is caught the same as an invented sentence. Proven end-to-end: a stand-in host returning one claim of each kind through the real compose CLI produces an actual markdown table with every row, a fenced mermaid block with structure intact, and real prose (not a long bullet) — asserted on rendered output. Full gate green including smoke (1976 tests).

Not done, stated in the commit: no ASCII/ other diagram notation, mermaid only; no grading of whether a claim chose the RIGHT kind, only that whichever kind it chose renders correctly and passes the same fabrication screen bullets already did — a prompting/quality question the prompt guides but cannot structurally enforce, same limit as every other model-authored field in this system.

title: A claim that survived attribution vanished for how its section was spelled
description: Found immediately while verifying the role-attribution fix (construct-8y03): recomposing the same PRD run a second time on the same free model produced 9 claims kept but every one of the spec shape's six sections still empty. The render loop in cli/index.ts matched claim.section against shape.sections with exact string equality, the identical defect class as the role bug, at a different call site — and unscreened, so a mismatch never surfaced anywhere, not even as a discard line.
acceptance_criteria: A claim's section is canonicalized against the shape's declared section names the same way its role is canonicalized against dispatched roles; a genuinely unrecognized section is discarded and disclosed, never silently dropped; verified by replaying the exact claims from the second broken compose.
notes: 2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): fix landed in 721a32d7 on main (verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor), which predates this bead — filed and closed retroactively, same pattern as construct-8y03 and construct-sszq earlier the same session. Benign.
close_reason: Fixed (721a32d7). rolekey.ts generalized to a plain normalized-lookup mechanism shared by both roles and sections (roleLookup, sectionLookup — same implementation, named for each use). screenComposition now takes the shape's section names as an optional third parameter and canonicalizes claim.section exactly as it canonicalizes claim.from, discarding and disclosing a genuine mismatch rather than letting it silently vanish. Composer prompt tightened to name the exact section identifiers. Verified against the actual second failure: the 6 real mixed-case claims ('Requirements', 'Non-Goals', 'open questions') from the broken second compose replay clean, all kept and correctly placed. Full gate green including smoke (1962 tests).

title: Correctly-attributed claims were refused for how the role was spelled
description: Gerald, 2026-08-13, after the first three real documents were dispatched to a live model: 'It didnt actually ship a strategy document, prd, or rfc structured and aligned with the template. it gave me shit.' Two of three came back with 0 claims kept (0/11, 0/8). screenComposition and screenPosition matched an attributed role against the dispatched set with exact string equality; a smaller free model wrote real dispatched roles in humanized form ('Product Scoping' for 'product-scoping') and every genuine, correctly-grounded claim was discarded alongside the actual fabrications (a document byline as a role, Construct's own internal position-role id cited as a fifth specialist). The guard was correct in principle and indiscriminate in practice.
acceptance_criteria: A claim or restsOn entry naming a dispatched role in a different case or with underscores instead of hyphens resolves to that role rather than being refused; a name that does not resolve to any dispatched role under any spelling is still refused in full; verified by replaying the exact claims from the real broken document through the fixed code.
notes: 2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): the fix landed in dad3e3ca on main (verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor), which predates this bead — filed and closed retroactively after Gerald flagged the broken documents, same pattern as construct-sszq earlier the same session. Benign.
close_reason: Fixed (dad3e3ca). New shared module kernel/run/rolekey.ts: normalizes case/separators before comparing an attributed role against the dispatched set, resolving to the real identifier and refusing only what genuinely doesn't match under any spelling. Applied at both call sites with this exact defect — screenComposition (compose.ts, claim.from) and screenPosition (position.ts, restsOn and resolved took/over) — the second only surfaced because the RFC document happened to exercise it. Composer and position prompts (hosts/compose.ts) now name the literal identifier to use with a worked example, reducing how often the fallback fires without depending on it. Verified against the actual failure: the 6 real claims from the broken held-lessons-prd.md replay clean through the fixed screenComposition, all kept. Full gate green including smoke (1958 tests).

title: Composition arranges; nothing takes a position across the concerns
description: The composer prompt said in as many words: 'Arranging is the ENTIRE job. You may not add a claim, resolve a question they left open, decide something none of them decided.' That rule was written against a real failure - a composer asserting scope or sequence a role was separately dispatched to establish - and in guarding it forbade the thing that makes a strategy a strategy. On a recorded run three of five roles independently reached the same call and the document never said so, because saying so would have been deciding something none of them decided; the reader had to count bullets to find the recommendation. The prohibition is on the wrong noun. A fact is something Construct cannot know except through a role that read the ground and inventing one is fabrication; a judgment is what the facts add up to and nobody was dispatched for it. Construct is the only participant that read everything and must say what it adds up to.
acceptance_criteria: A composed document opens with Construct's own call, signed as a judgment across concerns rather than any role's finding; every factual sentence in it names the roles it rests on and one resting on nobody is refused structurally; the call resolves cross-role disagreements naming the side not taken and the reason; it carries its strongest objection and a pre-mortem or is reported short; each role sees the call beside its own deliverable and can say it misreads them, on the support call that already runs; a position that cannot be produced leaves the arranged document standing.
close_reason: Landed de21f75d. Verified live by recomposing run-20260813174506233: the document opens with Construct's own signed call, every factual sentence names the roles it rests on, it resolved two cross-role disagreements naming the side not taken with a reason (not arrival order), and carried its strongest objection, a pre-mortem, and one undecided item with what would settle it. The role veto fired on first use - three roles objected to the same clause and strategy-alignment's objection was correct, that the call stated as settled what its deliverable framed as a question for the owner. Repairing the position on an objection rather than reporting it is filed separately.

title: A failing structural gate sends the deliverable back, once
description: Every structural verdict on run-20260813160805209 failed (claims-cited x5, ground-exhausted x5) and the run composed a strategy from all five deliverables anyway. The coordinator records verdicts and moves on; no repair path exists in the kernel. ground-exhausted failing 5/5 means every role named documents it never opened - the gate caught the cop-out by name, five times, and the run shipped regardless. Add a bounded repair round: on a failed structural check, re-dispatch the author once with the verdict detail, re-run the checks, append the new draft. One round only (same stop rule as research and closing). Record must distinguish passed-first-time from passed-on-repair.
acceptance_criteria: A deliverable failing a structural gate is re-dispatched exactly once before composition; the repaired draft is appended (log stays append-only, latest draft wins); verdicts re-recorded so promotionState's last-verdict-wins rule resolves; a still-failing deliverable composes with the existing disclosure; repair is visible in the work log and distinguishable from a first-pass pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: A document is composed from deliverables that failed their challenges, and never says so
description: Verified against the recorded BlackStory run (run-20260813133151758) on 2026-08-13. All five deliverables recorded failing:['claims-cited'] — evidence-provenance, product-scoping, program-sequencing and strategy-alignment sit at promotion state 'challenged', privacy at 'draft' with legal-issue-spot still outstanding. Not one of them passed the citation gate the spine declares on every brief. The composed document was produced from all five anyway and presents as authoritative: it reports what the composer discarded and what the support screen refused, states that nothing was added by the composing, and says nothing whatsoever about its sources having failed their own gates. The compose command in src/cli/index.ts selects sources on task.state === 'done' and never reads promotionOf(). So the one screen a reader has — 'every claim is one of the roles, checked against it' — is true about the composing step and false about the material, and the document says the true half. This is the same class as the rest of this epic seen from the other end: the run knew, and nothing carried what it knew to the person reading the output.
acceptance_criteria: compose reads each source's promotion state and the reader is told, in the document, which deliverables had failing or outstanding challenges and which; a run where every source is clean reads exactly as it does today; whether a failed source is refused outright or composed-with-disclosure is a recorded decision rather than an implicit one
notes: 2026-08-13: found while judging the BlackStory deliverables against the reader rubric, not by looking for it. The promotion states are already recorded and already correct — this is purely a surfacing gap. Related: construct-kpkv.5 wired the reader rubric in, which is what put a judging pass over real deliverables for the first time.
close_reason: Landed: compose reads promotionOf per source and discloses failing/outstanding challenges above the claims. Disclosure-not-refusal recorded as the decision in compose.ts. Full gate green (1815 tests).

title: The personas we solve for are a document nothing runs against a real deliverable
description: docs/persona-acceptance-rubrics.md defines who Construct is for and what each of them requires before they would call a deliverable adequate: a common floor (C1-C4) plus must/should lines for engineer, PM, operations, legal, compliance, R&D leadership, director/VP, architect, support/on-call and designer/UX. It was committed before any judging, deliberately, so it could not be tuned to pass what it grades. Nothing in src/ reads it. It is used to judge fixture-organization harness runs and has never been run against a real one. The BlackStory strategy run is the proof of what that costs: it violates must-lines that were already written down and agreed. C2 (actionable as given, numbered issues with the step that resolves each, not a restated gap) fails against a nine-item 'what nobody answered' list. P1, S3 and O2 (an owner is named; 'the team' is not an owner) fail against a document that states in its own words that all three fixes are [unowned]. S1 (the price of saying yes is named specifically - the work that stops or slips) fails: no capability is costed against another. The four mechanism fixes under this epic - reading the ground, closing the gaps, choosing the shape, ranking code - would each have improved that document and none of them would have made it pass P1, S3, O2 or S1. Mechanism without the reader's standard produces a better-built document that the reader still rejects.
acceptance_criteria: the reader-acceptance lines that are structurally checkable become declared challenges keyed to the concern, the way strongest-objection is keyed to DECISION_CLASS_DOMAINS in run/outcome.ts, so a deliverable that names no owner for what it recommends does not promote past draft; the lines that need judgment are recorded as needing a judging pass rather than silently dropped; the rubric document and whatever code enforces it are checked against each other by lint so they cannot drift; the BlackStory run is re-judged against the rubric and the verdict recorded with the judging model named
notes: 2026-08-13: raised by Gerald mid-session as the steel thread - understand the persona and intent, define them, and keep them a constant consideration rather than a phase. They ARE defined; the defect is that nothing carries them into a real run. P0 within this epic because it is the line between mechanism and outcome: the other four beads make the document better built, this one makes it acceptable to the person receiving it. DISPATCH: Fable/Opus-class for the judgment of which rubric lines are structurally checkable versus judgment-only; the wiring itself is Sonnet-class. Self-contained: rubric at docs/persona-acceptance-rubrics.md, the keying pattern to copy is DECISION_CLASS_DOMAINS in src/kernel/run/outcome.ts, the challenge shape to copy is src/kernel/challenge/catalog.ts. Do NOT invent new rubric lines - the document is the source and was committed before judging on purpose. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Landed ad07d8f1 + this commit. Reader rubric enforced: 18 concern-keyed must-lines carried, 8 structural gates declared per concern, two-way parity lint in npm run lint, org map now asks the rule. Verified against the real BlackStory deliverables — S3 correctly fails strategy-alignment. Per-deliverable re-judging surfaced construct-kpkv.6.

title: After the cutover, construct cleanup would delete v3's own state — the XDG paths are shared
description:
Found completing construct-1we.2, and it lands squarely on construct-1we.3 which is the very next step.

The cleanup catalog removes ~/.local/state/construct, ~/.local/share/construct, ~/.cache/construct and ~/.config/construct as predecessor traces. v3 resolves its OWN directories to exactly those paths — kernel/paths.ts uses APP = 'construct' under the standard XDG variables, and the packaged smoke asserts the store lands at XDG_DATA_HOME/construct/construct.db.

So the moment construct-1we.3 installs v3 and it starts writing, 'construct cleanup' becomes a command that deletes the caller's own store: the SQLite database holding every work log entry, every task row, every raised decision, and the capability secret. Append-only triggers do not help — the file is unlinked, not written to.

This is the same family as construct-7pp, one layer up. There the fix was that an uninstaller may only remove what it installed; here the uninstaller cannot currently TELL what it installed, because the predecessor and the successor were given the same name and therefore the same directories. Until v2 is gone from a machine the ambiguity is harmless, which is exactly why it stayed invisible through Phase 1: cleanup was only ever run while v2 was the only thing there.

Sharpened by construct-3fr: v3 now also publishes under the predecessor's package name, so the two agree on every identifier a naive check might use.
acceptance_criteria: Running 'construct cleanup' on a machine where v3 is installed and has state does not remove v3's store, secret, or config, and says so rather than silently skipping. The distinguishing evidence is something durable rather than a version guess — the v3 store is a SQLite file with a schema table the predecessor never wrote, so its presence identifies the directory's owner. Whatever is chosen, a machine carrying BOTH must have v2's traces removed and v3's kept, proven by a fixture-home test seeding both. The packaged smoke gains a case that runs cleanup against a home where v3 has already written, and asserts the store survives.
notes: 2026-08-04 filed on completion of the v2 nuke, before construct-1we.3 runs. P0 because the window opens the moment v3 is installed, and the damage is the one thing the system promises is append-only. Timing note: this is NOT a reason to delay 1we.3 — v2 is now fully absent, so nobody has a reason to run cleanup on this machine again. It is a reason not to ship the alpha with the command in this state, since a new user running 'construct cleanup' after using v3 loses their work. DISPATCH: judgment then mechanical, Sonnet-class or better. The store-shape check is the honest signal; a version file would be written by whoever wrote last.
close_reason: cleanup refuses to remove a directory the running Construct owns, identified by construct.db or capability-secret — files the predecessor never wrote. Predecessor traces still go; a same-machine fixture with BOTH installed proves both halves. The packaged smoke now runs cleanup --yes --all against a home where the spine has written a real store through the installed package and asserts the store is byte-identical afterwards. Summary counts 'kept' separately so it cannot report a deletion that did not happen. Gate: lint, typecheck, 1433 tests, smoke.

title: cleanup deletes every hook, not Construct's — it would destroy v3's own tooling
description:
Found running construct-1we.2's mandatory dry-run, before anything was removed. src/kernel/cleanup/catalog.ts strips the whole `hooks` block from .claude/settings.json whenever any hooks exist, without checking whose they are:

    const hooks = settings.hooks;
    if (hooks && Object.keys(hooks).length > 0) { delete settings.hooks; changes.push('hooks'); }

The item's own label says 'un-merge Construct keys' and its describe() promises it 'preserves any user-added keys'. It does not. Anything under hooks is treated as Construct's.

MEASURED, NOT READ. This repo's own .claude/settings.json was copied into a throwaway project under an isolated HOME and 'construct cleanup --yes --scope=project' was run against it. Result: '[stripped: hooks]' followed by 'removed (file was Construct-only)' — the file was DELETED, because emptying the hooks block left nothing else in it and the emptiness test then judged the whole file Construct-owned.

What that would have destroyed in the v3 checkout: the PostToolUse no-fabrication-lint hook (scripts/hooks/no-fabrication-lint.mjs, this repo's own code) and both 'bd prime' hooks (SessionStart and PreCompact), which are what load beads workflow context into every session. None of the three is a v2 trace.

This is worse than a missed trace. cleanup's whole promise is that it removes the predecessor and leaves everything else alone, and the one checkout where it is most likely to be run — this one — is the one where it does the most damage.
acceptance_criteria: A hooks block containing only non-Construct hooks is left completely untouched, and the file is not deleted. A hooks block containing a mix leaves the non-Construct entries in place and removes only Construct's. Construct's own hooks are identified by something durable — the manifest convention the agents/commands items already use, or a marker written at init — not by a denylist of command strings that rots. Proven by a test built from this repo's real .claude/settings.json, asserting the file still exists and all three hooks survive. The emptiness test may only delete a file it actually emptied.
notes: 2026-08-04 filed from the halted construct-1we.2 nuke. Blocks the project-scope half of that bead: the machine scope was not implicated by this defect. DISPATCH: judgment, Sonnet-class or better — deciding how Construct's own hooks are identified is the bead. Note .claude/agents/ and .claude/commands/ already solve exactly this with a .construct-manifest listing what Construct wrote; that is the house pattern to follow. Close gate: full repo gate plus the real-settings test.
close_reason: Fixed and verified against this machine's real files: settings.json hooks partitioned by launcher path (repo's own hooks survive byte-identical), MCP registrations matched by the command they run (construct-mcp stripped, all eight unrelated servers preserved), and ~/.construct now a machine-scope ask-risk item reporting 676MB. Full gate green: lint, typecheck, 1430 tests, smoke.

title: Reclaim the construct package name and restart numbering at 3.0.0-alpha.0
description:
Gerald's decision, 2026-08-04: v3 ships under the predecessor's package name @geraldmaron/construct rather than @geraldmaron/construct-engine, with the version lineage continuing from v2's 2.1.1 as 3.0.0-alpha.0 instead of restarting at 0.0.0.

WHY THIS UNBLOCKS THE RELEASE. construct-506.4 was blocked on Gerald minting an npm granular token, because the existing NPM_TOKEN is scoped read+write to the single package @geraldmaron/construct and npm returns E404 when a token may not CREATE a package. Under this decision v3 IS that package, so the existing token is already sufficient and the human gate disappears.

WHY NOT 0.0.0 ON THAT PACKAGE. npm publish sets the latest dist-tag to whatever is published unless --tag is passed. Publishing 0.0.0 to a package whose latest is 2.1.1 would make a from-scratch rewrite the default install for existing consumers (~3,439 downloads in the month to 2026-08-03). A prerelease under --tag alpha cannot move latest, so 3.0.0-alpha.0 expresses STRATEGY's 'no stability promise until the Phase 5 second-user gate' through npm's own semantics rather than through a number that merely implies it. .github/workflows/release.yml already publishes with --tag alpha, so no workflow logic changes — only its comment.

WHAT CANNOT BE DONE. v2's 48 published versions (1.0.0 through 2.1.1) cannot be removed. npm allows unpublish within 72 hours; after that only when there are no dependents, fewer than 300 downloads per week, and a single maintainer. This package is months past the window and around 800 downloads per week. Deprecating the range with a pointer to the rewrite is the achievable equivalent and is deliberately left as a separate step so it is a decision rather than a side effect.

Nothing needs to be killed in the repo: CHANGELOG.md contains only v3 work under ## Unreleased, and this repo's git history begins at the Phase 0 bootstrap. v2's changelog and history stay in construct-legacy, which is archived rather than merged.
acceptance_criteria: package.json names @geraldmaron/construct at version 3.0.0-alpha.0; STRATEGY.md's version-lineage paragraph records the change in place, per its own rule that changing a commitment means editing that section; README.md no longer tells a reader to install a package that will not exist; every remaining construct-engine reference in source comments and workflow comments is corrected; the full repo gate passes; construct-506.4's notes record that its human gate is gone. Publishing is NOT part of this bead.
notes: 2026-08-04 filed from the session that landed the Phase 2 engineering sweep. Gerald chose 'make the change, do not publish'. The tag re-cut sequence documented on construct-506.4 still applies and still matters: the v0.0.0 tag points at 681e057, now ~30 commits behind main, and must be deleted locally and on the remote rather than re-run. The next tag is v3.0.0-alpha.0 and release.yml's tag/version equality check will enforce the match.
close_reason: package.json is @geraldmaron/construct at 3.0.0-alpha.0, STRATEGY.md's lineage paragraph amended in place, README and every remaining reference corrected, lockfile regenerated and npm ci verified, full gate green including a packaged smoke that installs the renamed package as a consumer. Publishing deliberately not done.

title: Cutover: retire v2 Construct and relaunch on v3, built and tested locally
description:
The end state this tracker points at: the v2 Construct on this machine is removed and v3 — this repo — is the construct in daily use, installed and tested locally. No npm publish gates this: the cutover installs from a locally packed tarball (the packaged-install smoke already proves that path in a scratch home), while construct-506.4 stays the distribution gate for the public alpha only. bd refuses epic->task edges, so the sequencing lives on the child tasks.

Child sequence (corrected 2026-08-03 after live investigation, folded in from NOTES 2026-08-04): prove-isolated (1we.1, done) -> NUKE v2 (1we.2) -> install v3 (1we.3). NOT install-first: v2 holds both the global bin name and the XDG dir identity, so v3 cannot be installed for real until v2 is gone. 1we.2 must also npm uninstall -g @geraldmaron/construct after running cleanup. The nuke waits on the Phase 2 dogfood (construct-r67.9, done) because you do not delete the old tool before the new one has survived real outcomes.

## Success Criteria
v2 is absent from the machine and all checkouts, construct-legacy is archived read-only, v3 is installed globally as `construct` from a locally packed tarball, owns the state dirs, and has run its first real outcome against the real HOME (1we.3's AC).
notes:
2026-08-03 filed during full reconcile. Epic carries no dependency edge on construct-r67 deliberately: Phase 2's exit includes an external-user probe (r67.10), a second host adapter (r67.4) and the MCP write surface (3sa), none of which gate a local single-user cutover. The narrower true gates are edges on the child tasks.
2026-08-03 reorder after live investigation: the child sequence is prove-isolated (1we.1) -> nuke (1we.2) -> install (1we.3), NOT install-first as the epic description says. v2 holds both the global bin name and the XDG dir identity, so v3 cannot be installed for real until v2 is gone. 1we.2 must also npm uninstall -g @geraldmaron/construct after running cleanup.
close_reason: v2 is absent from this machine and construct-legacy is archived read-only; v3 is installed globally as 'construct' from a locally packed tarball, owns the state dirs, and has run its first real outcome against the real HOME. The per-checkout ask-risk remainder is construct-2rq and blocks nothing.

title: Implication map's 0.000 miss rate does not survive wording it did not author
description:
Found by the construct-r67.9 dogfood, which is exactly what that quota exists for. The map scores miss 0/37 = 0.000 against tests/kernel/implication/fixtures/labeled-outcomes.json (target <= 0.15). Ten outcomes written independently, in the words a user would actually use, score miss 10/18 = 0.556 — 3.7x the target — measured with the gate's own method.

The corpus is distribution-balanced (40% non-engineering, 20% legal, as the quota asks) but it is phrased in the catalog's own vocabulary, so the gate measures vocabulary overlap rather than implication. Same domain, two wordings:

  employment    corpus 'Hire two contractors to run our support desk' (hire, contractors) -> employment
                mine   'Bring on two part-time people to help with support over the holidays' -> NOTHING
  accessibility corpus 'Add screen reader support to the dashboard' (screen reader) -> accessibility
                mine   'Make the app usable by our blind customers' -> NOTHING (only product-scoping)
  commerce-tax  corpus 'Rebuild the checkout flow to accept subscriptions' (checkout, subscriptions) -> commerce-tax
                mine   'Start charging our European customers in euros instead of dollars' -> NOTHING (privacy + product-scoping instead)

Three of the ten implicated NO domain at all, which is why this blocks construct-r67.9: an outcome that implicates nothing queues no tasks, so it cannot run end to end through the spine at all. The quota cannot be met while this holds.

Secondary, same surface: over-broad keywords are cited as evidence. 'single sign-on' cites signal 'sign' for contracts; 'pilot' (a trial) cites product-scoping in an aviation-free sentence. The over rate 5/13 = 0.385 is still inside the 0.6 target, so the gate does not catch this either. Citing a wrong signal is worse than scoring one, because map.ts's own comment says signals exist so the inference 'can be argued with rather than taken on faith'.

title: Phase 2: OpenCode host adapter — first-class, pinned and conformance-probed
description: Implement the OpenCode adapter behind the harvested host adapter interface (src/kernel/hosts/interface.ts), execute(role, task, tools) -> deliverable. notes:
2026-08-03 VERIFIED against a live OpenCode 1.15.4, not just unit-tested.

End to end through the adapter interface: createOpenCodeAdapter -> init() -> invoke({role:'privacy issue-spotter', task:'Read dpa.txt. Name the single biggest privacy risk in it, in one sentence.'}) returned status ok, one completed 'read' tool call, and a correct one-sentence deliverable naming the sub-processor discretion clause. Pin: PINNED_VERSION 1.15.4 in src/hosts/opencode/pin.ts, alongside 8 named behavioral expectations. scripts/probe-opencode-conformance.mjs checks all 8 against a live binary. Verified all three exit paths, not assumed: 0 with all 8 holding on the real host; 1 on version drift (proved with a shim reporting 9.9.9, which failed version-pinned and printed why it matters); 2 when no binary is reachable, so 'could not run' never reads as 'passed'.

Capturing fixtures from the real host corrected two claims I had written from a 2>&1 transcript: notices go to stderr (stdout under --format json is clean NDJSON), and a failed run DOES exit non-zero. Both were wrong in the first draft of pin.ts and are now recorded accurately. Kept the parser's non-JSON tolerance, documented as an accommodation for stream-merging callers rather than a host behavior.

Adapter lives in src/hosts/opencode/, which fills the exports['./hosts/*'] path r67.12 flagged. No host capability reimplemented (STRATEGY risk 4): no session store, retry policy, tool broker or model routing. Declares only 'interrupt' and 'concurrent'; 'stream' is deliberately NOT declared because the transcript is reduced after exit — our limitation, declared rather than hidden.

Unit tests found a real defect: on a timeout, kill() makes the child exit, so Promise.race between the child and the timer was a coin toss and a timed-out run could return ok. Fixed with an explicit expired flag checked after the race.

30 new tests (1096 -> 1126). Full gate green including the read-only-HOME sterile run and the packaged-install smoke.

title: Construct learns from documents it is fed, never from the work it does
description:
The learning loop exists and closes, which is the part worth protecting: src/kernel/context/loop.ts distills deltas from an ingested note, recordLesson stores them, src/kernel/lessons/admission.ts gates them risk-weighted (a lesson whose source was an ingested external document can never auto-admit, and that rule runs first and cannot be outvoted), and coordinator.ts injects admitted lessons into the dispatch envelope as standing context cited [cite:lesson], never as evidence. That is a real, well-guarded mechanism.

It has exactly one input. grep shows recordLesson has a single caller — the context loop. So Construct learns only from documents somebody hands it, and never from its own operation. Nothing that happens in a run can become a lesson: not a deliverable that failed its structural checks, not a repair that had to be sent back, not a role whose claims were repeatedly unsupported, not a position its own roles objected to, not an inbox decision Gerald resolved against the default the run proposed. All of that is already on the append-only work log — the observations exist and are simply never distilled.

The consequence is that the same mistake is available to be made on every run forever, and the system cannot answer 'what have you learned from working with me'. This is the load-bearing gap behind Gerald's 'what happens when it needs to learn? how does it learn?' (2026-08-13).

The guards that must survive any implementation: a run-derived lesson is still risk-tier gated and still cited [cite:lesson] rather than treated as evidence; a lesson derived from the system's own output must not launder an unverified claim into standing context, which is the exact failure the external-source rule exists to prevent — self-derived and external-derived are different, but neither is trusted for being familiar. Start from what the work log already records rather than adding new observation.
acceptance_criteria: At least one class of run outcome becomes a candidate lesson through the existing admission gate; the provenance of a run-derived lesson is distinguishable from an ingested one at the point of admission and in the record; no self-derived lesson can enter dispatch as evidence; demonstrated on real recorded runs, not fixtures.
notes: 2026-08-13 EDGE (recorded here because bd refuses task->epic edges): serves construct-99x (Phase 4 pack breadth) and depends on nothing currently open. The observations it would distil are already on the append-only work log; no new instrumentation is needed before this can start. Guard that must survive: self-derived and ingested-external lessons are different provenances and neither is trusted for being familiar.
close_reason:
Fixed the load-bearing gap (2846efa0). First run-derived lesson class wired end-to-end: a resolved cross-domain decision (kernel/store/decisions.ts) distills mechanically (no model, verbatim from typed columns) into a lesson candidate via src/kernel/lessons/fromDecisions.ts, wired at 'construct decide' so it fires the moment a resolution exists. Provenance is a third case at the admission gate (runDerived() in lessons/admission.ts), recognized structurally from the citation prefix rather than a caller flag — no schema change, no ALTER on the existing lessons/lesson_admissions tables. Held unconditionally pending a named human, same shape as external-sourced lessons, with its own distinct reason. Verified against real production data, not just fixtures: run against the actual run-20260813172834638:stance decision in the live store caught a real defect (Construct's own reversible-default framing note, which rides the positions array under role 'construct', was being folded in as a fifth specialist's finding) and the distiller was fixed against it before landing. Full gate green (1936 tests).

Deliberately not built: a CLI surface to browse or approve the held queue (filed separately, construct-wwaq, P2) — the mechanism itself is what this bead asked for, and it produces real, verified, inspectable rows; making them reachable without opening the database is useful but not required to close the gap. Also not built: distillation from the other run-outcome classes named in the original description (failed structural checks, sent-back repairs, repeatedly-unsupported claims) — the bead's acceptance criteria asked for 'at least one class,' and the pattern this establishes (mechanical transcription, structural provenance, unconditional human gate) is the template for adding the others.

title: Nothing challenges a vague outcome before the run is staffed and paid for
description:
A role that lacks a fact can raise one ask through the inbox mid-work (src/kernel/run/asks.ts), fail-open, one per run. That is the only place the system handles missing information, and it happens AFTER the outcome has been read, the domains inferred, the roles staffed and the money committed.

Nothing reads the outcome itself and asks whether it is answerable. 'Fix onboarding' infers domains from keywords the same way 'Decide whether to ship the Q4 pilot on the current threat model' does, and dispatches with the same confidence. The failure is invisible: five roles each answer the vague question competently in their own concern, the composition arranges five competent answers to the wrong question, and the position pass now states a call across them. Every check in the system passes, because every check is about faithfulness to deliverables and none is about whether the ask was answerable.

Design constraints from house rules: the anti-nagging rule is structural (one open ask at a time, asking never blocks work), so a clarity gate must not become a questionnaire in front of every outcome. It should fire rarely and only where the ask cannot be staffed sensibly at all, and where it fires it should still be able to proceed on a stated, reversible assumption — the same fail-open shape asks.ts already uses. Cheapest honest version: the staffing step reports what it took the outcome to mean and what it assumed, so a reader sees the interpretation before paying for it.
acceptance_criteria: An outcome too vague to staff is either flagged before dispatch or is dispatched under a stated interpretation the user can see and correct; the path never blocks on an answer; measured against real vague outcomes, not fixtures.
close_reason: Fixed (b62fb7e2). DensifiedIntake carries a new underspecified field, populated by the existing intake-densifier call (no new model call, no new cost) — one sentence naming what staffing would have to guess, empty in the ordinary precise-ask case. Printed in outcome's 'as understood' block and in the context-loop confirm summary. Fail-open throughout: the run proceeds on the stated guess exactly as before, same shape as the existing inbox-ask mechanism. Tested at the densify layer (gap stated vs. not invented) and typechecked/linted/full-gate green (1928 tests). Not built: a hard clarity gate that blocks staffing — the bead's own acceptance criteria ruled that out ('the path never blocks'), and a disclosed guess is the correct shape given the anti-nagging constraint.

title: Construct has two document shapes, and a PRD is neither
description:
src/kernel/run/shapes.ts carries exactly two shapes: review and decision. shapeForOutcome() keyword-matches DECISION_SIGNALS and otherwise returns review. So every ask that is not a decision comes back in the review shape — the-answer, what-each-concern-established, where-they-disagree, what-follows.

Ask Construct for a PRD, a spec, a plan, an incident write-up or a policy and it produces a review OF that subject rather than the artifact. The composition machinery is sound and shape-agnostic; the shape catalog is the narrow part. This is the concrete form of 'this is about more than strategy documents' (Gerald, 2026-08-13).

A PRD shape is not a new pipeline — it is a sections list plus the expectations each section is held to, in the same structure DECISION already uses. The real design question is which shapes earn their place (candidates: prd/spec, plan, brief, incident-review) and whether shapeForOutcome's keyword read is strong enough to route to four-plus shapes, or whether shape selection should be a declared property of the outcome rather than inferred from its wording. Keyword routing across two shapes is already a guess; across five it is a coin toss, and picking the wrong shape is not a small error — the shape decides what the document argues.
acceptance_criteria: At least one artifact shape beyond review/decision exists with its sections and expectations; shape selection for more than two shapes is either measured on real outcomes or made explicit rather than inferred; a run asked for that artifact produces it rather than a review of it.
close_reason:
Fixed (b405c3c5). A third shape, SPEC, added to src/kernel/run/shapes.ts alongside review and decision — the-problem, the-goal, requirements, non-goals, open-questions, risks. Composition itself needed no changes: it already reads shape.sections generically and every downstream surface (CLI usage, --shape validation, unfilled-section reporting) already derives from COMPOSITION_SHAPES rather than naming shapes by hand, so adding the array entry was the whole wiring. Signal words for the chooser name the document type ('write a PRD', 'spec out', 'the requirements for') and are checked before decision signals so 'write a PRD deciding between two approaches' still returns spec, not decision — the document type asked for is what a reader notices missing. Proven end-to-end through the real compose CLI surface (tests/cli/compose.test.ts): a stand-in host answering with spec-shaped claims renders 'Shaped as a spec' with The problem / Requirements / Non goals headings and none of review's or decision's. Full gate green including smoke (1941 tests).

Not resolved, by design: the acceptance criteria's second clause ('shape selection... measured or made explicit') is satisfied by the existing --shape override, not by a better classifier. Keyword routing across three shapes is a better guess than across two, not a solved one — flagged in the original finding as a real risk (picking the wrong shape decides what the document argues) and left as a known, disclosed limitation rather than addressed with a heavier mechanism this bead did not require.

title: One unreachable role kills the whole composition, and the free path is where it happens
description:
Live evidence, run-20260813174506233 recomposed on nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free (2026-08-13): the composer call, the position, the position's screen and one role's claims check all completed, then privacy's support call returned no text and compose exited 1 with 'an unverified composition is not promoted'. Every completed call was discarded and no document was produced.

Refusing to PROMOTE an unverified composition is correct and must stay. Discarding the whole document because one role of five could not be reached is a different thing wearing the same sentence. The unverified part is that role's claims, not the other four roles' work, and the failure mode scales the wrong way: on a flaky free host the probability that at least one of N calls returns empty rises with N, so compose gets less usable exactly as a run gets bigger. Gerald's standing directive is that the everyday setup is a free hosted model, which is where empty replies live.

Two candidate fixes, needs a decision before implementing. (1) One retry of the support call before failing — cheap, preserves current fail-closed semantics exactly, matches the 'one corrective reprompt' precedent in src/hosts/jsonrepair.ts. (2) Fail-soft per role — drop the unreachable role's claims, disclose it in the uncleared-sources block that already exists, keep the rest. (2) is the bigger change and moves what 'not promoted' means, so it is Gerald's call.
acceptance_criteria: A composition where one role's check returns no text still produces a document from the roles that were checked, or retries before failing; either way the reader is told which role went unchecked and what became of its claims; the existing refusal case in tests/cli/compose.test.ts is updated deliberately rather than by accident.
notes: 2026-08-13 EDGE (recorded here because bd refuses task->epic edges): serves construct-ecz (untuned-model quality). The failure is only reachable on the free/hosted path this epic owns — a paid host returning empty is rare enough that nobody would have found it. Found by recomposing run-20260813174506233 on nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free.
close_reason: Fixed (a00518d5). One retry added to every model call compose makes (invokeRetrying in src/hosts/compose.ts, used by composer, position, position repair, claims screen, objection veto, closing round). Preserves fail-closed semantics exactly: a call that still fails on the second attempt refuses the composition as before (existing fixture unchanged and still green). New test proves the actual rescue — a support call returning empty exactly once now still produces the document. This is option (1) from the bead, the one that did not need Gerald's decision; option (2) (fail-soft per role) was not built and is not needed now that the common case (one transient empty reply) no longer loses the whole document.

title: A role's objection to the call is reported, and could repair it instead
description: First live run of the position pass (run-20260813174506233, recomposed): the call was sound and three roles independently objected to the same clause. strategy-alignment's objection was precise and correct - the call stated as settled what its deliverable framed as a judgment call it was asking the owner to decide, and imported a term ('public MCP', 'public/automated catalog surface') the deliverable never used. The veto worked and the objection prints beside the call. But a deliverable that fails its checks now goes back to its author once, and the position does not: an objection this specific is repairable in one call, and reporting it leaves the reader holding a call plus a correction to apply themselves. Two smaller things from the same run: three roles quoting the same sentence print as three lines, and the same one-round stop rule must apply so the position cannot repair forever.
acceptance_criteria: A position whose roles raise an objection goes back once, with the objections and the same no-new-facts constraint, and is re-screened; the improvement rule is the repair round's - a second attempt is taken only if it drops objections without introducing new refused claims; identical quotes from several roles collapse to one line naming all of them; one round only; a position that cannot be repaired prints with its objections exactly as it does today.
notes: 2026-08-13 Landed 886f6829. Verified through the real compose surface (tests/cli/compose.test.ts): a call a role says misreads it goes back once and the repair is what the reader gets; a second attempt that answers the objection by resting on a role that never ran is refused and the first call stands with its objections; the position role is invoked exactly twice however many objections survive. Collapse and the improvement rule are unit-held in tests/kernel/run/position.test.ts. NOT observed on a live model — no API key in this session; filed as construct-bpzk.
close_reason: Landed 886f6829. The call now goes back once with the collapsed objections and the same no-new-facts constraint, is re-screened, and only the roles that objected are asked again. The second attempt is taken only if its objections are a strict subset of the ones it was sent back for and it brought back no refusal the first did not have — the repair round's rule, extended with the failure mode unique to this pass (a rewrite that answers an objection by resting on a role that never ran). One round; a call that cannot be repaired prints with its objections as before, and a repaired call tells the reader it is a second attempt. Identical quotes from several roles print once naming all of them. Full gate green (lint, typecheck, 1922 tests, smoke). Live-model behaviour of the repair is unobserved and tracked as construct-bpzk.

title: Ground exhaustion cannot tell a document nobody opened from one nobody cited
description: namedButUnread flags any path in the deliverable with no [cite:path] marker and no stated read failure, and reports it as 'work it could have done'. Four of five roles on run-20260813160805209 used zero cite markers, so every path they named was flagged - 61 documents across five deliverables. evidence-provenance wrote in the same draft: 'where a question in this memo could be settled by a named document under the declared root, I opened it rather than marking it unknown', and still failed with 14 named-but-uncited. The verdict text asserts work was not done when what was actually missing was the marker. Two different failures, one sentence, and the more serious one is now hidden inside a citation-discipline complaint. The gate should separate them, or its detail must stop asserting the stronger claim.
acceptance_criteria: A path discussed in cited-adjacent prose is distinguished from one merely listed; the verdict detail for a citation-discipline miss no longer asserts the document went unread; the evidence-provenance draft from the recorded run is the regression case - it must not be told it left work undone when its own text says it opened the documents.
close_reason: Closed

title: What the record keeps and what a published artifact says are not the same words
description: Record vocabulary is leaking verbatim into published documents. A composed strategy memo currently carries [unverified], [unowned], [assumed], [cite:docs/x.md], slug section headings (what-would-change-it), and bracketed role ids. Those markers are load-bearing for the structural gates and must stay in the store; they are the wrong register for a reader, and they make an artifact read as machine output rather than as work. 'This needs checking against a source we did not have' says the same thing as [unverified] without the robot voice. Add a rendering boundary between the record and the artifact: the store keeps markers, the published surface renders them into plain sentences. Not a cosmetic pass - the gates must keep reading the marked text, so the rendering happens at publish and never on the way in.
acceptance_criteria: A rendering layer sits between composed claims and published output; [unverified], [unowned], [assumed] and citation markers render as plain-language clauses; slug section names render as sentence-case headings; the stored deliverable and the text the challenges read are unchanged, proven by a test that the same claim passes the same gate before and after rendering; the house register is stated once in the module rather than spread across call sites; a use case that genuinely needs the markers can ask for the record form.
close_reason: Closed

title: An ask to decide is answered with a proposal, not with the absence of a document
description: The outcome named 'the next two releases' and asked what stops being funded. All five roles reported that no document defines release boundaries and no budget artifact exists, and stopped. The material held the mobile bead list and an entity target exceeded 2.4x - enough to propose a split and a cut. Construct did make the call (mobile earns the next block) and then disowned it in the gap list. A contributor proposes and labels the proposal; naming the absence of a pre-written answer is refusing the ask in the shape it was asked. Related: 5 [unowned] markers in one document while the requester who dispatched the run is the obvious default decision owner.
acceptance_criteria: A role whose outcome asks it to decide, choose, sequence, or cut produces a proposal marked as its own judgment rather than reporting that no document states the answer; the absence of the source document is recorded as the reason the proposal is a proposal; the default decision owner is the requester unless the material names another, so [unowned] is never the whole answer on a decision the run was asked to make.
close_reason: Closed

title: A role reads its scope declaration as permission not to open a file it found
description: evidence-provenance grepped for repo-qv9h, FOUND docs/decisions-carryover.md line 136, and declined to open it because that document was 'outside what this role reviewed'. It cited its own scope declaration as grounds for not doing work it had already located. ROLE_OWNERSHIP_BOUND (grounding.ts) says a FINDING another role owns is not yours to REPORT; it is being read as 'a document another role read is not yours to open'. The two are different and the second is false - the licence is the root, not the read-set. GROUND_EXHAUSTION_RULE already says the right thing and loses to the ownership bound in practice. Fix the wording so the ownership bound is explicitly about what you report, never about what you may read.
acceptance_criteria: ROLE_OWNERSHIP_BOUND states in its own text that it bounds reporting and not reading, and that any document under a declared root is open to any role; GROUND_EXHAUSTION_RULE names the found-it-then-stopped case explicitly; the fixture-scored runs are re-rendered from the same export so the measured prompt is the shipped one.
notes: 2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): landed in 69427db4, whose body trailer names it alongside construct-aotn. The reconcile reads the commit subject only (hosts/repo/evidence.ts uses %s), and one subject line cannot carry four ids readably. The subject-line convention and multi-bead commits are the disagreement; tracked separately.
close_reason: Closed

title: A question naming something checkable inside licensed ground is work, not a question
description: ground-exhausted is path-shaped: it fires on a path named but not cited. The cop-out is question-shaped and passes free. On run-20260813160805209, 4 of 5 what-happens-first items and 4 of 6 what-would-change-it items were greps inside a repo the run was licensed to read - 'confirm which store each kill-switch reads from', 'confirm whether commitCanonicalWrite calls assertNoCrossSourceProfileAggregation', 'determine whether bb_canonical.claims empty is a scheduled migration'. Each names a symbol, table, or identifier rather than a path, so every gate passed. Extend the principle already written in ground-exhausted ('a path this role could name inside a root it was licensed to read is work it could have done') to handback language that names a checkable identifier.
acceptance_criteria: A structural check reads the handback and open-question language of a deliverable and fails when a question names a symbol, table, file, or identifier resolvable inside a declared root with no stated attempt to resolve it; passes when no roots are declared; conservative enough that a question about intent, funding, or a person's decision is never flagged; tested against the recorded BlackStory deliverables, which must fail it.
notes: 2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): landed in 69427db4, whose body trailer names it alongside construct-aotn. The reconcile reads the commit subject only (hosts/repo/evidence.ts uses %s), and one subject line cannot carry four ids readably. The subject-line convention and multi-bead commits are the disagreement; tracked separately.
close_reason: Closed

title: A closing answer is screened on what it owes, not on a deliverable's headings
description: 4 of 6 closing answers on run-20260813160805209 were discarded for lacking a labelled pre-mortem, scope-diff, or strongest-objection. Those sections are meaningful on a full deliverable and absurd on a one-paragraph answer to 'who owns repo-qv9h?'. screenClosedAnswers applies the author's entire brief challenge set. Result: the run held answers, failed them on form, and printed 'the gap stands' - reporting a gap it had closed. Screen a closing answer on the checks that mean something for a supplementary answer (claims-cited, ground-exhausted: is it sourced, did it name a document it never opened) and not on the deliverable-shape sections.
acceptance_criteria: screenClosedAnswers applies only the challenges meaningful to a supplementary answer; the excluded set is named with its reason in the module comment; a closing answer that asserts an uncited fact or names an unread document is still refused; test covers an answer that would previously have been discarded for a missing pre-mortem and now survives.
notes: 2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): landed in 69427db4, whose body trailer names it alongside construct-aotn. The reconcile reads the commit subject only (hosts/repo/evidence.ts uses %s), and one subject line cannot carry four ids readably. The subject-line convention and multi-bead commits are the disagreement; tracked separately.
close_reason: Closed

title: --ceiling bounds lifetime spend across every run, not the run you are starting, and says otherwise
description: src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts calls totalSpend(store) at lines 698, 1159 and 1211 without the run argument the function accepts (src/kernel/store/tasks.ts:313 takes an optional run and scopes the SUM to it). So the ceiling is applied to the SUM of spend across every task in the store, for all time. Three consequences, all observed. (1) The end-of-run line 'spend 26.03 of 30.00 ceiling' reports lifetime spend while reading as this run's — the run it printed for cost 4.74, recorded exactly in its own role-reported work-log entries. (2) Once lifetime spend passes the ceiling, every future run halts at dispatch regardless of its own cost: run-20260813144804609 recorded dispatch-halted with spend 18.03 against ceiling 10 before doing its own work. (3) The default ceiling is 10, so any store with more than 10 of lifetime spend halts all runs by default until the user finds --ceiling and raises it past a number that keeps growing. The fix is not obviously 'pass the run': a lifetime ceiling is a real protection against runaway total spend and a per-run ceiling is a real protection against one bad run. Decide which --ceiling means, or carry both with distinct names, and make the printed line say which it is.
notes: 2026-08-13, second finding on the same surface: the number the ceiling binds on is not money on this host. The claude adapter spawns the Claude Code CLI with no key and lets it use its own OAuth; this machine authenticates as a Max subscription (billingType stripe_subscription, organizationType claude_max, hasExtraUsageEnabled false, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY set, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is plain api.anthropic.com). Claude Code still reports total_cost_usd, which src/hosts/claude/result.ts takes as spend with the comment 'a real number on this host; the ceiling binds'. Under subscription auth it is an API-equivalent estimate of what those tokens would have cost, and nothing is billed. So today the ceiling halts runs against a lifetime-accumulating estimate that corresponds to no charge at all, while the real limit on this host is the subscription rate limit, which nothing reads. This has to be settled together with the per-run-versus-lifetime question rather than after it: an amount, a scope, and whether the host is billing per token or not are one design, and a ceiling denominated in dollars is meaningless on a host that does not charge them. Note the project already has a rule for this class from the OpenCode work: a cost of zero with zero steps is unmeasured, never free. The same distinction is owed here, in the other direction: a positive cost under a subscription is unbilled, not spent.
close_reason: Closed

title: The named-owner gate checks that an owner is named, not that the decision owner is
description: Observed on the re-run of the BlackStory strategy outcome (run-20260813144804609, 2026-08-13). rubric-strategy-alignment-S3 was declared on the strategy-alignment brief and PASSED, on a deliverable whose own decision-owner section reads 'Not named in the material as a single role or person for what capability to fund next' and which raised an ASK to the user for exactly that. It passed on two narrow action-owner attributions — docs/data/firebase-wind-down.md names an owner for specific console steps — because namesAnOwner asks whether any owner attribution names somebody, and cannot ask which decision that owner owns. The rubric line says 'The decision owner is named, and the deliverable says whether it is asking that person to decide or informing them.' The check enforces the weaker 'an owner is named somewhere'. This is the documented limit of a structural pass behaving as documented (readers.ts says a checker cannot see which decision an owner owns), so it is not a surprise — but it means the gate does not catch the failure it was built for, which was a document recommending three things with nobody's name against any of them. Note what did work: the deliverable declared the gap in its own decision-owner slot and raised a single ASK, which is the ladder behaving correctly. The gate is what is weak, not the run.
acceptance_criteria: either the check is tightened so an owner attribution is read against what it owns (a decision-owner slot with a placeholder value fails even when action owners are named elsewhere), or S3 is reclassified as judgment-only with the reason written down and the reader-rubric parity lint updated to match; whichever is chosen, the re-run deliverable above is the regression case and must come out with the intended verdict
notes:
2026-08-13: found by checking whether the gate fired on a real run rather than assuming it did, after the same class of false pass was already caught once today (construct-kpkv.5, an explained placeholder reading as a name). Second instance of one pattern: an owner check is easy to satisfy accidentally. DISPATCH: Fable/Opus-class — the choice between tightening and reclassifying is a judgment about what a free check can honestly carry.

2026-08-13: tightened rather than reclassified. The choice: S3 stays structural because the playbook template already asks the owner question in a named slot (strategy-alignment 'decision-owner', operations 'ownership', measurement 'instrumentation'), so the deliverable's own structure supplies the binding the checker was said to lack — reading the slot is not a judgment the check is unequipped to make, it is the deliverable answering where it was asked.

Diagnosis was sharper than this bead first recorded. Pulling the deliverable back out of the work log (run-20260813144804609, work_log seq 538) and running the regex showed the two attributions that carried the pass were NOT the firebase-wind-down action owners. Both came from the free-prose 'owner is X' alternative, inside the deliverable's own rubric-strategy-alignment-S3 self-report: 'owner is not named for the roadmap-commitment question itself (see decision-owner above)' and 'owner is named only for specific Firebase console actions'. The check counted the sentence reporting that no owner was named as an owner being named. The '## decision-owner' section was invisible to it entirely — no colon form, so the regex never reached it.

Landed ee343fc4. Three parts: (1) slotSection in plan/ladder.ts beside unheadedSlots — one parser for the shape, one asks whether the slot is headed, the other what is in it; (2) namesAnOwnerIn(slot) reads that slot, falling back to the whole-document read when the slot is unheaded (the missing slot is already a ladder gap, so the check is strictly stricter, never differently scoped); (3) placeholder heads match on their opening, not whole, so 'Not named in the material as a single role or person for...' reads as the placeholder it is.

One regression I introduced and caught before commit: slot bodies are sentences, so the exact-anchored collective 'the team' stopped matching 'The team owns this call.' Collectives now match as an opening with a lookahead that keeps a narrowed collective ('the team lead') a name — the rubric names 'the team' outright, so erring toward fail is right on this line.

Regression case verified: S3 against the recorded deliverable now returns passed=false, 'every owner attribution is a placeholder (Not named in the material as a single role or person for "wh…)'. Full gate green — lint clean, typecheck clean, 1837 tests pass, smoke pass. Parity lint untouched (it governs concern/id/weight, which did not change).

Known residual limit, stated rather than hidden: within a headed slot, prose that is neither a name nor in the placeholder family still reads as a name. Presence-not-quality is the declared limit of every structural pass here; this narrows the hole, it does not close it.
close_reason: Landed ee343fc4. Owner gate now reads the slot the owner question was asked in (decision-owner / ownership / instrumentation) instead of the whole deliverable, and placeholders match on their opening. The recorded BlackStory re-run deliverable is the regression case and now fails S3 as intended. Full gate green.

title: Testing Construct against BlackStory through nanobot, on a build that carries the work
description: construct-grs7 established the projection survives a foreign host, on alpha.5, with three recorded outcomes and no dispatch. What it could not establish is whether the surface is usable for BlackStory's actual operator work, because the operator surfaces that work needs - reading a record, seeing what disagrees in the declared ground, composing a run, honouring an erasure - did not exist there (construct-1ju5) and the build was four releases stale. This bead is the re-run once those close: BlackStory as the subject, real research-triage decisions, on the current build with the projection grown. It is the test of whether Construct contributes to that project rather than reports on it, which is the same question the strategy-document work under construct-kpkv answers from the other end.
acceptance_criteria: a recorded session against BlackStory through nanobot exercising record, inbox, review and compose on the current build; what worked and what broke written up as an update to docs/host-trial-nanobot.md rather than a second document; no change to BlackStory production scheduling and no capability token in the instance
notes: 2026-08-13: acceptance amended by the construct-1ju5 decision, which landed after this bead was written. 'Exercising record, inbox, review and compose' through nanobot is no longer the right test: review and compose are now deliberately NOT projected, because both are the CLI asking a host model several times and paying for it, and a host model must not be able to spend the user's money by being helpful. Erasure is off the surface for the same class of reason (irreversible, on a host that can enable externally reachable channels). So the amended test is: through nanobot, exercise catalog (which now names the version answering), record_outcome, records, record and inbox against real BlackStory work; review and compose are exercised from the CLI against the same workspace, and that split is itself the finding to write up.
close_reason: Landed: second pass verified on alpha.10 through nanobot with a local model. Catalog names version + 17 domains, read back by the host model; records/record probed; a real BlackStory outcome recorded producing briefs that carry ground-exhausted and the reader-rubric gates. Acceptance amended on the record for the review/compose projection decision. Finding filed as construct-clrw. Write-up appended to docs/host-trial-nanobot.md. No capability token in the instance.

title: The BlackStory operator surface runs a binary ten versions behind the tree
description: The nanobot instance at ~/.nanobot-blackstory/ attaches 'construct serve' from PATH, which is /opt/homebrew/bin/construct at 3.0.0-alpha.5 while the tree is at 3.0.0-alpha.9. Everything the last four releases added - records, review, compose, decide --apply, the third role grant, two catalog domains - is unreachable from the surface whose entire purpose is reachability, and nothing on either side said so. The trial write-up (docs/host-trial-nanobot.md) names this as its first finding: a claim about coverage made from inside a host is a claim about the installed version. Upgrading is necessary but not sufficient - the same drift recurs on the next release unless the surface states which build answered. Sequenced after construct-o5dk because upgrading across a ten-bump schema gap is exactly the case the version guard exists for and cannot currently fire.
acceptance_criteria: the instance runs the current build, verified by reading the catalog through the host and getting the tree's domain count; the version that answered is legible from the surface without leaving it; the standing local-only capability-token condition from construct-grs7 still holds
close_reason: Landed: 3.0.0-alpha.10 cut and installed globally (/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules). Verified live through construct serve — catalog answers construct=3.0.0-alpha.10, 17 domains (was alpha.5/15). Live store schema_version advanced 4->14 on first open. No capability token in the nanobot instance; that standing condition holds.

title: Every composition comes back in the same four sections whatever was asked
description: COMPOSITION_SECTIONS in src/hosts/compose.ts is a fixed four: the-answer, what-each-concern-established, where-they-disagree, what-follows. That is a run report, and it is the right shape for a run report. Asked to decide what BlackStory commits to over two releases, it is the wrong shape for the ask: the document that came back has no statement of current position, no comparison of the capabilities it dismisses, no release-by-release sequence, no owner on anything, and its first answer is a control gap to close rather than a commitment to make. Fixing the shape must not reopen the door the no-adding rule closed - the composer still may only arrange what the roles established, so a strategy section it cannot fill from deliverables is a section it reports empty, exactly as 'where-they-disagree' was reported empty in run-20260813133151758. Shape follows from the outcome and is chosen kernel-side; a composer that picks its own headings is choosing what the document argues.

title: The composer names what nobody answered and nothing goes and answers it
description: src/kernel/run/compose.ts produces Composition.uncovered; src/cli/index.ts:3182 prints it under '## what nobody answered' and that is the end of it. Nothing classifies a gap, nothing dispatches at one, nothing re-composes. So a run that correctly identifies nine things it did not establish hands all nine back to the reader, including the ones it had everything it needed to close. The gap classes are distinct and want different handling: closable from the declared ground (dispatch a bounded second pass to the owning role, licensed at the named path), user-held (the ASK ladder already exists and is fail-open), and genuinely unsettleable (stays in the list, which is where the list earns its keep). Bounded on purpose: one closing round, then the remainder stands - a run that keeps chasing its own gaps never delivers, which is the same reasoning research.ts's one-pass-then-climb rule rests on.
acceptance_criteria: uncovered items are classified and the ground-closable ones dispatched in one bounded round to the role that owns the concern, with the closing deliverables composed into the same document and attributed; the unclosed remainder still prints, and a run where nothing is closable behaves exactly as it does today; spend ceiling and concurrency bound still bind the closing round

title: An open question whose answer is in the declared ground is work, not an open question

title: A run answers the ask it was given, and closes the gaps it can close
description: The BlackStory strategy run (run-20260813133151758, alpha.9) produced 44 attributed claims and a nine-item 'what nobody answered' list, and Gerald's read is that it is not a strategy document: it stops at survey depth, defers the question it was asked, and hands back the remaining work instead of doing it. Four causes were traced in this tree, and they compound. (1) A grounded role has no rung between its declared sources and external research, so an open question whose answer sits in a file under the declared root is written down as unanswered rather than settled - five of the nine items say in words that the code was not read. (2) The composer's 'uncovered' list is terminal: src/cli/index.ts prints it and nothing consumes it, so a gap the run identified is never dispatched at. (3) COMPOSITION_SECTIONS in src/hosts/compose.ts is fixed at four generic headings, so a strategy ask and a risk ask and a research ask all come back in the shape of a run report - no position, no options weighed, no sequence, no owners. (4) The survey defaults to prose emphasis, so a codebase declared as ground is read as if it were a document set. Together these mean Construct behaves as a reviewer that reports what it noticed rather than a contributor that finishes the job.
acceptance_criteria: the BlackStory strategy outcome re-run on this tree produces a document whose shape matches the ask, whose open items are ones no reading could have settled, and which sequences and owns what it recommends; each of the four causes closed with a test
notes:
2026-08-13: re-run landed as run-20260813144804609 on 3.0.0-alpha.10, composed to ~/Downloads/blackstory-strategy-2026-08-13-rerun.md. OPEN ITEMS are now ones no reading could settle: the closing round put all four back to all four roles (16 calls) and every one came back with a specific reason naming what document would settle it and why the material does not contain it — one role reported it tried to open decisions-carryover.md and AGENTS.md and was denied read permission, which is the ground-exhaustion rule's honest ending. Source standing is disclosed above the claims: 4 of 4 deliverables failed claims-cited and ground-exhausted. OWNS WHAT IT RECOMMENDS: not met, and now traceable — the material genuinely names no decision owner, the deliverable said so in its decision-owner slot and raised a single ASK for it, and the S3 gate passed anyway on narrow action-owner attributions (filed as construct-k5jf). title: Every note's producer prompt now carries every record and every document in the workspace

title: The applier can never work on cursor or codex, and nothing says so

A model under either cannot make the change, so apply will always report applied=false there. The refusal is honest but the capability is inert, and the surface offers --host=<opencode|claude|codex|cursor> as though all four could carry a change out. Meanwhile claude dispatches -p with no sandbox flag, so on that host apply is an unsandboxed write path reached from a queue command.
acceptance_criteria: a host adapter declares whether it can carry out an outward change, and decide --apply refuses a host that cannot before spending a model call rather than after; a host that can states what posture the apply dispatch runs under; the claude write path is either explicitly scoped or explicitly documented as unsandboxed with what that permits

title: notes over a directory has no spend ceiling: an unbounded model bill from one command

The cost surfaces after it is spent.
