title: An unmet concern is staffed by a profile with evidence, or honestly declined
description: Once unmet concerns are recorded, the question is what to do with them, and both easy answers are wrong. Dropping them is what we already do. Letting a model mint a role on demand rebuilds the predecessor's 53 role overlays, every one of them graded 'strong' by a static file rather than by a measurement, which is the failure that produced computeEvidenceTier in the first place. The middle path is headhunting: given a recorded unmet concern, produce a STAFFING PROFILE and put it in the decision inbox for acceptance. A profile names the proposed domain and its concern sentence, states why each nearest existing domain does not already cover it (by name, one line each), cites primary standards or states honestly that none was found and why, declares the deliverable slots the concern requires, and carries an evidence tier that is computed from what exists, never asserted. Three refusals are first-class and each is an honest no: the concern is already covered (name the domain), no standard or body of practice can be named and the concern is not merely procedural, or the concern requires a licensed profession, in which case the answer is that construct cannot staff it and a licensed reviewer is required. Unlike the acquisition ladder, this one fails CLOSED: the assumed default in the inbox is 'not staffed', because admitting a domain changes routing for every future run and a default that silently widens the catalog is the invention half of commitment 15. Per-role depth stays retired: a profile is a coverage unit - routing, attribution, obligation - and never a persona, and nothing here claims that a differentiated question set produces differentiated findings.
acceptance_criteria: a staffing profile schema with proposed domain, concern, near-neighbour rebuttals, standards or stated absence, slots, computed evidence tier; a gate that refuses on overlap, on unnameable practice, and on licensed-profession concerns with the reason stated; proposals reach the decision inbox with 'not staffed' as the default and never self-admit; an accepted profile becomes a catalog entry through the normal committed-data path, not a runtime mutation; tests cover each refusal and the accept path; full repo gate passes
close_reason: Landed 48bc94dd: kernel/staffing/profile.ts with evaluateProfile gate (malformed, already-covered, licensed-profession, no-practice-to-name), computed evidence tiers stopping at grounded, and proposeStaffing raising a two-position decision defaulting to NOT STAFFED. 11 tests. Full gate green. Follow-up filed for the CLI surface.

title: What is missing from the record is a finding, not silence
description: An aggregator lives or dies on what it fails to hold, and construct has no concern for it. The measurement domain asks whether a claim about behavior can be observed - product telemetry - which is a different question from whether the corpus is empty in the places that matter. Blackstory knows the difference and had to invent the whole apparatus itself: empty-quadrant-and-aggregators.md, geographic-gap-scanner.md, capture-completeness-ops-bar.md, dpla-bulk-gap-analysis.md, and a decade-coverage gate. None of that was prompted by a routed concern. Add domain coverage-gaps and lens coverage: what the corpus should contain, how absence is distinguished from non-existence, what the sampling frame is, whose record is systematically missing, and what coverage claim the surface makes to a reader. Boundary against evidence-provenance, stated in both entries: provenance asks whether what is said is traceable, coverage asks whether what is unsaid is a bias.
acceptance_criteria: domain coverage-gaps in DOMAINS; lens coverage in LENSES with questions, slots, escalation; LENS_STANDARDS entry with primary standards or an honest ungrounded reason; the boundary against evidence-provenance stated in both; GLOSSARY parity passes; tests; full repo gate passes
notes: 2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): landed in 268114a9 on main, whose trailer names construct-om1t. Verified: git merge-base --is-ancestor 268114a9 main. Benign.

Full gate green.

title: Where a claim comes from is a routable concern, not an assumption
description: Construct speaks a research protocol on every dispatch (kernel/run/research.ts: primary over aggregator, reachable citation or [unverified], one pass then climb). That is a method floor for every role. What it is not is a concern anybody owns: no catalog domain fires on provenance, no lens asks whether a claim's source is the kind of thing that can support it, and no deliverable slot demands the source class beside the claim. Measured against blackstory, the defects that actually shipped were of exactly this shape - designation dates read as historical eras, unresearched listings defaulting to 'still operates today', a laundered 'still operates' assertion - each one a claim whose provenance and kind were never stated beside it. Add domain evidence-provenance to kernel/implication/domains.ts, lens research to kernel/plan/lenses.ts equipping it, and its entry in kernel/plan/standards.ts citing primary standards (never a summary or an aggregator). The lens's slots must require, per claim: the source, the class of source (primary record, derived record, aggregator, inference), and what kind of thing the claim asserts when a date or status is involved.
acceptance_criteria: domain evidence-provenance in DOMAINS with concern and keywords; lens research in LENSES equipping it with questions, slots, escalation; LENS_STANDARDS entry citing primary standards or an honest ungrounded reason; GLOSSARY parity lint passes; dispatch speaks the lens; tests cover routing and the slot requirements; full repo gate passes
close_reason: Landed 268114a9: domains evidence-provenance and coverage-gaps, lenses research and coverage with ceilings and slots, LENS_STANDARDS entries citing primary standards opened before naming (PROV-DM, RiC-CM 1.0, ISO 15489-1, Total Survey Error, Datasheets for Datasets, Trouillot). Full gate green.

title: A concern the catalog cannot carry is named, not dropped
description: The namer proposes domains and admissible() in kernel/implication/naming.ts silently discards anything outside the catalog, without a reason and without a reason code. Measured against a real outside project (blackstory: place-connected Black history aggregator), the four or five concerns that decide whether that product is trustworthy - citation provenance, corpus coverage bias, source rights, community harm - have no catalog domain, so the namer's proposals for them were dropped and nobody could see that they had been. A silent discard is indistinguishable from a catalog that covered the outcome. Record the diff instead: admissible() returns what it kept AND what it refused with a reason code (not-in-catalog, no-reason-given, duplicate), NamedMap carries them as unmet concerns, and the outcome path writes one work-log entry per unmet concern. Routing behavior is unchanged: an unmet concern still does not dispatch. This bead only makes the gap visible; staffing it is separate work.
acceptance_criteria: admissible() returns kept plus refused-with-reason; NamedMap.unmet carries them; startRun writes a work-log entry naming each unmet concern and its stated why; construct log shows them; existing routing behavior unchanged and asserted by test; full repo gate passes
close_reason: Landed 65daf06a: admissible() returns refusals with reason codes, NamedMap.unmet carries them, outcome path logs one entry per unmet concern, CLI log renders the proposal verbatim. Routing unchanged and asserted. Full gate green.

The coordinator (src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts) never reads lessons; no dispatch assignment carries what the workspace already learned, so the 'learning staff' claim holds only for the note-drop door. title: Section 10 never pins the model tier on the claude host, so a run can be served by two tiers and still be quoted per-tier
description:
scripts/measure-decisions.mjs sets MODEL = undefined for --namer-host=claude when --namer-model is absent, so the adapter uses whatever the session default resolves to. The script's own preamble states 'Figures are per-model, never per-architecture — a different tier answering differently is the point of measuring per tier', and RESEARCH-DECISIONS 17 quotes its run as 'served by claude-sonnet-5 — the same tier 10 measured, so the difference below is the catalog and the prompt, not the model'. Nothing enforces that.

Observed 2026-08-10 on the armE-all-exclusions run: 'model(s) that ran: claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5'. A single 126-consultation run was served by two tiers, and its per-outcome record carries no per-consultation model attribution, so the mixed answers cannot be separated after the fact.

The run reports modelsRan, which is how this was caught, but reporting is not pinning: a mixed run still writes a record and still compares like a clean arm. Every 10 figure on the claude host is exposed to this, including the 0.301 the README quotes.
acceptance_criteria: The claude host path requires an explicit model or refuses to record; a run whose modelsRan set has more than one entry is refused the same way a run with failures is; the per-outcome record carries the model that served each consultation
notes: 2026-08-11: closing. All three clauses met and gated by tests/scripts/measure-decisions-attribution.test.ts, which drives the script end to end against a stub speaking ollama's wire shape (0.5s, no model calls, deterministic). (1) --namer-record on the claude host requires --namer-model and refuses BEFORE any consultation — asserted, including that the refusal precedes the consultations rather than following them. (2) A two-tier run is refused as an arm, the arm file left untouched. (3) Every perOutcome row carries servedBy naming the model that served that consultation, and the refused run's attribution is written to <record>.mixed.json so the run is separable by tier rather than lost. The local path now attributes what the response says answered rather than what was requested, and reads OLLAMA_HOST. A first attempt to verify with a live qwen3.5:4b section-10 run took 35 minutes and died on transport (5 of 126 failed) before reaching the record — the wrong instrument for a bookkeeping property. NOT retroactive: four of the five existing arm records in fixtures/namer-arms/ carry model: null and were verified single-tier by reported modelsRan, not by a pin; RESEARCH-DECISIONS 18 now says so and says they could not be recorded today.
close_reason: Pin required and refused before spend; mixed run refused and kept separable; per-consultation attribution on every perOutcome row — all three gated by an end-to-end test

title: Section 10 scored every repaired namer reply as a namer failure, so its figures are part keyword arm
description:
scripts/measure-decisions.mjs inlines admit() to match escalate.ts's admissible(), but escalate.ts UNWRAPS the namer's reply first: createHostNamer returns a bare DomainNaming[] normally and a NamerReply object ({namings, retried, firstFailure}) when jsonrepair.ts had to correct the first reply. The script iterated the reply directly, so every outcome that needed a repair threw 'namings is not iterable', was counted in the failure tally, and fell back per configuration — B to the keyword map.

Observed on the 2026-08-10 shipped-baseline re-run: 6 of 126 consultations. Those 6 outcomes were scored on the keyword arm while the run reported its numbers as the namer's, and the keyword arm's out-of-family miss is far worse (unspent A0 0.663 against B 0.289), so the contamination inflates measured namer miss.

This matters beyond one run because the contamination is not constant across arms: a longer or harder prompt provokes more malformed first replies, so the arm with the bigger catalog pays more keyword-fallback penalty. Any comparison of prompt variants on this instrument is confounded by it. The 0.301 and 0.624 figures in RESEARCH-DECISIONS 17 were both produced by the unfixed script (17 reports 0 failed for the held run, so that one may be uncontaminated; the shipped 0.301 run's failure count is not recorded).
acceptance_criteria: The script unwraps NamerReply exactly as escalate.ts does; repairs are reported separately from failures and carried in the arm record; the shipped baseline is re-run on the fixed instrument and its figures recorded
notes: 2026-08-10: fixed. The NamerReply unwrap now matches escalate.ts; repairs counted and reported separately from failures and carried in the arm record; the script refuses to write a record for any run with a failure. Shipped baseline re-run on the fixed instrument: 0 failures, 7 repairs, out-of-family miss 0.280 (was 0.301 on the contaminated instrument). Figures in RESEARCH-DECISIONS 18.
close_reason: Closed

title: A framed conflict reads the role's reply, not its deliverable, so citations vanish from the inbox
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an outcome implicating two or more concerns on a host with a write surface, so roles submit drafts through submit_draft.
2. Have the roles disagree.
3. construct inbox

## What happens

Observed on run-20260811001658945: the security role submitted a 9,243-character deliverable ending in a full stance block —

  STANCE: proceed
  BECAUSE: the exposures found are real but bounded ...
  CITE: src/kernel/cleanup/catalog.ts (lines 90-110), src/kernel/capabilities/tokens.ts, docs/first-run.md

— and replied with a 1,714-character summary whose restated block carried only 'STANCE: proceed — these are real but bounded exposures ...'. frameConflicts parsed the REPLY, so the inbox showed that role's position with no reason and no citation, while its deliverable of record carried both. Commitment 11 asks for both sides cited; this drops citations silently, on the path the product itself designed.

## Why it matters

This is the same defect deliverableTextOf was written to fix for the challenge checks — 'a verdict about something other than the thing being relied on'. The lesson was learned once and applied in one place. The stance parser kept reading task.result.

## Fixed

src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts frameConflicts now parses through deliverableTextOf, the same helper the challenges use. Test in tests/kernel/run/conflict-quality.test.ts reproduces the live shape (long draft with a full block, short reply with a restated stance word) and asserts the citation survives into the decision.
acceptance_criteria: A framed conflict carries the citation and reason from the deliverable of record even when the reply restates a bare stance word; regression test drives the shape observed on run-20260811001658945

title: The catalog-conditions namer regressed out-of-family miss 0.301 to 0.624: prune, reword, or revert
description: RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md 17 records the 2026-08-10 re-measurement of the 10 gate after the domain catalog gained implicatedWhen/notImplicatedWhen and the namer prompt began rendering them. The gate is met (B dominates the zero-model fallback on both axes out-of-family) but B's own out-of-family miss went 0.301 to 0.624 against its prior measurement on the same tier and the same corpora, with the keyword arm byte-identical across both runs. The mechanism is sound; this wording is not shippable on these figures. Three candidate causes to separate: (1) notImplicatedWhen exclusions are too broad -- prune to the ones with a measured confusion behind them; (2) the prompt's 'Naming nothing is a valid and useful answer. Do not reach.' line is what costs the recall now that exclusions are present; (3) the conditions crowd out the model's own reading. Each is one re-run of 'node scripts/measure-decisions.mjs --namer --section 10 --namer-host claude --namer-binary /opt/homebrew/bin/claude'. Over-rates are not comparable across the two runs (the script's over denominator changed), so miss is the only axis that decides this.
acceptance_criteria: A re-measurement recorded in RESEARCH-DECISIONS with out-of-family miss at or below the 0.301 the inversion was adopted on, or the change reverted with the reason recorded; Gerald's call recorded either way
notes:
2026-08-10: VERDICT — Gerald accepts the recommendation. The revert stands: the catalog conditions and the prompt that renders them stay out of the shipped path. Recorded under the standing stakeholder protocol — the session measured and recommended, Gerald accepted.

What is adopted with it: the reason. Not 'the exclusions were too broad' (refuted, ~0.04 of ~0.27) and not 'the do-not-reach line costs the recall' (refuted, byte-identical across the shipped and regressed arms), but that inclusion-condition text buys no precision at this tier and costs 0.225 of out-of-family miss. Figures and the 2x2 in RESEARCH-DECISIONS 18; arms in fixtures/namer-arms/.

Carried forward as a limit, not a footnote: arms D and E were not shown to be free. p=0.61 and 0.33 on 168 label-pairs cannot size a modest recall regression, and both moved the wrong way. A future attempt at a measured exclusion set needs a corpus that can see the difference before it needs another run.
close_reason: Revert stands; three candidate causes separated, two refuted; Gerald accepted the recommendation on the recorded figures

title: Ownership is guessed, not known: the coverage claim's weakest joint
description: Construct's remaining claim after the role-depth retirement is coverage, obligation and provenance — 'of course legal sees this'. Coverage rests on the implication catalog inferring which domains an outcome touches, and RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 4 records that 116 of 207 catalog keywords have never fired. So ownership is guessed from vocabulary. Tools in the adjacent lane (Spotify Xirp via a Backstage catalog) read ownership from a real registry instead; see RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 16. This bead is not 'adopt Backstage'. It is: decide and implement where Construct gets ownership facts, given it has no catalog of its own. Options to weigh in writing before building: an optional declared-ownership file a user maintains (cheap, honest, unverified), reading an existing catalog when one is present behind an adapter seam (accurate, adds a dependency), or accepting keyword inference and stating its measured miss rate wherever coverage is claimed (no new code, weakest claim). Whichever is chosen, the coverage claim must carry its own accuracy figure rather than asserting completeness.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision naming the chosen source of ownership facts and what it costs; the coverage claim on every surface carries a measured accuracy figure or an explicit unverified tag; if a seam is built, it is optional and degrades to today's behavior when absent
notes:
2026-08-10: closing. All three acceptance clauses met.

(1) Written decision naming the source of ownership facts and its cost: RESEARCH-DECISIONS 17. Relation A (component-to-team) is a registry fact and refused for coverage; relation B (outcome-to-concern) has no registry and cannot have one, because the promise is that a user is not ambushed by a domain they did not know existed. Inference accepted with its figure carried.

(2) The coverage claim carries a measured accuracy figure: the README now states miss 0.280 (26/93, [0.199, 0.378]) and over 0.374 (40/107, [0.288, 0.468]) from a recorded single-tier run whose per-outcome answers ship in fixtures/namer-arms/shipped.json, so a reader can re-derive both without paying for the run. That is the 'figure it has actually earned' this bead was held open on (construct-cuvk).

(3) No seam was built, so the optional-and-degrades clause is vacuous.

What this bead does NOT deliver, and construct-8p1 records why: the precision lessons still do not reach the router. Handing the router the catalog's conditions costs 0.225 of out-of-family miss and buys no precision, so 3's finding stands open as a defect with no proposed fix. That is a separate problem from where ownership facts come from, which is what this bead asked.
close_reason: All three clauses met; the shipped router now carries a reproducible measured figure on the front door

title: Role-plant scoring has no discrimination check: a lens gets credit for findings any lens produces
description: roleCoverage in score-org-harness.mjs credits a role plant whenever ANY claim in the run matches its document pair and keyword sets. Nothing requires that the run was dispatched as the owning lens, and nothing requires that other lenses FAIL to produce it. A plant that every lens earns measures corpus coverage, not lens depth, and 'at depth' in the README is defined as lens depth. Evidence: in clean-context Claude runs, the security plant TH2 was earned by the security, operations AND design lens runs, and SA2 was earned by all three; each by a different claim. High-claim-count runs sweep the corpus and collect other roles' plants incidentally. The fix is a discrimination check over a full matrix of per-lens runs: a role plant is lens-discriminating only if the owning lens earns it and non-owning lenses do not. A plant that fails discrimination is retired, not re-keyed, because adding keywords only moves the coincidence.

title: A keyword carrying punctuation or an internal stopword could never fire, and two shipped ones never did
description: Found 2026-08-10 while adding the wave B concerns. Two independent defects in src/kernel/routing/dispatcher.ts made catalog keywords silently unmatchable. (1) The text went through tokenize() which splits on every non-alphanumeric character, while a keyword was split on whitespace only, so any keyword containing a hyphen, slash, or apostrophe stayed one part that could equal no token — dead forever. (2) Adjacency was judged against the raw token run, so a keyword with an internal stopword ('hard of hearing' reduces to hard+hearing) could never be consecutive in the sentence it was written for, scored 7 instead of 10, and sat under the signal floor. The shipped catalog had two live casualties: accessibility 'hard of hearing' and marketing-claims 'send to everyone'. Both fixed: keywords tokenize the same way text does, and adjacency is judged against the stopword-filtered run as well as the raw one. A standing test now fires every catalog keyword in a sentence containing it verbatim and fails on any that cannot fire.
acceptance_criteria: Both defects fixed at the source rather than by rewording keywords; a standing test proves every catalog keyword can fire; the deliberate v2 golden divergence is recorded with its reasoning; full gate green
close_reason: Fixed at the source in 059090c2 with standing tests; full gate green. ekv: keywords now tokenize the same way text does, adjacency is judged against the stopword-filtered run too, and a standing test fires every catalog keyword in a sentence containing it verbatim — it found the two live casualties (accessibility 'hard of hearing', marketing-claims 'send to everyone'), both now firing. The v2 golden case that locked the old adjacency behavior was updated deliberately with the reasoning recorded in the test header. 83y: lensDirective renders the ceiling and the coordinator test asserts it for the security lens.

title: Structural keyword scoring credits a wrong-mechanism claim: R2 passed on the wrong bug
description:
The fixture-organization scorer counts a plant found when one claim cites both planted documents and matches an AND-set of keyword terms. That is deliberately structural, and it has a false-positive mode: a claim can cite the right pair and satisfy every term while describing a different mechanism than the one planted.

Observed on the 2026-08-10 qwen3.6:35b composed run. R2's plant is: every hydration cycle lands a new commit on the deployed-from branch, progressive sync restarts its wave on source change, so on hydrated repos rollout waves restart every cycle and large rollouts may never complete. Terms: hydrat + commit|push + wave|restart|progressive.

The claim that scored it: 'The rfc-002 decision to treat hydration as a first-class feature that pushes to the sync branch explains T-27949: the ApplicationSet controller specChanged status promotion logic advances to Healthy based on the pre-update child state before the generated spec change is applied, breaking the progressive sync trigger.' That is T-27949's other bug, the specChanged/Healthy promotion gap. It satisfies hydrat, push, and progressive incidentally, cites both documents, and never states the wave-restart mechanism. Rung 2 flipped FAIL to PASS on it.

This is the same class as X1's recorded miss, seen from the other side. X1 is a wrong-mechanism claim the scorer correctly failed because its vocabulary did not overlap; R2 is a wrong-mechanism claim the scorer wrongly passed because its vocabulary did. So the instrument's verdict on mechanism correctness currently depends on vocabulary coincidence, in both directions.

Not fixable by adding terms, which would only move the coincidence. What distinguishes them is whether the claim states the planted causal chain, and the honest options are a per-plant negative term set (terms whose presence indicates the wrong mechanism), a required-phrase set naming the chain rather than its parts, or accepting that mechanism correctness is a judged property and recording a named judge's verdict beside the structural score.
acceptance_criteria: A run stating a plant's documents-and-vocabulary but not its mechanism does not score that plant; the 2026-08-10 qwen R2 claim is the regression case; the fix does not widen the key for content misses, and any judged component records the judging model per the house rule
notes:
2026-08-10 PARTIAL. Landed: every plant result now records the claim that earned it (scorePlant in scripts/score-org-harness.mjs), so a false credit is readable on the face of a score file instead of needing to be re-derived from the run by hand, which is how this one was found. Three tests, including the R2 regression case held as a documented limit rather than a fixed one. Today's score file regenerated: verdicts identical, evidence added. Full gate green (1684 tests).

NOT fixed, and the diagnosis says why a structural fix does not exist. R2's document pair (rfc-002 + T-27949) supports two mechanisms: the planted wave-restart-per-hydration-cycle loop and the ticket's separate specChanged/Healthy promotion gap. Both are written in the same vocabulary because they are about the same feature, so a claim about the second satisfies the first's terms. Measured the obvious structural escape and it does not exist: across all 22 corpus documents no plant has every term met by a >=50%-frequency alternative, so term distinctiveness thresholds cannot separate these. Adding or narrowing terms only relocates the coincidence, and narrowing them now would be editing a key to fit an observed run, which is the mirror of the widening the house rule already forbids.

What remains is a choice Gerald owns, because one option touches a STRATEGY claim:
(a) per-plant discriminator recorded in the key (a required relation phrase, or terms whose presence marks the neighbouring mechanism). Structural and gating, but authored after seeing a run.
(b) a named-judge verdict on mechanism correctness beside the structural score, using each plant's pre-recorded gist, which was committed before any run and is currently unused by the scorer. Follows the LLM-as-judge house rule and the dated distractorGate precedent for adding a check without rewriting recorded scores. Cost: STRATEGY Phase 5 leans on 'scoring is structural (keyword sets and document pairs, not judgment)' as part of what keeps measured claims honest without external subjects, so this needs that sentence amended rather than quietly contradicted.
(c) accept the limit, gate nothing on the affected plants, and state in any quoted figure that mechanism correctness is unverified for plants whose pair carries more than one mechanism.
close_reason: Decided by model under the LLM-as-judge protocol after the human label was lifted: option (b), a judged mechanism verdict recorded beside the structural score. (a) is refuted by the same evidence that refuted keyword narrowing for the discrimination work — terms proxy for a mechanism, so authoring a discriminator after seeing a run fits the standard to results and only relocates the coincidence. (c) leaves the instrument unable to gate. (b) judges against each plant's gist, which the key committed before any run and the scorer has never read, so the standard was fixed in advance. Shipped: scripts/judge-org-harness-mechanism.mjs (--emit/--apply), three tests, STRATEGY's 'scoring is structural' sentence narrowed with a dated amendment rather than quietly outlived. Regression case confirmed: a clean-context judge pass over the 2026-08-10 composed run refused R2 for exactly the recorded reason, and also refused X2 and R1 as false credits (X2's claim inverts the planted direction). 3 of 4 structurally credited plants in that run were false credits. Correlated-error caveat recorded in every judged file.

title: Nothing records what a run read, so the grounded dispatch path is wired to an always-empty source
description:
The coordinator now fills a dispatch's material from sourceReadsFor(store, run) (materialFor in src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts), and a role that has material is given the grounded synthesis protocol instead of the no-material rule. That consumer is live on the dispatch path.

The producer is not. recordSourceRead in src/kernel/store/sources.ts has no caller anywhere in src/ — its only callers are in tests/kernel/store/sources.test.ts. So every real run reports zero reads, materialFor returns [], and the grounded protocol reaches nobody today.

The surrounding surfaces already exist and make the gap sharper rather than theoretical: sources are declared per workspace (construct source), sourcesFor reads them back, the plan text already says a run is 'grounded in N declared sources', and construct notes --file already pulls a document through the extraction ladder. What is missing is the step that records, per run, which declared sources were actually read and how completely — including the unreachable ones, which the store models as first-class precisely so a failed read cannot pass as coverage.

Until this lands, two things are true and should be said plainly wherever the protocol is cited: the grounded protocol is shipped and tested but dormant, and any claim that the fixture-organization rungs measure what a real run receives holds only for the prompt text, not for the material block.
acceptance_criteria: A production path records a SourceRead per declared source a run consults, with honest coverage and detail, including unreachable ones; a run over declared sources produces a non-empty materialFor and the role's assignment carries the named documents; test covers the end-to-end path rather than materialFor alone
notes: 2026-08-10 (Fable session, accepted direction from Gerald in chat): the who-reads question is settled by stakeholder clarification — Construct must be pointable at one or more codebases/directories/repos, must not hamper the host, and fails open. Decision: the kernel surveys and RECORDS (hosts/sources.ts walks local ground; kernel/run/sourcereads.ts owns coverage judgment, once per run); the role READS content through the host's own tools; remote kinds record unreachable rather than vanish. Producer wired into construct work before dispatch; e2e test drives source add -> outcome -> work and asserts the assignment carries named documents and the unreachable source. Implemented on feat/source-reads.
close_reason: Producer live: construct work surveys declared sources, records SourceReads with honest coverage (complete/partial/unreachable), materialFor non-empty, grounded protocol reaches real dispatches. Full gate green.

title: The org-harness measures a prompt the product does not send: the grounded-synthesis protocol is harness-only
description:
scripts/org-harness-producer-prompt.mjs states in its docblock: 'The role depth comes from the committed lenses (src/kernel/plan/lenses.ts), so what a run was told is exactly what the product's dispatches are told — the harness measures the shipped depth, not a bespoke eval prompt.'

That is true of the lens block (posture, questions, slots — genuinely read from lenses.ts) and false of everything that does the work on rungs 1 and 2. Rendered assignmentFor() for a role and probed for the harness's own strings, every one is absent from the product: 'The valuable findings combine two documents that never cite each other', 'which OTHER document changes what this one means', 'removing either cited document would collapse the finding', 'Name mechanisms in the corpus's own vocabulary', 'Use the sources; do not merely list them', 'Depth over breadth', the cross-reference/conflict/risk taxonomy, and 'When a finding rests on two documents, cite both'. The product assignment is 3,962 chars and contains none of them.

The product in fact instructs the opposite about citation. MATERIAL_PROTOCOL in src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts says 'Never cite a file path as the source for a claim about your domain', because a real run once cited this tool's own module as authority. The harness scores a run entirely on corpus-relative file-path citations. Both rules are right for their own context; they are not the same prompt, and there is no document-grounded dispatch path in src/ that carries the harness's.

Consequence, and why this is P1 rather than a docblock nit: the harness is named as the pack-depth close gate on construct-99x's decomposition and as the eval gate on construct-fdl. Rung-1 and rung-2 scores therefore measure a prompt that ships nowhere, so tuning that prompt to pass the gate would raise the score without changing any shipped behavior — the exact shape commitment 15 exists to forbid.
acceptance_criteria: Either the grounded-synthesis protocol ships in the product as a document-grounded dispatch path and the harness renders it from that source, or the harness docblock and every bead citing it as the shipped-depth instrument are narrowed to the lens block, which is what it actually shares. Not both claims standing at once.
notes:
2026-08-10 FIRST HALF LANDED (c23fea85): src/kernel/run/grounding.ts holds GROUNDED_SYNTHESIS_PROTOCOL and groundedMaterialProtocol(); assignmentFor takes options.material and swaps the grounded protocol in for MATERIAL_PROTOCOL when a dispatch has documents, never both, since the two rules contradict each other; the coordinator fills material from the store via materialFor(store, task.run); scripts/org-harness-producer-prompt.mjs imports GROUNDED_SYNTHESIS_PROTOCOL instead of keeping its own copy, and its docblock now states what it shares (lens depth + synthesis discipline, both from src) and what stays local (the JSON envelope and citation format, which are the eval's output contract, not depth). tests/kernel/run/grounding.test.ts holds eight properties, including a drift test that renders the prompt through the script and asserts the kernel export appears verbatim. Full gate green: lint, typecheck, 1681 tests, smoke.

Not closed, because the acceptance says the protocol ships in the product and it is dormant: nothing calls recordSourceRead, so materialFor returns [] on every real run. Blocked on construct-818, which lands the producer. The instrument-validity half of this bead is fixed; the ships-in-the-product half waits on that.
close_reason: Second half landed with construct-818 on feat/source-reads: construct work now surveys declared sources and records SourceReads before dispatch, so materialFor is non-empty on real runs and the grounded-synthesis protocol ships in the product's own dispatch path (e2e test in tests/cli/spine.test.ts drives source add -> outcome -> work and asserts the assignment carries the grounded protocol with named documents). The harness renders from the same export (first half, c23fea85). Both acceptance branches now agree: the protocol ships and the instrument measures it.

title: A citation naming an internal artifact passes the citation check while inventing its provenance: roles cite [domain catalog] for facts it does not contain
description:
Found during the stakeholder-acceptance runs (construct-9xq) on a real run through the shipped CLI: run-20260806032817359, host opencode, model ollama/qwen3.5:4b, employment role.

The employment deliverable supports substantive legal assertions with the citation [domain catalog]:
- 'Poland's labor code (Kodeks Pracy) governs contractor classification and employment terms [domain catalog]'
- 'Cross-border employment triggers Polish tax and social security obligations [domain catalog]'
- 'GDPR non-compliance creates fines up to 20 million EUR or 4% of global turnover [domain catalog]'

The domain catalog (src/kernel/implication/domains.ts) contains none of it. The employment entry is a domain name, a one-line concern, a keyword list, and licensedReview: 'attorney'. Grep for kodeks, labor code, 20 million, 4% of global, or social security across domains.ts and lenses.ts returns zero. The contracts role did the same thing in its stance line: 'CITE: domain catalog - contracts role requires source material'.

Why this is the same defect as construct-wt6 in a new shape, and worse. That bug was a role citing an installed module path as authority; the fix failed a [cite:...] whose body is a SOURCE PATH. 'domain catalog' is not a path, so it passes. The role has satisfied the citation requirement by naming an internal artifact that demonstrably does not contain the cited content — fabricated provenance that clears the check designed to catch fabricated provenance. The facts here happen to be roughly right (the GDPR ceiling really is 20M EUR or 4%), which makes it worse rather than better: the deliverable reads sourced, the provenance is invented, and nothing flags it. A reader who trusts the citation has been misled by exactly the unit of trust the project stakes itself on.

Fix direction, to be decided rather than assumed: the check cannot verify content it has no access to, so the honest move is probably to refuse a citation whose body names a Construct-internal artifact at all (the catalog, the lenses, the brief, the playbook, the work log) and require [unverified] instead, since a role's own scaffolding is never evidence about the world. That is a small allowlist-shaped rule on top of the existing source-path rule in src/kernel/verify/claims.ts. Verify the vocabulary against real model output before fixing the matcher: this is a model-facing heuristic and the wording models actually use is the requirement (a hermetic fixture will not tell you).

Do NOT fix this by removing the citation requirement from role assignments, and do not widen [unverified] into a blanket escape: the employment deliverable is otherwise good work and the requirement is what produced it.
acceptance_criteria: A citation whose body names a Construct-internal artifact fails the citation challenge and the deliverable is held rather than promoted; the rule is validated against real model output from at least one live host, not only hermetic fixtures; the existing source-path rule and the [unverified] path are unchanged in behavior; a test pins at least the 'domain catalog' wording observed in run-20260806032817359; full repo gate green
notes:
2026-08-05 DISPATCH: minimum tier Sonnet-class or better — deciding what counts as an internal artifact and validating against live output is judgment work. Self-contained: the matcher is src/kernel/verify/claims.ts; the observed output is quoted above; reproduce with the CLI per docs/first-run.md against any local host. Close gate: full repo gate plus a recorded live-host run showing the citation refused.

2026-08-05 PROVENANCE: this is the third instance of the citation-provenance class (construct-wt6 module path, construct-ikg unreadable deliverable, this one). Worth stating in the fix's commit message that the class recurs and why the previous fix did not cover it.
close_reason: Fixed: findScaffoldingCitations refuses bracketed and CITE:-stance citations naming domain catalog / role lens / playbook / work log / keyword map / implication map; wired into the claims-cited challenge ahead of the untagged check. Validated against the real stored deliverables: flags employment (7), contracts (1), privacy (3); passes compliance and security which cited honestly. Source-path rule and [unverified] path unchanged. Full gate green, landed on main. Judged/validated by: Fable 5 session under standing approval.

close_reason: Note cap (25/task, counted across role-authored action names) with stop message and logged-once marker; drafts still land after the note wall. Proven live: run-20260805192830381 completed all three roles in normal time with no loop. Full gate green (1547 tests + smoke).

title: The deliverable a user paid for has no surface that shows it
description: Found assembling the journey-simulation review (2026-08-05): after construct work reports a task done, no CLI surface prints the deliverable body. work prints the role, cost, and its concerns (deliverableConcerns); construct log prints action names; nothing writes the deliverable to a file or shows it on demand. The draft sits in the store as work_log detail under draft-submitted, readable only with sqlite by hand. The deliverable is the product — a run that ends with 'done, $0.0006' and no way to read what was produced is a spine with its last step missing. What: a surface (construct show <task-or-run>, or work printing a path, or log --full) that renders the latest draft per task with its promotion state and licensed-review qualifier. Also worth folding in: scripts/journey-sim.sh should archive what this surface shows per run.
acceptance_criteria: A user who has run construct work can read the full deliverable text for each task through a documented CLI surface, including its promotion state and licensed-review qualifier; docs/first-run.md shows the step; journey-sim.sh captures it; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better once the surface shape is decided; the shape decision (new command vs log flag) is the judgment part — Fable/Opus-class or Gerald. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: construct show --run renders each task's latest draft (or the role reply where no draft exists) with promotion state and licensed-review qualifier; docs/first-run.md documents it; journey-sim.sh captures it. Landed with full gate green.

title: A role that never stops submitting drafts runs until the host timeout kills it
description: Found by journey simulation (run-20260805183824874, opencode + openrouter qwen3-30b): the employment role looped submit_draft/finalized_draft 20+ times over ten minutes until the adapter's 600000ms timeout marked the task failed — after an identical earlier run finished cleanly in 14s with 2 drafts. The write surface accepts unlimited resubmission and its success reply carries no stop signal, so a small model in a loop reads {ok:true} as 'continue'. Supersession stays legal (the clean run superseded once); what changes: (1) every accepted resubmission's reply says the draft is on the record and to stop if final, (2) a hard cap (5 drafts per task) after which submits are refused with a stop message, recorded once as draft-cap-reached rather than flooding the append-only log.
acceptance_criteria: Second and later accepted drafts carry an explicit stop note in the tool reply; the sixth submit for a task is refused with a stop message; the cap event lands on the log exactly once however many times the role keeps trying; the clean two-draft path is unchanged; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: found and fixed in-session by Fable 5. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Resubmission replies carry an explicit stop instruction; sixth submit refused with denial draft-cap; cap event logged exactly once regardless of retries; clean two-draft path unchanged. Full gate green (1544 tests + smoke). Live evidence: run-20260805183824874 (20+ draft loop to host timeout) vs run-20260805171251873 (clean).

title: A run forgets the host and model it was filed with, and work silently dispatches to whatever the host last used
description: Found by journey simulation wire capture (2026-08-05): construct outcome --host=opencode --model=openrouter/qwen/... records nothing about that choice, so construct work --run <id> without re-stated flags dispatched roles to the host's last-used TUI model — google/gemini-3-pro-image-preview, an image model — producing a misleading provider routing error. The user named a model at the moment of intent; the run must remember it. Fix: record the dispatch surface (host, model, binary, dir) with the run at outcome time; work uses the recorded values when flags are absent; an explicit flag at work time still wins and the divergence is logged.
acceptance_criteria: outcome with a named host records host/model/binary/dir on the run; work without flags dispatches with the recorded values; explicit work flags override and the override is on the work log; a run filed with no host keeps current behavior; full repo gate green + recorded rerun of the hosted journey.
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: found in-session by wire capture; fixed by Fable 5. Close gate: full repo gate + recorded rerun.
close_reason: run_dispatch table (schema v7, write-once) records host/model/binary/dir at outcome; work uses the record when flags are absent, explicit flags win and divergence is logged. Proven by recorded rerun run-20260805171251873: work with no flags dispatched on the recorded OpenRouter model, full ladder done, spend measured $0.0006. Landed with full gate green (1537 tests + smoke).

title: The role tools' untyped schema properties route to zero strict-provider endpoints
description: Found by journey simulation rerun (run-20260805164356137) after the host-tools fix: OpenRouter still fails dispatch with 'No endpoints found that support tool use. Try disabling construct_append_work_log'. Cause: submit_draft.deliverable and append_work_log.detail carry no type in their inputSchema ('as JSON, an object or a string'). Strict providers require typed properties, so endpoint routing excludes everyone. Fix: declare them string in the schema and have role-serve parse JSON-looking strings on receipt, accepting objects as before so the Claude host contract is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Both tool schemas are fully typed; role-serve accepts a JSON string, a plain string, and an object for deliverable/detail with tests; a hosted journey run on an OpenRouter open-weight model dispatches without endpoint-routing failure; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 Fix landed (typed schemas + fromWire parse on receipt), full gate green. Same pending close gate as construct-4xr: recorded OpenRouter rerun blocked on 1Password unlock.
close_reason: Tool schemas fully typed; role-serve parses JSON-carrying strings on receipt (fromWire), objects still accepted. Note: the original 'No endpoints' error turned out to be construct-ppg (image-model fallback), but untyped properties remain a real strict-provider hazard; hardening kept. Recorded rerun green.

title: A role dispatched to OpenCode carries the host's bash and file-mutation tools it must never need
description: Found by journey simulation (runs run-20260805164046407, run-20260805164205580): dispatching a role to opencode with an OpenRouter model fails with 'No endpoints found that support tool use. Try disabling bash' — the host offers its full ambient toolset (bash, edit, write, patch) to the model, and OpenRouter's endpoint routing cannot place the request. The same ambient access is how a role once cited the tool's own package as legal authority (the recorded source-path-citation defect). A role's write surface is exactly two MCP writes (submit_draft, append_work_log); the host's mutation tools are authority it should not have. Fix: the OPENCODE_CONFIG construct already injects gains a tools section disabling bash/edit/write/patch for role runs; read tools stay so a role can read material handed to it via --dir.
acceptance_criteria: buildOpenCodeConfig emits tools:{bash:false,edit:false,write:false,patch:false}; existing config-shape tests updated; a journey simulation with an OpenRouter open-weight model completes dispatch (no endpoint-routing failure); full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 Fix landed (mutation tools disabled in generated OPENCODE_CONFIG), full gate green, 1531 tests. Close gate still open: the recorded OpenRouter rerun is blocked on 1Password authorization timeouts; rerun journey-sim-j1.sh once op resolves.
close_reason: Generated OPENCODE_CONFIG disables the host's tool authority for roles (bash/edit/write/patch plus glob/grep/list/webfetch/task/todos; read stays for --dir material). Wire capture confirmed role requests carry only the two MCP writes plus read. Recorded rerun run-20260805171251873 green.

title: Journey simulations: the core user journeys run through the packed spine on free local models, recorded as simulations
description: No external testers are available yet, and the project must not stall on them. A recorded set of journey simulations — packed install, isolated HOME, opencode + local ollama model — exercises the spine across the core user journeys (rough intake, legal outcome with citations, budget-capped run, decision inbox conflict, verdict loop, waiver path). Each run is recorded as a simulation, never as the external-user gate (r67.10 stays open and untouched by this). Every defect a simulation surfaces is filed as its own bead at discovery time. This bead is the harness plus the first recorded batch; it does not certify usability.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable harness runs journey outcomes end to end on a zero-cost local model; each run is recorded as a simulation with its run id; defects found are filed as beads with edges; r67.10's meaning is not diluted; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 Harness promoted to scripts/journey-sim.sh (work step carries no flags on purpose — the recorded dispatch surface is under test). REMAINS: rerun 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<from op item geralddagher-site:openrouter> scripts/journey-sim.sh <results-dir> openrouter/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507' with 1Password unlocked — proves densifier live and records the full journey batch on the promoted script. Gerald's move (op approval prompts time out unattended).
close_reason: Harness promoted to scripts/journey-sim.sh; recorded batches: hosted j1 clean (run-20260805171251873), hosted j1 failing (run-20260805183824874, found construct-rk1), free j2-j4. Four defects found and fixed by simulation this session (4xr, b7l, ppg, rk1), one filed open (densifier stall). r67.10 untouched.

title: Intake optimizes the rough outcome itself, so the user never has to say 'optimize this prompt'
description: Observed across real sessions: outcomes arrive as long, nonlinear, often voice-dictated text with fillers, corrections, and embedded tangents, and the user repeatedly has to append 'optimize this prompt' by hand. The optimization belongs to Construct's intake, not to the user's discipline. What: an intake layer that takes the rough framing and produces (1) the primary outcome in one sentence, (2) extracted explicit and implied constraints, (3) decisions already made, (4) parked tangents — while preserving the original text verbatim with provenance, showing the user the densified version for correction rather than silently replacing their words. The keyword implication map then reads the densified form. Free-tier honest degradation applies: without a model host, intake passes the raw text through and says so.
acceptance_criteria: Given a real rough framing from the corpus, intake emits a densified outcome plus extracted constraints with the original preserved verbatim and visibly diffable; without a host it degrades honestly; measured against the Gerald-authored corpus, not AI-invented text; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 Implemented and committed: densify seam (kernel/intake/densify.ts), host densifier (hosts/densifier.ts) mirroring namer.ts, CLI wiring (original words stay the record, densified form logged as intake-densified and fed to the namer, stated fallback on failure). Hermetic tests green incl. corpus-carried-verbatim over all 30 framings; full gate green (1543 tests + smoke). REMAINS before close (house rule: validate model-output matchers against a real provider): one recorded hosted run of a rough corpus framing. Command staged in construct-ij8 notes. Blocked on 1Password unlock — Gerald's move.
close_reason: Densifier live-validated against the real provider: both corpus framings (incl. the correction-heavy one) produced parseable extractions via densifierPrompt+parseDensified on qwen3-30b; hermetic tests carry all 30 framings verbatim; honest degradation proven live twice (stated fallback on host stall). Host-side invoke stall filed separately. Full gate green.

title: A non-text draft is stringified to [object Object] and passes the citation check
description:
Found regenerating the isolated first-run artifact (2026-08-05, run-20260805154317182, opencode + ollama/qwen3.5:4b-cx32k), after the draft-reading fix landed.

The employment role called submit_draft with a JSON object rather than text — its keys were finding, what_needs_to_be_true, likely_to_be_missed, cannot_determine, and, notably, 'claims-cited' and 'scope-diff', so the challenge ids in the assignment's obligations block were read as a response schema. The object was stored as-is and reached the structural checks, where string coercion turned it into the literal seven characters '[object Object]'. claims-cited passed on that string, because a string with no amounts, percentages, or dates has nothing untagged in it. scope-diff failed for the same reason, not because the role omitted the work: its cannot_determine key held exactly the content scope-diff looks for.

The contracts role in the same run submitted a string, but the string was itself a JSON envelope whose single key was 'deliverable', so the deliverable of record is a serialized wrapper rather than prose.

This is the third instance of one failure mode: a verdict recorded about something other than the deliverable. Two are fixed (construct-gws, construct-m0t); this is the same class arriving through the shape of the payload rather than through which field was read.

What to decide, not assume: whether submit_draft refuses a non-string deliverable outright, whether the kernel unwraps a known envelope shape, and whether a challenge that cannot see real text records unanswered rather than passed. The last one matters most on its own: a check that cannot read the deliverable must never report a pass, whatever the cause.
acceptance_criteria: A draft that is not text is refused at submit or recorded as unanswerable, and never produces a passing verdict; a structural check never runs over a coerced object; reproduced against the recorded run; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 Fixed on the reading side rather than at submit, deliberately: the append-only record keeps what the role actually sent, and refusing at submit would discard the work. draftText in src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts unwraps the {deliverable: ...} envelope and returns null for anything else; the coordinator then records every declared challenge unanswered with the reason. Verified on the same local model (run-20260805155758801): the employment task produced neither draft nor reply text and recorded challenge-unanswered with 'the deliverable is not readable as text' at state draft, where the previous build would have recorded a passing citation verdict; contracts submitted prose and reached final on two real passes. The [object Object] shape itself did not recur on this sample and is covered by unit test instead.
close_reason: Unreadable drafts are recorded unanswered, never passed; the JSON envelope is unwrapped. Verified on the same local model; full gate green (1505 tests, smoke pass).

title: Challenges ran against the reply text while the deliverable of record was the submitted draft
description:
Found re-running the isolated simulation on 2026-08-05 to verify the citation fix. The write-surface protocol tells a role in as many words that 'the draft is what lands on the record attributed to you', and roles believe it: in two consecutive local-model runs one role submitted a full deliverable through submit_draft and replied with a two-line summary, and another submitted a draft and replied with nothing at all (the run was flagged 'succeeded but produced no text'). The structural challenges read result.output.text, so the citation check passed a summary while the deliverable everyone would rely on went unread, and a task with an empty reply had no checks run on it at all.

This is the same class of failure as the challenges never running: a verdict recorded about something other than the thing being relied on.
acceptance_criteria: Structural challenges run against the submitted draft when one exists, falling back to the reply text; a run where the role submits a draft and replies with a summary records verdicts about the draft; full repo gate green.
close_reason: Fixed together: the assignment states what counts as evidence, the citation challenge fails source-path citations, and challenges now read the submitted draft. Verified by re-running the same outcome on the same local model; full gate green (1502 tests, smoke pass).

title: Briefs from the outcome path declare no challenges, so nothing is ever challenged on a real run
description:
Found in the isolated first-run simulation (2026-08-05, run-20260805144619133). Both deliverables came back at promotion state 'draft' with an EMPTY outstanding list, which reads as 'nothing is pending' and actually means 'nobody required anything'. briefFor in src/kernel/run/outcome.ts sets no challenges, so brief.challenges is undefined on every brief the spine produces, and the challenge machinery shipped in construct-h66.2 and construct-h66.3 never engages on the real path. It is reachable only by a hand-written brief.

The run makes the cost concrete. The contracts deliverable asserted Polish Labour Code art. 22 §1(1), Copyright Act arts. 41/43, Rome I art. 8, GDPR art. 28, and Directive 2011/7 — statutory claims from a 4B local model that nothing verified and nothing tagged. claims-cited and legal-issue-spot are exactly the challenges that case exists for, and neither was required.

What to decide, not assume: which challenges a spine-produced brief should declare by default, and whether that default varies by domain heat (commitment 13 says a substantive second-role pass runs only where heat warrants it, so requiring legal-issue-spot on every deliverable would spend a model call on every run). A defensible starting point is that the free structural checks are declared always because they cost nothing, and the substantive ones follow heat.
acceptance_criteria: A brief produced by the outcome path declares at least the challenges whose checks are free; a real run shows verdicts recorded and a promotion state that reflects them; the heat rule for substantive challenges is stated in the code or explicitly deferred with a reason; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 Fixed. SPINE_CHALLENGES in src/kernel/challenge/catalog.ts, declared by briefFor in src/kernel/run/outcome.ts. The heat rule is stated as a deferral with its reason rather than invented: no heat signal exists in the spine, and declaring the conditional three anyway would either spend a model call per deliverable or leave a permanently unanswerable challenge. Test tests/kernel/run/spine-challenges.test.ts goes through startRun+workRun, never a hand-written brief, because a test-authored brief is exactly what passed while the real path did not. Found while testing: the citation checker does not see durations or statute references, filed as construct-od7.
close_reason: Spine briefs declare claims-cited and scope-diff; conditional three deferred in code with their reason. Full gate green (1497 tests, smoke pass).

title: A role cites whatever is nearest on disk instead of its domain
description:
Found in the isolated first-run simulation (2026-08-05, run-20260805144619133, opencode + ollama/qwen3.5:4b-cx32k). Outcome: 'We want to hire a contractor in Poland'. The employment role returned: 'I reviewed the Construct package to ground the engagement: the employment domain catalog, the brief schema, and how inference cites evidence' and cited 'kernel/implication/domains.js — employment domain keywords' as its evidence for an employment-law question.

The role was dispatched into a working directory containing Construct's own installed package, had ambient filesystem access through the host, and grounded a legal issue-spot in the tool's source code. The contracts role in the same run did not do this and returned real statutory citations, so this is not a model that cannot do the work — it is a role reaching for the nearest readable thing when its assignment gives it no material.

Why it matters beyond the odd output: a citation is the unit of trust in this system (commitment 15). A role that cites the nearest file produces a deliverable that LOOKS cited and is not, which is worse than an uncited one. In a user's own repository the nearest readable thing is their source code, so this reproduces wherever Construct is run.

Directions worth weighing before picking one: the assignment can state that the outcome text is the material and the filesystem is not evidence for a domain question; the dispatch can run in a directory with nothing in it; or the citation can be checked for whether it plausibly belongs to the domain. The first is cheapest and the third is the only one that catches it after the fact.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatched role no longer grounds a domain answer in Construct's own package or the working directory; reproduced by re-running the same outcome on the same local model and inspecting the citation; whatever mechanism is chosen is stated in the assignment or the dispatch rather than relying on a model's judgement.
notes: 2026-08-05 Verified by re-run, not by reasoning. Same outcome, same binary, same local model (opencode + ollama/qwen3.5:4b-cx32k), packed install in an isolated HOME. Two sample runs: no file-path citation in either, and the employment role now reports 'CITE: none — Polish-law claims are [unverified]' where it previously cited kernel/implication/domains.js. Both halves landed: MATERIAL_PROTOCOL in src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts states the rule before the work, findSourceFileCitations in src/kernel/verify/claims.ts checks it after, folded into the claims-cited challenge so it fails on the real path. The re-run also surfaced construct-m0t, fixed in the same commit.
close_reason: Fixed together: the assignment states what counts as evidence, the citation challenge fails source-path citations, and challenges now read the submitted draft. Verified by re-running the same outcome on the same local model; full gate green (1502 tests, smoke pass).

title: Lesson store: workspace-scoped by default, with provenance carried and promotion explicit
description:
Commitment 6, as amended 2026-08-03 after adversarial review: a lesson belongs to the workspace it was produced in. Promoting one to serve the user across all their workspaces is a user decision per lesson, permitted only for technique and process lessons, with source quotes and facts stripped before promotion. A workspace carries a consent tier deciding whether it may consume globally-promoted lessons at all, and client or confidential work defaults to no.

The review that produced that amendment found the original design made client A's confidential facts part of client B's prompts as the happy path. The storage shape is therefore the safety property: scope is not a filter applied at read time but a fact recorded with the lesson, and a lesson with no workspace is not addressable by any workspace.

What: the store (workspace scope, provenance including where the lesson came from and whether that source was an ingested external document, the strip-on-promotion rule, and the workspace consent tier), plus the reads a prompt assembler will need. Retention automation and learned heat baselines are explicitly NOT in scope: STRATEGY defers each behind a written data-volume trigger.
acceptance_criteria: A lesson records its workspace, its provenance, and whether its source was externally ingested; a read scoped to workspace A never returns a workspace-B lesson; promotion to global is per-lesson, refuses non-technique lessons, and strips quotes and facts; a workspace whose consent tier forbids it consumes no global lessons; no retention or heat machinery ships; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: Fable/Opus-class — the scope rules are the safety property and the failure mode is silent cross-client leakage. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Lesson store shipped: workspace NOT NULL, append-only triggers, strip-on-promotion owned by the store, consent default-deny, cross-workspace supersession refused. Full gate green (lint, typecheck, 1516 tests, smoke).

title: Challenge contracts: the named checks a brief can require, run deterministically and free
description:
Commitment 13 says every brief may name challenges a deliverable must satisfy before promoting past draft, and that deterministic structural checks run always and free while a second-role substantive pass runs only where heat warrants it. The completion half already exists: brief.challenges declares them, src/kernel/run/promotion.ts derives state from recorded verdicts, and src/kernel/verify/claims.ts is one such check already written (untagged load-bearing claims). What does not exist is the catalog of named challenges or anything that runs them: a brief can declare 'pre-mortem' today and nothing will ever check it, so the challenge is satisfied by nobody noticing.

What: a challenge catalog with an id, a stated question, and a deterministic structural checker per challenge where one is possible (documented strongest objection present, pre-mortem present on plans, every load-bearing claim tagged via the EXISTING findUntaggedClaims, scope diff against the brief's declared inputs). Structural means it checks that the work was done and shown, never that the argument is good — judging the argument is the substantive pass and is not this bead. Run them at draft submission and record a verdict per challenge in the same VERDICT_ACTION shape promotion.ts already reads, so no second promotion path appears.
acceptance_criteria: A named challenge catalog exists; each structural checker runs without a model and is tested against passing and failing deliverables; running them records verdicts promotion.ts already understands, with no new promotion path; the citation checker reuses verify/claims.ts rather than reimplementing it; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better. Self-contained; read src/kernel/run/promotion.ts, src/kernel/completion/promotion.ts, src/kernel/brief/schema.ts and src/kernel/verify/claims.ts before editing. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Shipped. src/kernel/challenge/catalog.ts: five named challenges, four with free deterministic presence checks (claims-cited reuses verify/claims.ts), run by the coordinator when a deliverable lands and recorded as existing verdicts attributed to construct:structural. A challenge with no structural form is recorded unanswered, never passed, so promotion cannot ride on the cheap checks alone. assignmentFor now states the declared challenges and their questions before the work. Full gate green (1488 tests, smoke pass).

title: A person who did not build Construct can run one real outcome without being told how
description:
The Phase 2 audit (2026-08-05) found every remaining item in the program funnels through construct-r67.10: one external person runs one real outcome. 3ft, the 2jb epic, and Phases 3/4/5 all sit behind it. Nothing else is buildable without it.

What stands between that bead and a person is documentation, not code. README.md still describes the surface as it was before construct serve (MCP projection), verdict, --domains, and the voice landed, so the first thing an external reader sees understates what they can do and omits the lowest-friction path entirely: mounting the projection in the agent host they already use, where they never learn a CLI.

What: a first-run walkthrough that takes someone from install to a delivered result and a recorded verdict, covering both the CLI path and the in-host projection path, stating honestly what is alpha and what a host costs. README refreshed to match what shipped. Every command in it verified by running it, not asserted.
acceptance_criteria: A first-run document exists whose every command has been executed as written; the MCP projection path is documented with a real config; README names serve, verdict, and --domains; the friction-recording path (construct verdict, filing issues) is stated so r67.10's acceptance criterion can be met by the person themselves; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better. Self-contained. Close gate: full repo gate, plus every documented command actually run.
close_reason: Shipped. docs/first-run.md walks install to delivered result to recorded verdict, covering the CLI and the MCP projection path; every command was executed as written against a sterile XDG_DATA_HOME before publishing (doctor, outcome, outcome --domains, log, inbox, verdict listing, verdict recording, serve handshake showing all 8 tools). README refreshed to name serve, verdict, --domains, --host, and to link the walkthrough. Full gate green (1474 tests, smoke pass). r67.10 now needs only a person.

title: Team-in-a-box direction lands as dated STRATEGY amendments: standing watch, one voice, decision-theory demotion
description: Why: Gerald's 2026-08-05 direction review (brain dump, this session) reframed what Construct is competing on: not the crowded cloud-coding-agent lane, but the empty one — an extra set of eyes and ears across the tools a team already uses, harnessing host agents (commitment 1) rather than rebuilding them. Three deltas are not yet in STRATEGY.md: (1) watching as a product capability — standing outcomes over designated ground (doc repos, trackers) surfacing divergence and contention as inbox decisions, dogfooded first on Construct itself (commitment 16 made operational); (2) voice as a commitment — artifacts sound like Construct unless the user says otherwise (the predecessor design-language never actually carried over; see the voice bead); (3) speculative decision-theory modeling named in 'What is killed' — measurement stays, modeling without a consuming decision dies. What: dated amendments to STRATEGY.md, CHANGELOG Unreleased entry, close with the landing commit.
close_reason: Landed: STRATEGY.md amendments (standing watch in end-state + Phase 3, commitment 17 voice, decision-theory demotion in What is killed), CHANGELOG Unreleased entry, tracker pruning recorded on construct-2jb. Gate green before commit (1449 tests, lint, typecheck, smoke).

title: One MCP projection of the spine reaches every MCP host; adapters are for execution, not presence
description:
Shape B from the 2026-08-04 routing review: when the user is inside Claude Code, Codex, VS Code agent mode, or OpenCode, the host model has read their words before Construct is called. The spine (outcome, work, log, inbox, decide, plus catalog and brief contracts) is exposed as ONE MCP server, so every MCP-speaking host gets Construct without a per-host build. Adapters remain what they are today: execution transports (src/hosts/*), not presence.

CONTROLS (this bead was accepted-with-controls in adversarial review; they are the spec, not suggestions):
- Thin projection over the existing spine. No logic that does not already exist in src/cli + src/kernel. A second orchestrator inside the projection is the homebrew-runtime creep risk 4 vetoes.
- Completion stays kernel-owned (commitment 14). The projection MUST NOT expose any tool that advances draft -> challenged -> final. The host model may propose — name domains through the namer seam, submit drafts, append to the work log — and never certify.
- Host-model text arriving through the projection is untrusted input to the kernel's gates exactly as CLI input is; admissible() and the evidence bar apply unchanged.
- Per-editor extensions are out of scope and rejected pre-Phase-5. ACP (Zed family) is noted, not built.

Expected shape: new src/hosts/mcp/ projecting kernel surfaces; no kernel changes anticipated — if one turns out to be needed, that is a finding to surface, not to absorb silently.
acceptance_criteria: An MCP server exposes the spine's read/append surfaces; no completion-advancing tool exists on it (tested, not asserted); one real outcome driven end to end from inside one MCP host as the smoke; per-editor extension work absent; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05: elevated P2→P1 under the team-in-a-box direction. The MCP projection is not a convenience surface anymore — it is the carrier of the whole harness-the-hosts bet: one projection reaches Claude Code, Codex, VS Code Copilot, Zed, JetBrains (MCP is the de facto host protocol as of 2026). Thin stays a constraint: presence, never execution or completion.
close_reason: Shipped: src/hosts/mcp/projection.ts + jsonrpc.ts (framing shared with roleserve), construct serve CLI verb, 8 tests including the by-name refusal of submit_draft/append_work_log/promote/work and the untouched-completion sweep. Acceptance smoke: run-20260805060156645 driven from inside Claude Code headless via --mcp-config — model proposed 3 namings, all admitted through the unchanged gate, logged as host mcp:claude-code (judged by Fable in-session; Gerald's standing 'continue executing' covers execution, figures recorded here). No per-editor work. Full gate green. Landed a861920. Follow-up filed: construct-r67.24 (verdict tool).

title: Host-embedded operation is a strategy decision: amend STRATEGY.md or drop the direction
description:
Commitment 16: work without lineage is a decision — amend the document or drop the work. Gerald's direction (2026-08-04/05, this session): Construct should operate optimally inside OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, VS Code and similar hosts. STRATEGY.md currently authorizes neither half of that: the audience is "non-technical operators, reached through an outcome-in/decisions-out surface," and Phase 5 gates platform investment behind the external-user gate. Host-embedded operation is an unstated pivot until the document says otherwise — the exact drift class the predecessor died of.

DRAFT AMENDMENT POINTS (for Gerald to edit into STRATEGY.md himself; the diff is the drift record):
1. Name host-embedded operation as a first-class deployment shape beside the standalone CLI: the spine projected into whatever agent host the user already works in, via one protocol surface (MCP; ACP noted for the Zed family), never per-editor builds.
2. Scope it by phase: Phase 2 carries only a thin projection that serves dogfooding; host breadth (Codex, VS Code conformance work) is Phase 4/5 material behind the existing gates.
3. State the routing corollary if the inversion experiment's figures support adoption: where a capable host model is present it is the primary domain namer under the kernel's admissible()/evidence/completion gates; the keyword map is the zero-model fallback and the evidence layer. (Adoption itself is decided on construct-4jq, not here.)
4. Record the release policy the direction implies, consistent with what Phase 1 already says (Gerald, 2026-08-05): no backwards compatibility with anything pre-3.0.0 — the first official release is the first version of all of this, interfaces and flags change outright rather than deprecate, and the only backward obligation is 'construct cleanup' removing every trace older installs left behind.

Closing the other way is equally valid: a dated decision here to drop the host-embedded direction, which closes the MCP projection bead as superseded.
acceptance_criteria: STRATEGY.md carries a dated amendment naming host-embedded operation and its phase scoping, edited by Gerald — or a dated decision to drop the direction lands in NOTES here and the MCP projection bead is closed as superseded.
