title: A worktree agent's uncommitted files were reset by something it did not run
description:
During the 2026-08-20 fan-out, one worktree agent observed GLOSSARY.md and STRATEGY.md lose already-committed branch content mid-session; reflog showed 'reset: moving to HEAD' it did not issue. It restored verbatim from branch commits b3abe265/b64140fa before proceeding (documented in fcd3f2e2's body). Separately, another worktree reported a base missing the branch's skills wedge entirely. Suspects, unproven: the repo's beads git hooks (core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks post-checkout/post-merge) interacting with concurrent bd export/import in the shared .git, or the worktree-creation machinery. Do not run concurrent worktree agents alongside bd write operations until understood.
## Steps to Reproduce
Not yet reproduced: create a worktree, run bd export/import in the main checkout, watch the worktree's index. The two observations above are the only evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The reset's cause is identified with a recorded reproduction or ruled out with a recorded attempt; a guard (hook scoping, or a documented do-not-run-concurrently rule in CLAUDE.md) lands; both agent observations are explained.
close_reason: Investigated with a recorded two-worktree reproduction (2026-08-20, this container). Findings: (1) the 'reset: moving to HEAD' reflog entry is git's own worktree-add internals — it appears at creation, before any bd command or commit, so the observed evidence was misattributed, not malicious; (2) bd export/import in the main checkout does NOT touch worktree files — a planted uncommitted edit survived the full cycle; (3) bd invoked from a worktree does resolve the main checkout's .beads workspace (cross-context confirmed via bd where) but produced no harm in reproduction; (4) both agents' actual losses involved only UNCOMMITTED state, consistent with harness-level worktree state management outside this repo's reach — unprovable from here, recorded as the residual. Guard landed: the dispatch protocol now states uncommitted worktree state is volatile and agents checkpoint-commit early (CLAUDE.md). No speculative hook guard added: the measured reproduction showed no repo-tooling harm, and a guard without a measured failure is mechanism without a boundary.

title: Construct stop hooks fire in unrelated projects and crash on a missing .construct/run.mjs
description: Observed 2026-08-20 on Gerald's machine: launching Claude Code inside ~/Developer/Projects/geralddagher-site (a project with no construct footprint) ran 8 stop hooks and one failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for '/Users/geralddagher/Developer/Projects/geralddagher-site/.construct/run.mjs' (Node v24.19.0, non-blocking exit). Something at user level (~/.claude/settings.json or equivalent) injects construct hook entries that resolve .construct/run.mjs relative to whatever project is open. Fail-open held — the session continued — but a construct hook that errors in every non-construct project is mis-scoped: fail-open must also mean fail-silent-and-fast outside construct's own projects. Unknown whether this is predecessor (v2) debris the cleanup catalog should already cover, or the current hook set installed globally; the diagnosis decides the fix.
acceptance_criteria: A local session identifies which settings level injects the hook and whether it is predecessor or current construct; hooks become project-scoped or existence-guarded (a missing .construct/ exits 0 silently, instantly); if predecessor debris, the cleanup catalog gains the entry and construct cleanup removes it; verified by launching Claude Code in a non-construct project and observing zero construct hook errors.
notes:
2026-08-20 RESOLVED. Root cause: geralddagher-site/.claude/settings.json carried a full construct-legacy (v2) hook install — SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit, 8 Stop hooks total, every command pointed at "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.construct/run.mjs" — but the project's .construct/ directory was never created there, so every hook threw MODULE_NOT_FOUND (fail-open held; non-blocking).

This is predecessor debris, not current-construct behavior: current construct (this repo, 3.x) has no .construct/run.mjs launcher at all (kernel/hosts/cli architecture, node:sqlite store). It is exactly what src/kernel/cleanup/catalog.ts's existing 'project-settings' item already detects and strips (isPredecessorHookCommand matches .construct/(launcher/)?run.mjs) — no catalog change was needed, the entry already existed.

Checked the other three sibling projects with .claude/settings.json (oracle-app, admin-app, blackstory): none reference run.mjs — only geralddagher-site was affected.

Fix applied: `construct cleanup --scope=project --yes` in geralddagher-site. Removed the entire hooks block (43 hook entries, all predecessor's — nothing of the user's was in it) + 2 predecessor mcpServers (context7, construct-mcp) from settings.json, and 1 stale agent file (.claude/agents/construct.md + its manifest). Committed there: 111cc20 "Strip predecessor construct hooks that crashed on missing .construct/run.mjs".

Verified: grep for run.mjs in settings.json now 0 matches; `construct cleanup --dry-run` reports nothing left in ✓ tier; only remaining hook is the user's own PostToolUse JSON validator (not construct's); zero Stop hooks remain, so the stop-hook phase that crashed now runs nothing.
2026-08-20 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): the landing commit is real but lives in a different repository — geralddagher-site@111cc20, not this repo — because the bug and its fix were entirely in that sibling project's .claude/settings.json. This repo's construct-3jfu-touching commit is a tracker-only update (d6db1db9), which correctly carries no code trailer since no construct source changed. Verify with: cd ~/Developer/Projects/geralddagher-site && git show 111cc20 --stat.
close_reason: Closed

title: No CLI surface to list or approve held (run-derived) lessons
description:
construct-tnxi wired resolved decisions into candidate lessons through the existing admission gate (src/kernel/lessons/fromDecisions.ts, wired at 'construct decide'). Every one is held unconditionally pending human approval by design — that is correct and must not change. But there is currently no way to see the held queue or approve an entry: recordLesson and decideAdmission are kernel functions, reachable only by reading the database directly (as verified during that bead's own testing). A held lesson is functionally invisible once printed once at decide time.

Minimal CLI surface needed: something to list held (and admitted) lessons for a workspace, and something to approve a held one by calling decideAdmission again with basis:{kind:'human-approval', approver, detail}. Both are thin wrappers over kernel functions that already exist and are already tested (lessonsFor, admissionOf, decideAdmission).
acceptance_criteria: A CLI command lists held lessons for a workspace with their reason; a CLI command admits a held lesson by id with a named approver; both covered by a CLI-level test against a real store.
notes:
2026-08-20 Done. 'construct lessons' lists a workspace's lessons with their standing verdicts (held first; a lesson with no verdict lists as held — absence of a verdict is a hold nobody wrote down); 'construct lessons --admit=<id> --by=<approver>' re-runs the admission gate with a human-approval basis, so the only-a-human-admits rule stays in the gate, not the command. The tier domain is re-derived from the cited decision for run-derived lessons, 'unrated' (high) otherwise — never declared by the caller. Three CLI-level tests against a real store, full gate green (1979 tests, smoke pass). Landing commit be6ef924.
2026-08-20 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): landing commit be6ef924 on branch claude/construct-vision-direction-sn3qg5, not yet merged to main; resolves on merge.

2026-08-20 SECURITY REVIEW ADJUDICATED: the same bot pass flagged as HIGH that --admit accepts any --by string without authenticating the human. Judged not actionable as scoped: the CLI's trust boundary is the machine's shell — identical to decide, waive, and verdict, none of which authenticate — and dispatched roles are bounded by capability tokens that cannot record admissions; a shell-holding agent could equally write the SQLite row directly, so the command adds convenience, not capability. What the design does guarantee: the human flag is required by construction, the approver is recorded append-only, and a false admission is attributable and revocable by a newer held row. If construct ever gains a genuine multi-principal surface, admission authentication becomes real work — that trigger files the bead, not this bot pass.

notes: 2026-08-13: third instance of one pattern in one day, and the first found by a live run rather than by reading the checker. The earlier two were an explained placeholder and a whole-document read counting narrative as attribution; this one is a denial with a subject in front of it, which anchored rules cannot see. Fixed with two rules rather than another prefix: a denial-of-ownership test that reads anywhere in the head (names no / no <..> owner / not named / nobody / no one), and a word-count backstop above the longest plausible role title, since an attribution is a name or a role and anything sentence-length is describing a situation instead of answering. Both real strategy deliverables now fail S3 correctly; the recorded verdict in the work log stays as it was, because the log is append-only and the run genuinely passed at the time. Kept narrow deliberately: 'D. Okafor, who is not on call this week' still passes, and that case is a test.
close_reason: Fixed with this commit. Denial-of-ownership now read anywhere in the head, plus a word-count backstop above the longest plausible role title. Verified against both recorded BlackStory strategy deliverables: each now fails S3 where one previously passed. 3 regression tests added; full gate green (1853 tests).

title: Line-scoped ground evidence in routing, measured across runs and model families before any claim
description: RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 20 decided the direction: a project's own documents define its vocabulary, so ground evidence should be admitted to routing from the line an outcome's project-specific term appears on. Nothing in src/ does this today and no improvement is claimed. What is measured so far is one premise on one outcome with the deterministic router: privacy is reached at line scope with 4 domains implicated, and every wider window costs precision monotonically for no recall gain. What is unmeasured is everything that matters for shipping it: the model namer (the path that actually runs and actually missed), more than one outcome, and more than one model family. scripts/probe-ground-routing.mjs is the instrument and takes --ground/--outcome/--expect/--json. Do NOT widen the window past the line without a measurement that says why, and do NOT bind project terms to concerns in a static list — section 20 rejected declared vocabulary as the mechanism.

title: The reconcile re-derives adjudicated drift on every run, so the settled entries bury the live ones
description: scripts/reconcile-tracker.mjs reported 36 drifted beads, 34 of them benign and six already annotated 'DRIFT RESOLVED (audit)' on 2026-08-05 by a commit whose stated purpose was 'so the next audit does not re-litigate it'. It re-litigated them every run since, because reconcileSession compares only landed/in_flight and never reads the notes. The cost is not the noise: it is that a genuine drift has to be found among three dozen permanent entries, which is the failure mode the ritual exists to prevent.
notes: 2026-08-13: found during a full reconcile, not by the tool reporting itself. Fix: a NOTES marker 'DRIFT ADJUDICATED (<direction>)' that reconcileSession reads, with the direction recorded so a verdict on one disagreement never settles the opposite one; the legacy bare 'DRIFT RESOLVED' maps to closed-without-commit, which is the only direction it was ever written for. Adjudicated entries are counted and named, not listed. construct watch inherits the fix, since constructFindings reads report.drifted. Board went 36 drifted -> 0 drifted, 36 adjudicated. Convention written into CLAUDE.md's recording rules, along with the trap that bd update --notes replaces rather than appends.
close_reason: Landed with this commit. reconcileSession partitions drift into drifted/adjudicated by reading a dated, direction-named NOTES marker; five tests cover the direction rule, the legacy marker, partial settlement and that adjudication never invents agreement. All 36 standing disagreements adjudicated with checkable reasons. Full gate green.

title: A privacy-defining field named in the project's own vocabulary reaches neither router
description: Observed 2026-08-13 while verifying the nanobot surface on alpha.10, one run, one local model (qwen3.6:35b via ollama) — an observation, not a measurement. The outcome recorded was 'Decide whether the bulk canonical-edit path may change living_status for a filtered set of entities without a second approver, before the next release ships.' living_status is the field that carries BlackStory's living-person privacy guarantee; the whole question is a privacy control question. The host model named security, system-design, program-sequencing and coverage-gaps, and did not name privacy — 'second approver' reads as authorization, and security is a true and adjacent answer. The deterministic keyword map, run as a control on the same text, names NOTHING at all: privacy's keyword list carries 'personal data', 'delete everything', 'another customer' and similar, and none of them appear, because the user wrote the question in their own system's vocabulary. So this is not a model underperforming the fallback; neither path reaches the concern, for different reasons. The general shape: a project's privacy-defining field has a name that belongs to that project, and a router keyed to generic vocabulary cannot see that a domain-specific identifier IS the concern. Related to the earlier trial finding that a missing concern is answered by the nearest available one — except here the concern exists in the catalog and was still not reached.
acceptance_criteria: a decision recorded on whether this is addressable at all and how — candidate directions are workspace-declared vocabulary that binds a project's own terms to concerns, and letting a declared ground's own documents inform naming; whichever is chosen or rejected, the reasoning is written down, and any claim about improvement is measured across more than one run and one model family
notes:
2026-08-13: DISPATCH — Fable/Opus-class, this is a routing-design judgment with a measurement obligation attached. Do NOT 'fix' it by adding living_status to privacy's keyword list: that tunes the instrument to the one observed case and teaches nothing. The correlated-error and single-run caveats travel with any number quoted from this observation.

2026-08-13 DISPATCH note honoured: the fix is NOT a keyword added to privacy's list. Decision recorded as RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 20, with a measurement rather than an argument. Ground-informed naming is chosen over workspace-declared vocabulary, because the project already states the binding in its own documents (BlackStory's docs/architecture.md carries 'Living persons | ... unknown living status treated as living') while a declared glossary needs the user to know in advance which of their terms are privacy-defining, and cannot help on a first run. Measured at four context widths on the recorded outcome: outcome alone reaches 1 domain and not privacy; the line the term sits on reaches privacy with 4 domains; +/-1, +/-2, +/-4 reach privacy too but at 9, 11 and 12 domains. The binding is on the line, not in the neighbourhood. Instrument committed as scripts/probe-ground-routing.mjs so the follow-up does not rebuild it. Implementation and its obligation (more than one run, more than one model family, and the model namer rather than the keyword router) filed as construct-9phl. Correction to this bead's own record: the keyword control does not name NOTHING on this text, it names program-sequencing at 36; privacy is still absent, so the finding stands.
close_reason: Decision recorded: RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 20. Addressable, and the direction is ground-informed naming at line scope, not workspace-declared vocabulary; both directions reasoned through and the rejection written down. Measured at four context widths (privacy unreached on the outcome alone; reached at line scope with 4 domains; wider windows cost precision for no recall). No improvement claimed — the measurement is one outcome on the deterministic router, and the shipping obligation travels with construct-9phl. Probe committed as scripts/probe-ground-routing.mjs.

title: A codebase declared as ground is surveyed as if it were a document set
description: src/hosts/sources.ts defaults SurveyEmphasis to 'prose' and src/cli/index.ts:3344 applies that default when none is passed. For a ground root that is a repository, prose ranks the 60 markdown files ahead of every file that would settle a question about behaviour, and the run header then reports '60 documents listed, prose-first' as though that were coverage of the root. The BlackStory run's open questions are the visible cost: every one that needed code named a path the survey never listed. The license block does let a role go past the list, which is why this is a ranking defect rather than a fence defect - but a default that hides the code from the survey makes going past the list an act of initiative rather than the obvious next step.
acceptance_criteria: the emphasis default reflects what the declared root actually holds rather than assuming prose, or the survey header states plainly that code was ranked out and how much; the cap interaction is stated; existing prose-ground behaviour is unchanged where the root is prose
notes: 2026-08-13: affects every run whose declared ground is a repository, whatever the ask — a security assessment over a code ground is mis-served by prose-first ranking in exactly the same way, and worse, since its evidence is almost entirely code.
close_reason: Landed: survey reports unlistedCode so the partial row says what kind of thing the cap dropped. Verified against the real BlackStory root (40 of 6055 listed, 3895 unlisted source files). Full gate green (1823 tests).

title: The MCP projection has not grown with the CLI: records, review, compose and erasure are unreachable from an operator surface
description: The nanobot trial (construct-grs7) established the projection as an operator surface whose value is reachability from chat rather than a terminal. Since then the CLI gained review (drift over declared ground), record add/list/show/erase (per-subject facts with cited field history), compose (one document from a run's deliverables) and decide --apply. None are projected, so an operator working through nanobot can record an outcome and read an inbox but cannot see a customer record, ask what disagrees in the ground, compose a run's deliverables, or honour an erasure request. drop_note is also record-only there: it does not run the context loop the CLI runs, so a note dropped through the projection produces no deltas, proposals or drift.
acceptance_criteria: a decision recorded on which of these belong on an operator surface and which are deliberately CLI-only, with whatever is decided in scope projected and probed; drop_note's record-only behaviour is either stated in its tool description or the loop is run behind it
notes: 2026-08-13: follow-up commit fixes a typecheck error the repo-gate caught after close (test compared a string against the tool-name union). Complete gate re-run green on the final state: typecheck, lint, 1829 tests, smoke.
close_reason: Landed: records + record projected (fields, citations, history); review/compose/erasure recorded as deliberately CLI-only in the projection header with reasons; drop_note states its record-only behaviour and names the command that runs the loop. Probed live through construct serve over stdio. Full gate green (1829 tests).

title: The schema version guard has never been able to fire and never will
description: openStore INSERTs schema_version only when absent and throws only when found > SCHEMA_VERSION. It never UPDATEs. The live store on this machine reports schema_version=4 while the tree is at 14 — it has claimed 4 since creation, through ten bumps. The forward-incompatibility protection ('written by schema version N, newer than this build understands') therefore cannot fire for any store created before a bump, which is every real store. Verified live 2026-08-13: the installed alpha.5 binary opens a store carrying schema-14 tables and reads runs written by alpha.9 without complaint. Benign today only because every change so far has been additive new tables filled in by CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; the day a change is not purely additive, an old build opens a store it cannot understand and the guard stays silent.
acceptance_criteria: opening a store whose recorded version is older than the build advances the recorded version, so the guard reflects what the store actually carries; a store recorded as newer than the build is still refused; the advance is safe to run repeatedly and does not depend on a migration step that does not exist
close_reason: Landed: openStore advances a recorded version below the build; newer-than-build still refused; repeatable. Full gate green (1825 tests).

title: A multi-role outcome merges issues but composes no document
description: Settled by the live strategy run (RESEARCH-DECISIONS 19). Synthesis merges issues across roles; nothing writes one document from N deliverables, so an outcome spanning three concerns returns three partial views and leaves composing to the reader. Each role correctly declines to claim the whole — strategy-alignment says so in its own scope-diff slot — which makes this a missing pass rather than a missing playbook. A composition pass must cite the deliverables it composes and must not assert anything none of them established.
acceptance_criteria: a run with more than one completed deliverable can produce one composed document that cites which role's deliverable each part came from; a claim in the composition that appears in no source deliverable is refused by the same discipline that refuses an uncited claim; a single-deliverable run composes nothing and says so; the composition is a draft like any other and goes through the same challenges
close_reason: construct compose: structural attribution screen + per-role support check, unsupported claims removed, uncovered section required; proven on run-20260813111558843 where both screens fired

title: The external-read tool invites a role to log a read it did not make
description: Observed live 2026-08-13. A role recorded an external read whose locator was 'no external source used' and whose took field said 'n/a — recorded to satisfy the tool's per-read logging habit; this dispatch did no external research'. The tool description says to 'record the read when you make it, not at the end', which a model read as a per-run obligation. The store's own guard passed because both fields were non-empty strings. A provenance table whose rows include declarations of having read nothing is worse than an empty one.
acceptance_criteria: the tool description states that it is called only when the role actually read something outside its material, and that not calling it is the normal case; a role that did no external research produces no rows
close_reason: Tool description and role protocol now say it is called only when the role actually read something outside, and that not calling it is the normal case

title: A record cannot be erased, and records hold exactly the data an erasure request names
description: records and record_fields are append-only by trigger, matching every other evidence table. But unlike the work log, records hold per-subject facts about named people and organizations — the data an erasure request under GDPR Article 17 or CCPA is about. There is no deletion path at any layer, so the honest answer to a customer asking to be forgotten is currently that the store cannot comply. Construct ships a privacy lens; this is the one table where append-only and the obligation collide.
acceptance_criteria: a decision recorded in RESEARCH-DECISIONS on how erasure and append-only evidence coexist, and whatever it decides is implemented: either a redaction path that preserves the shape of the history while removing the subject's content, or a documented statement that records must not hold personal data with what they are for instead
close_reason: Erasure implemented: unlock-scoped deletion for records and notes, append-only erasure log holding no erased content, notes naming a second subject reported not destroyed

title: An approved outward write that nobody applies is a decision, not a change
description: kernel/store/sources.ts markApplied records that a proposal was applied and refuses without authority — but nothing performs the application. Approved proposals against a github/jira/docs source terminate as rows. Give an approved proposal a path to actually land through the host, and make an unappliable one say so rather than sit silently approved.
acceptance_criteria: an approved proposal can be handed to a host for application with its change and justification; the applied decision is recorded only from what the host reported succeeding; a proposal whose source has no way to be written reports unappliable with its reason rather than remaining silently approved; rejection still cannot be overridden by applying; tests cover apply-succeeded, apply-failed, and unappliable.
close_reason: applyProposal seam + host applier + construct decide --apply; applied recorded only from what the host reported; rejection never overridden; unappliable stays approved

title: A customer is a record, not a domain string in workspace memory
description: The context loop turns notes into workspace lessons keyed by a free-text domain. 'Acme's renewal moved to Q3' becomes a lesson in domain acme, not a field on a record, and the only per-customer isolation available is one workspace per customer — which also isolates the memory you wanted shared. Add a record store: named entities within a workspace that a note-derived delta can update, each field change citing the note line that taught it.
acceptance_criteria: records are append-only-evidenced entities with typed field updates, each update carrying a resolvable note citation; the context loop can route a delta to a record instead of workspace memory; records are readable back with their field history; workspace lessons keep their current behavior for non-record facts; schema migration is additive; tests cover creation, update with citation, and refusal of an uncited update.
close_reason: records + record_fields (schema 13); note-cited field updates through the context loop; construct record add/list/show with field history

title: Research a role did outside declared ground leaves a provenance row or it did not happen
description: Construct builds no connectors and has no web tier; whatever domain research happens is the host binary's own tools. It produces no source_reads row, so a deliverable resting half on a declared repo and half on the open web carries provenance for one half and silence for the other. The fabricated-provenance gate does not notice, because it only guards declared sources. Record what a role read outside declared ground as its own read class.
acceptance_criteria: a host-reported external read is recordable against the run with its locator and what was taken from it; the deliverable's grounding summary distinguishes declared-source grounding from external research; a claim citing neither is still refused; no connector is built and nothing fetches — this records what the host reports; tests cover a run with external reads only, declared only, and both.
close_reason: external_reads table (schema 12), record-external-read grant + MCP tool, role protocol instruction, show distinguishes declared ground from reported research

title: No surface reaches the staffing gate: a recorded unmet concern cannot be staffed without writing code
description: kernel/staffing/profile.ts evaluates a profile and raises the proposal to the decision inbox, and kernel/implication/naming.ts records the unmet concerns that motivate one, but nothing on the CLI or the MCP projection connects them. Today a user reads 'concern-unmet' in the work log and has no command that turns it into a proposal. Needed: a spine verb that lists recorded unmet concerns for a run and submits a profile through evaluateProfile, printing the refusal verbatim when it refuses. Projection side stays read-only under the existing rule: the host model may draft a profile, never accept one.
acceptance_criteria: a CLI verb lists unmet concerns per run and submits a profile through the existing gate; refusals print with their kind and reason; acceptance stays a human decision through the inbox; no new gate logic outside kernel/staffing
notes: 2026-08-13: landed as 'construct staff' with two subcommands. list reads concern-unmet entries from the work log (per run, or across all runs); propose reads a drafted profile from JSON and puts it through evaluateProfile unchanged. No gate logic outside kernel/staffing: the verb prints the refusal's kind and reason verbatim rather than summarizing, and an admitted profile becomes an inbox decision whose default position stays NOT_STAFFED, so nothing on this path widens the catalog. Two things the gate did not cover and the surface must: a hand-drafted profile missing a list would have crashed on a property access, so the lists are defaulted before evaluation and come back as a malformed refusal; and proposing the same profile twice would have hit a primary-key collision, so an already-open decision is reported instead. MCP projection deliberately untouched — the host model may draft a profile, never submit one. 8 tests through the real CLI surface, verified end to end through bin/construct.mjs. Full gate green.
close_reason: Landed: 'construct staff list' surfaces recorded unmet concerns per run with the reason each was refused; 'construct staff propose --file=' submits a drafted profile through evaluateProfile, printing refusals verbatim with their kind and raising admitted profiles to the inbox at NOT_STAFFED. Acceptance stays a human decision. 8 CLI tests; verified through the packaged bin. Full gate green (lint, typecheck, 1850 tests, smoke).

title: A repo surveyed for its code is not a repo surveyed for its prose
description: hosts/sources.ts caps at DOCUMENT_CAP=40 and sorts prose ahead of code, so a real repository hands a role forty markdown files and no code. That is the right default for 'understand the surfaces' and wrong for 'understand the code', and there is no knob for which was meant. Make the survey shape declared per source rather than constant.
acceptance_criteria: a source carries a survey emphasis (prose-first, code-first, or all) and a cap, declared at source add and stored; the walk honours both; the default is today's behavior so existing workspaces are unchanged; the recorded partial row names which emphasis dropped what; tests cover each emphasis against one fixture tree.
close_reason: source_shapes table (schema 11); --emphasis/--cap on source add; walk ranks per emphasis; partial row names the ranking that dropped the rest

title: Notes accepts a directory of documents, not one file per invocation
description: construct notes takes one positional file. Ingesting a directory of call transcripts is one shell invocation per file, each a separate host model call. Accept a directory locator and ingest every extractable document under it as its own note, sharing one docling probe, reporting per-document outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: notes accepts a file or a directory; a directory walks with the same skip rules and ordering as the source survey; each document lands as its own append-only note; one refusal does not abort the batch and every refusal is printed with its remediation; the work log records the batch; tests cover a mixed directory with one unreadable document.
close_reason: notes accepts a directory; each document its own note, shared probe and survey, refusals do not end the batch; per-note loop extracted

title: Trial: nanobot as the operator surface for blackstory research decisions
description: Trial nanobot (HKUDS/nanobot, Python, MIT) as a carrier for construct's MCP projection, with blackstory as the specific subject rather than a toy outcome. Blackstory's operator work is research triage - reading a nomination, deciding an era, flagging a laundered assertion - and it is currently reachable only from a terminal, which is why the decision inbox is a data structure rather than a habit. Attach construct's projection (construct serve, stdio) as an MCP server in a nanobot instance scoped to its own config and workspace, record real blackstory outcomes through it, and answer three questions on the record: does the projection survive a host it was not designed for, does the inbox get used when it is reachable from a chat surface, and what does the host model do with the catalog tool that the CLI namer does not. Scope limits: presence only, no dispatch (the projection exposes none by design), no capability token in a nanobot instance reachable from any non-local channel, and blackstory's production discovery pipeline stays on its own scheduler - this trial does not relocate it.
acceptance_criteria: a nanobot instance with its own config and workspace, construct projection attached over stdio, at least three real blackstory outcomes recorded through it, findings written up including what broke, and an explicit local-only statement about capability tokens; no change to blackstory production scheduling
notes: 2026-08-13: trial run. nanobot v0.3.0 installed via uv tool, isolated instance at ~/.nanobot-blackstory/, construct serve attached under tools.mcpServers, local model via ollama (apiBase needs the /v1 suffix or the provider 404s before any tool is reached). Projection loaded unmodified; the host model read the catalog and recorded three real BlackStory outcomes (run-20260813042226946 and siblings), all namings admitted, readable from the standalone CLI attributed to the namer. No dispatch, no completion advance, no capability token in the instance - the last is a standing condition because that host can enable externally reachable channels. Two findings: the host reads the INSTALLED catalog (machine had alpha.5 with 15 domains while the tree carried 17, unwarned on either side), and a missing concern is answered by the nearest available one (a coverage outcome was named 'measurement' with a reason that reads perfectly and is the wrong concern). Write-up: docs/host-trial-nanobot.md. DRIFT: that file was swept into another concurrent session's commit 344be9c7 by its git add -A, so the doc is on main under a bead that did not author it; not rewritten because that session is live.
close_reason: Superseded by the second pass under construct-n42q, which closed both of this trial's open findings (installed-vs-tree catalog drift, and the version being illegible from the surface). The unmet-concern observation recurs in a new form and is tracked as construct-clrw.

title: Cursor CLI host adapter: subscription-auth dispatch through the user's cursor-agent binary
description: Feasibility established from Cursor's primary CLI docs (cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters, read 2026-08-11): cursor-agent supports non-interactive dispatch via '-p --output-format json|stream-json', '--model <model>', '--workspace <path>', '-v', and a non-interactive 'status' auth probe; 'login' authenticates against the user's Cursor subscription. Same seam and restraint as src/hosts/codex (the freshest shape to copy: adapter.ts + pin.ts with named expectations + conformance probe script + presence row). Every depended-on behavior becomes a probed expectation against a pinned cursor-agent version BEFORE the adapter trusts it — the docs describe, only the probe verifies (output framing, exit codes on failed runs, unknown-model behavior, whether events name the model, stdin handling). Must NOT: bundle a runtime, add an API-key-only path (subscription login is the point; CURSOR_API_KEY may be supported as secondary), assert unprobed framing.
acceptance_criteria: adapter + pin + probe:cursor passing against an installed cursor-agent; presence row dispatchable; CLI --host=cursor wired through adapterForHost; full gate green
notes:
DISPATCH (2026-08-11): blocked on Gerald's move — install cursor-agent (Cursor's CLI installer) and sign in; the installer is an external download Construct does not run unattended. After install: Fable/Opus-class session, copy src/hosts/codex shape (adapter+pin+probe), probe before trusting. Close gate: full repo gate + probe passing.
VERDICT (2026-08-11): cursor-agent 2026.08.11-e8db854 installed under Gerald's direction, logged in as his Cursor account. Probe pass 9/9. E2E: 4-role run on composer-2.5 delivered with degradation notes; gemini/kimi dispatches correctly failed loudly on the plan's monthly premium-API limit (resets 2026-08-20) with the host's own message now surfaced in the work log instead of a bare exit code. Judged by Opus 5 under standing approval.
close_reason: adapter + pin (9 probed expectations, all passing live) + probe:cursor + --host=cursor wired + presence row; plan-mode read-only dispatch; live e2e on composer-2.5 (untuned family): 4 roles delivered with model-untuned-best-effort notes recorded. Gate 1684/1684 + smoke.

title: README lens-coverage claim is stale: all fifteen concerns now carry a lens, not thirteen
description: README says thirteen of fifteen concerns carry a lens and two route to the default template; lenses.ts now equips all fifteen catalog domains (commerce-tax via the commerce lens, marketing-claims via the brand lens). Correct the README seat table and surrounding prose so the coverage report is true again; check docs/first-run.md and docs/org-map.md for the same stale claim (org-map is generated — regenerate, don't hand-edit).

close_reason: README seat table and coverage paragraph corrected; generated docs already current

title: Second tuned family: eval-gate GPT via the Codex adapter on the fixture-organization harness
description: hosts/tuning.ts records Claude as the only tuned family. Once the Codex adapter dispatches, run the existing fixture-organization scored runs (clean-context lens runs, all rungs — the same evidence standard the Claude entry cites) against the GPT family through codex, and append a TUNED_FAMILIES entry only if the gate passes. Measured gates over asserted claims (commitment 15): the entry is appended from run evidence, never from expectation. Until then GPT runs labeled best-effort with a degradation note, which is correct and stays.

DISPATCH (2026-08-11): Tier: Fable/Opus-class for judging, mechanical runs any tier. Blocked on construct-5wv9. Self-contained: evidence standard is the existing claude TUNED_FAMILIES entry (fixture-organization scored runs, clean-context lens runs, all rungs; harness under fixtures/org-harness*); promotion criteria are construct-p9e's family promotion gate. Append a gpt entry only from run evidence; a failing gate is a recorded result, not a retry loop. Close gate: full repo gate + the run record committed.
VERDICT (2026-08-11): judged by Opus 5 under Gerald's standing approval; scoring is the committed structural scorer against the pre-committed answer key, so no model judgment entered the pass/fail. Correlated-error caveat n/a (scorer is deterministic). Endpoint codex added to the shared runner so the prompt stayed byte-identical; run recipe matched the tuned family's composed shape exactly.

Before an adapter bead exists, establish: install path, non-interactive invocation shape, subscription auth behavior, and output framing stability. If probeable, file the adapter bead copying the opencode pin pattern; if not, record why in RESEARCH-DECISIONS.

title: doctor checks host reachability: opencode, claude SDK, codex — found, version, auth state
description: README states doctor does not yet check that a host is reachable, and a user whose first run fails on a missing host deserves the failure at doctor time. Extend construct doctor to report per known host adapter: binary/SDK found (yes/no + path), version vs pinned version, and whether it can authenticate (without triggering interactive login). Report, never block: a missing host is information, not an error, because serve-only use is legitimate.
acceptance_criteria: doctor output lists each host with found/version/auth columns; tests cover found and not-found paths via sterile harness; full gate passes
close_reason: presence survey wired into doctor, report-only; probes use the host environment discipline; gate green 1668/1668

title: Seat-mode tracker projection: proposals reach the user's actual tracker through the recorded substrate
description:
Seat mode now shapes every dispatch (posture: propose, never done), but proposals still live only in Construct's own deliverables. The substrate for projecting them into the user's tracker exists and is unreachable: src/kernel/tracker/{authority,projection}.ts and src/kernel/store/{projections,reconcile}.ts. Wire it behind the host seam (a host adapter action, never a kernel connector), authority boundaries as authority.ts declares them, every projected proposal recorded before it crosses.

NOTES-DISPATCH: DISPATCH (2026-08-11) — judgment half (which surface, which tracker first, authority mapping) is Fable/Opus-class; mechanical half (wiring recorded substrate to an adapter action) Sonnet-class. title: The catalog's precision lessons never reach the router, and handing it everything is measured wrong
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

No model call is needed: every arm's per-outcome answers are on file, so this re-derives for free.

1. Read RESEARCH-DECISIONS section 3 — 116 of 207 catalog keywords have never fired, and the precision knowledge bought since (which keywords fire mostly wrong, which conditions separate a near miss from a hit) lives in comments addressed to whoever next edits the catalog.
2. grep the router path for any read of those conditions: src/kernel/implication/ and src/kernel/routing/. Nothing reads them. The router sees one-line concerns.
3. Read RESEARCH-DECISIONS section 18's table, and re-derive it from fixtures/namer-arms/*.json with scripts/measure-decisions.mjs --namer-compare. Section 17's proposed fix — hand the router the catalog's conditions — costs 0.225 of out-of-family miss for zero precision.

## What happens

Section 3's finding stands open as a defect with no proposed fix. implicatedWhen clauses buy no precision at all (58 of them move the over-rate 0.376 to 0.377) while costing 0.225 of miss. notImplicatedWhen clauses buy precision that scales with dose (0.376 to 0.353 to 0.321 to 0.190) and cost recall more gently, but no configuration tested beats the shipped router on both axes, and this project's promise is stated on recall — a user not ambushed by a domain they did not know existed.

## Why it matters

construct-jor closed on where ownership facts come from and says explicitly that it does not deliver this. Left in prose, a defect nobody is holding stops being a defect and becomes a paragraph. This bead is where it lives now.

## PRECONDITION, from section 18

Arms D and E were NOT shown to be free. Their paired p-values are 0.61 and 0.33 on 168 label-pairs, which means this corpus cannot tell, not that they are equivalent — both moved the wrong way on miss. Anyone revisiting a measured exclusion set needs a corpus that can size a modest regression BEFORE spending another run. Sizing that corpus is the first move here, not the second.
acceptance_criteria: Either a mechanism that gets measured precision knowledge to the router without a recall cost this corpus can see, on a corpus large enough to size one; or a written decision that the lessons stay editor-facing, with the measured reason. No run against a new exclusion set is spent before the corpus is shown able to detect a regression of the size at stake.
notes:
2026-08-11: filed out of the section 18 close-out. Sections 3, 17 and 18 are the written record; fixtures/namer-arms/ holds the per-outcome answers of every arm, so a re-derivation costs no consultations.

2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (open-but-named): commits landed the measurement and its record (fixtures/namer-arms/, sections 3/17/18), not the outcome: acceptance needs either a mechanism carrying precision to the router or a written decision that the lessons stay editor-facing. Stays open.
close_reason: Closed

title: The README's routing figures were measured on the contaminated instrument and need re-deriving, not patching
description:
README lines 86-94 state the shipped router misses 0.301 (28/93, Wilson [0.217, 0.401]) and falsely implicates 0.188 (15/80, [0.117, 0.287]), citing RESEARCH-DECISIONS 10.

Both figures predate construct-rxah, which scored every JSON-repaired namer reply as a failure and fell that outcome back to the keyword arm. A clean single-tier re-run of the identical shipped configuration on the fixed instrument (2026-08-10, recorded in fixtures/namer-arms/shipped.json, 0 failures, 7 repairs) measures out-of-family miss 0.280 (26/93).

This is NOT a number swap. The miss figure has a stable denominator (expected labels, fixed by the corpora) and can be updated directly. The over-rate cannot: 17 records that the script's over denominator changed between runs, so 0.188 (15/80) is on a basis the current script does not reproduce — the clean run reports unspent over 0.376 (35/93), which is a different pooling. The README's over sentence needs its basis established before any figure replaces it.

Until then the front door quotes a number produced by a defective instrument. The direction is favourable (0.280 is better than 0.301) so this is not a false-advertising problem, but it is an unearned one.
acceptance_criteria: README's miss and over figures both re-derived from a recorded clean-instrument run with their denominators stated; RESEARCH-DECISIONS 10's quoted figures carry the same correction note 17 now carries; Gerald approves the front-door wording
notes:
2026-08-10: fixed in the same session it was filed, and cheaper than the bead assumed. No re-run was needed — the clean shipped run's per-outcome answers were already recorded in fixtures/namer-arms/shipped.json, so both figures were re-derived from it.

miss 0.301 (28/93) -> 0.280 (26/93). Two labels, noise, and conservative: the old figure understated the router.

over 0.188 (15/80) -> 0.374 (40/107). Roughly double and in the flattering direction. The denominator differs, so this is not purely a behavior change — but 0.188 is not reproducible by the current script and every available reading is worse, so it is replaced rather than reconciled. 10's claim that B held 'the lowest over-rate measured anywhere in this document' is withdrawn with it.

README, 10 and 17 all carry the corrected pair or a correction note. The 10 adoption is unaffected: A0 is byte-identical across runs and B still dominates it on miss.
close_reason: Both figures re-derived from the recorded clean run and published; 10 and 17 annotated

title: A dispatched role's capability token cannot be revoked before its lease expires except by rotating the secret every run shares
description:
The token a role carries is signed, bound to run+task+role, grant-constant, and expires with the task's lease. Its revocation story is thinner than its scoping: the only channel that kills a live token early is deleting or rotating the one install-wide signing secret, which kills every outstanding token for every run and role at once.

An operator who decides mid-run that a role should stop writing — a runaway loop past the draft and note caps, or content that should not land on the record — has no lever short of waiting out the lease (up to fifteen minutes) or taking down every run in flight.

Related, from the same deliverable: the token payload carries a nonce documented as distinguishing two tokens minted for the same task, and authorizeRoleToken never reads it. Nothing in rolewrite.ts supplies one to compare. A token minted for a crashed attempt therefore stays fully valid for the rest of its window, on the file's own terms. The cost of wiring it rises with time, because a slow role finishing a write just after a re-dispatch currently succeeds and would then be refused, so closing it later needs a look at real run timing rather than only a code change.

The decision, which is a design call and not a bug: is 'wait for expiry' an accepted position — in which case say so where the capability design is stated, the way the waiver design explicitly rejected --all — or is a reasoned, logged, per-task revocation surface worth building, in the shape construct waive already uses?
acceptance_criteria: Either the accepted-position statement lands where the capability design is written, or a per-task revocation surface ships logged the way waive is; the unread nonce is wired or its non-use is recorded as deliberate
notes: 2026-08-10: found by the security and system-design deliverables on stakeholder packet Case 5 (run-20260811002510453), independently reaching the same finding from different lenses. DISPATCH: Fable/Opus-class for the design call. Self-contained: src/kernel/capabilities/tokens.ts, secretfile.ts, src/kernel/run/rolewrite.ts, coordinator's mint call. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: construct log reports a leased task as still running without comparing its deadline to now
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a run and kill the process after a task takes its lease but before the deadline passes.
2. construct log --run <id>

## What happens

writeRunState in src/cli/index.ts prints 'Still running — N task(s) hold a lease until <timestamp>' whenever a task's state is 'leased', with no comparison of leaseUntil against the current time. A process that crashed after claiming and before the deadline reads as healthy until the reader notices the timestamp is in the past and does the arithmetic themselves.

## Why it matters

The footer exists precisely because a live run and a dead one ended at the same log line. It closes most of that gap and leaves this one: the tool hands the reader the comparison instead of making it. The deliverable that found this put it plainly — the fix's own comment says the goal was to avoid implying the tool is watching, which read the other way is an admission that it does not resolve the ambiguity.

## What to fix

Compare leaseUntil to the injected clock and say which it is: still running, or a lease that expired at <t> with nothing since, which is the shape of a process that died. Keep the no-polling posture — this is one comparison at read time, not a watcher.
acceptance_criteria: A run whose lease has expired reads differently from one still in flight; a test drives both states
notes: 2026-08-10: found by the operations and measurement deliverables on stakeholder packet Case 3 (run-20260811001658945), not by a session looking for it. DISPATCH: any tier; self-contained in src/cli/index.ts writeRunState. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: The operations and measurement rubrics require a named owner the material cannot supply: settle O2 and M3 against the [unowned] rule
description:
Four of eleven verdicts in fixtures/persona-acceptance/2026-08-10-panel-waveb.md are rejections, and all four are the same line.

O2 (Support/on-call): 'An owner is named for answering the failure, with what access that person needs; the team is not an owner.'
M3 (Data/analyst): 'Instrumentation names where a number would be recorded and who owns recording it.'

Both are must-lines. The deliverables named the access precisely, named where a number would be recorded, and wrote [unowned] with the reason the material contains no owner and who would have to supply one. That is what the work-product directive now REQUIRES, changed the same day under construct-z34: every issue names an owner or writes [unowned] and says who would have to decide, because a resolving step with nobody attached is a step nobody takes and an invented name is worse.

So the shipped rule and the pre-committed rubric disagree, and both are working correctly. The rejections stand as recorded — a rubric reinterpreted after seeing the deliverables it judges is not pre-committed, and the pre-commitment is the whole instrument.

The decision is narrow: does O2 (and M3) mean 'name a person', or 'name a person, or state that the material does not contain one and who would supply it'? If the second, amend the two lines with a date and let a future panel judge the amended text. The four recorded verdicts keep their as-run values either way.
acceptance_criteria: O2 and M3 either stand as written with the reason recorded, or are amended with a dated line; the 2026-08-10 wave-B panel verdicts are not rescored either way; a future panel judges against whichever text stands
notes: 2026-08-10: surfaced by the wave-B panel pass, which is the first time the rubric met deliverables produced under the [unowned] rule. Gerald's call — this is a requirements clarification, which is stakeholder work by the amended protocol. Labelled human.

title: A long stance qualifier bleeds into the conflict question's tally and makes it unreadable
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an outcome implicating three or more concerns on a host whose roles write qualified stances.
2. Have one role end with a long qualifier, e.g. 'STANCE: proceed these are real but bounded exposures (evidence destruction and capped-privilege forgery, not reach to funds or other tenants), worth filing as follow-up work rather than holding the install'.
3. construct inbox

## What happens

Observed live on run-20260811001658945:

  'Two concerns disagree on this outcome: <outcome> — 2 role(s) say hold, 1 say proceed these are real but bounded exposures (evidence destruction and capped-privilege forgery, not reach to funds or other tenants), worth filing as follow-up work rather than holding the install. This one is yours to call.'

frameConflict builds its tally from stanceLabel(), which is deliberately 'never plainer than what the role declared' and therefore includes the whole qualifier. That is right for a POSITION, where the qualifier is part of what the role said. It is wrong for the TALLY, which is a count and reads as one until a sentence-long qualifier lands inside it. The question line then runs past where a reader stops.

## Why it matters

The question is the first and often only thing read in the inbox. Keeping the qualifier there was a deliberate fix (a role writing 'proceed with conditions' must not be counted as a plain proceed), so the fix is not to drop it — the qualifier belongs in the role's position, where it already appears in full and where a reader looking for it will find it.

## What to fix

The tally counts the declared STANCE WORD; the qualifier stays on the position, unaltered. A role that qualified its stance is still not folded into the plain group — group by the full label internally if that distinction must survive, and render the count by word.
acceptance_criteria: A conflict question with a sentence-long qualifier reads as a countable tally; the qualifier still appears in full on that role's position; a test drives the case observed on run-20260811001658945
notes: 2026-08-10: found on a live wave-B stakeholder packet run, not in a fixture — the qualifier that broke it is one a real model actually wrote. DISPATCH: any tier; self-contained in src/kernel/run/conflicts.ts (frameConflict's tally) with tests in tests/kernel/run/conflicts.test.ts. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sources declared on a non-default workspace are unreachable: construct outcome hardcodes 'default'
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. construct source add --kind=directory --locator=./docs --workspace=waveb
2. construct source list --workspace=waveb  → the source is there
3. construct outcome 'anything'
4. construct plan <run-id>  → 'no sources declared'

## What happens

construct source add, source list, and mode all accept --workspace. construct outcome does not: every call site passes the literal 'default' to the planner (src/cli/index.ts, the planRun calls in the outcome paths). Since the plan is what records sourcesDeclared, and construct work grounds from plan.sourcesDeclared, a source declared on any other workspace can never reach a run. The surface accepts the flag on one command and silently ignores the concept on the next.

construct ask, added 2026-08-10, does take --workspace and passes it through, so the two question surfaces now disagree about whether workspaces exist.

## Why it matters

Workspaces are the mechanism for pointing different runs at different ground — a bounded ground for a cheap local model, the whole repository for a stronger host. Today the only reachable ground is whatever the default workspace holds, so changing ground means retiring and re-declaring sources in place, which mutates the record every other run is read against.

## What to fix

construct outcome takes --workspace, defaulting to 'default', and passes it to planRun the way ask already does. Check mode/engagementMode on the same path — it is read per workspace and is subject to the same hardcoding.
acceptance_criteria: construct outcome --workspace=<name> plans against that workspace's declared sources and engagement mode; a test drives it through the CLI and asserts the plan's sourcesDeclared; the default stays 'default'
notes: 2026-08-11: fixed. construct outcome takes --workspace and threads it to planRun (all five call sites passed the literal 'default'); engagementMode rides the same path. The plan line names a non-default workspace. CLI test in tests/cli/spine.test.ts asserts plan.sourcesDeclared is empty on default and populated on the named workspace. Landed on feat/source-reads. The reproduction source src-20260811001046179 on workspace 'waveb' can now be retired.
close_reason: construct outcome --workspace plans against that workspace's sources and mode; CLI test asserts plan.sourcesDeclared; default unchanged

title: A 35b local model cannot finish a grounded dispatch inside the pinned host's 10-minute timeout
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Declare a large local ground: construct source add --kind=git --locator=<a 356-document repository>
2. construct outcome --host=opencode --model=ollama/qwen3.6:35b --binary=/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode '<any outcome implicating several concerns>'
3. construct work --run <id> --ceiling=5

## What happens

Every dispatch fails at exactly 600000ms with InvocationTimeoutError: 'Host opencode invocation exceeded 600000ms'. Observed 2026-08-10 on run-20260810235757089: 40 documents surveyed from one source, four roles dispatched at concurrency 2, product-scoping and program-sequencing both failed at the ten-minute mark having produced nothing.

## Why it matters

The stakeholder-acceptance program says packet cases run on the cheapest host that produces honest output, and the cheapest reachable host is a local Ollama family. If a 35b-class local model cannot complete a grounded dispatch over a real repository inside the pinned timeout, then the free path is not merely lower quality on large ground — it produces nothing at all, and the failure costs ten minutes per role before it says so. That is a capability floor worth recording the way construct-3w9 recorded the namer floor, rather than rediscovering per run.

## What to decide

Whether the answer is (a) a per-host timeout the adapter declares and the coordinator respects rather than a fixed 600000ms, (b) a documented ground-size ceiling for local families, (c) both, or (d) recording the floor and leaving the timeout alone. Note the lease default (15 minutes) already exceeds the host timeout by design, so the tasks failed cleanly rather than being duplicated.
acceptance_criteria: The floor is recorded where a user meets it before spending ten minutes on it, and either the timeout becomes host-declared or the ground-size limit for local families is documented with the measurement behind it
notes: 2026-08-11: fixed as option (c). Adapters declare invocationTimeoutMs instead of hiding it; --timeout=<minutes> sets it on outcome/ask/notes/work; work refuses a limit at or past its lease, since a task outliving its lease is dispatched twice and paid for twice. src/hosts/floors.ts carries dated per-model throughput observations and construct work prints the nearest one before dispatching, with the model it was measured on, the evidence (phase-5 Case 0), and both ways out. A timeout failure line now names the flag that moves the wall. docs/model-family-promotion.md records the throughput floor beside the contract floor for qwen3.6:35b. Four CLI tests cover it.
close_reason: Floor surfaced before the spend; timeout host-declared and caller-settable; measurement recorded in docs/model-family-promotion.md

title: construct outcome crashes with an unhandled EPIPE when its stdout is closed early
description: Piping any CLI command that writes after the plan section into a short reader crashes the process with an unhandled 'error' event and a full Node stack dump. Reproduce: node bin/construct.mjs outcome '<text>' | head -1. The throw is at planRun (src/cli/index.ts:443) writing to a stdout whose reader has gone away. Piping into head, less, or grep -m1 is ordinary use, and a stack dump on it reads as a broken tool. Fix: handle EPIPE on process.stdout (treat a closed stdout as a normal end, exit quietly) rather than letting the write throw. Check every CLI write path, not just planRun — the same crash is reachable from any command that writes more than the reader consumes.
acceptance_criteria: node bin/construct.mjs outcome '<text>' | head -1 prints the first line and exits without a stack trace or unhandled error event; a test covers a CLI write to a closed stdout
notes: 2026-08-10: found while verifying the five wave-B packs through the shipped surface (construct-yx7). Not folded into those closes — it is a CLI robustness defect, not a pack defect. DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better; self-contained (src/cli/index.ts is the whole surface). Close gate: the full repo gate.
close_reason: Fixed: EPIPE on stdout/stderr ends the process quietly; test spawns through a shell and was verified to fail without the fix.

title: Per-lens claim volume is unbounded, so a run sweeps the corpus instead of working its lens
description: In the tuned-family sweep each single-lens dispatch produced 13 to 23 claims, against 3 to 6 from the local family. Nothing in the lens prompt bounds how much a role produces, and the volume is what lets a run collect other roles' planted findings on the way past — the mechanism behind ten of thirteen plants failing discrimination. This is a product question, not only a harness one: a real deliverable is not 23 findings, and a role that reports everything it noticed has not exercised judgment about what belongs to it. Decide whether the lens prompt should bound output (a stated budget, or an explicit instruction to drop findings another lens owns), measure the effect on discrimination, and record the result either way.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded comparison of discrimination and per-lens hit rate with and without a claim bound, on the same corpus and family; a decision recorded with its reasoning; whatever ships is in the committed lens prompt, not in a session
close_reason: Measured on both prompt shapes, same corpus and family: bounding ownership cut claims 190->106 (44%) and off-lens earnings 55->29 (47%) with no role losing its own plant, so the bound ships (ROLE_OWNERSHIP_BOUND in kernel/run/grounding.ts, imported by the fixture prompt, drift test both ways). It changed no plant verdict, so it does not rescue the depth measurement: still 1/13 discriminating. Volume is refuted as the explanation for the collisions.

title: The security plant is a paraphrase, not a plant: replace the inserted paragraph, not its grading entry
description: Two scored runs (2026-08-10-security-qwen, 2026-08-10-security-qwen-r2) both missed while reasoning correctly about the impersonation privilege boundary. Root cause is the corpus paragraph inserted into notes/note-1.md: it restates a mechanism the corpus already documents in rfc-001-sync-impersonation.md and in note-1's own pre-existing paragraph. A plant must be discoverable ONLY by combining the inserted text with a partner document; this one gives a correct finding several valid citation pairs and no plant-specific one, so the key cannot discriminate. Fix by replacing the inserted PARAGRAPH with a mechanism the corpus does not already state, then key it to the pair that carries it. Both recorded runs keep their scores; the new plant is committed before any run scored against it.
acceptance_criteria: A replacement paragraph that states something the corpus does not already say elsewhere; a keyed entry committed before any run scores it; a fresh clean-context security run recorded with its score, hit or miss
notes:

The real defect is the opposite one and larger: TH2 was also earned by six lenses that do not own it, so it cannot measure the security lens either way. Superseded by the plant-replacement work.

2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): closed as refuted, not fixed: the tuned-family sweep showed the plant is reachable, so there was nothing to change. Benign.
close_reason: Refuted by the tuned-family sweep: the plant is reachable (security run earned TH2). The genuine defect is non-discrimination, which is construct-eh1's scope.

title: Postconditions are declared on every brief and never validated in the dispatch path
description: satisfyBrief attaches registered postcondition ids to every brief (src/kernel/brief/satisfy.ts), and commitment 10 binds the declare/satisfy split, but validateBinaryPostconditions is never called anywhere in src/ — only from tests and the legacy capture script. So a brief can declare a binary obligation that nothing ever checks, which is the asserted-not-measured shape the project exists to prevent. Decide and record which is true: (a) challenges plus template slots superseded binary postconditions for prose deliverables, and the mechanism should be retired from the brief surface with STRATEGY commitment 10 amended to say challenges are the satisfied obligation; or (b) postconditions are real and the deliverable path must call the validator, which requires a packet shape carrying the fields a rule reads. Found 2026-08-10 while deleting the v2 fossil rules.
acceptance_criteria: Either the mechanism is retired from the brief surface with a dated STRATEGY amendment, or validation runs in the dispatch path with a test proving a violating deliverable is caught; no brief declares an obligation nothing checks; full gate green
close_reason: Resolved as option (a) with a dated clarification rather than by wiring a validator that could not judge prose. Commitment 10 now records that the challenge catalog and the template's required slots are what verify a deliverable today — both run on every dispatch and fail loudly — while binary postconditions remain the seam for a machine-checkable output packet, with no rule shipping registered and packs registering their own. The module doc states what it is NOT, so the next author does not register a rule against a prose role. No brief declares an obligation nothing checks: live briefs declare none and the registry is empty. Full gate green.

title: Base org coverage: every concern a cross-functional team owns is routable, carries stated obligations, and is attributed
description:
Gerald (2026-08-10, in chat): hardening around organizational contracts must not be the only foot in the door. Construct needs the base set of concerns, obligations, and checks that lets it actually help teams across the org: product, engineering/architecture, legal, program management, design/UX, strategy, operations/support, research, requirements gathering, conflict resolution. Titles map to CONCERNS, not to literal job-title personas: Architect is the system-design concern, VP/Director is the strategy-altitude concern, Support/Platform land in operations and system-design. The org tree and the wave plan live in docs/org-coverage-plan.md.

REFRAMED 2026-08-10 (construct-1pj, and see this epic's NOTES). This epic originally read 'routable, deepened, and measured'. Per-role depth is retired as a claim: differing question sets over one model do not produce differentiated findings (RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md sections 14-15). What survives, and what this epic delivers, is the three jobs that never depended on differentiation — ROUTING (a concern is implicated from wording that never names it, so nobody is ambushed by a domain they did not know existed), OBLIGATION (what that concern's deliverable owes, as slots a checker can see), and ATTRIBUTION (the work log says in whose name each finding was written).

## Success Criteria
Every concern in the target org tree (docs/org-coverage-plan.md) either routes through the namer and carries a lens stating its obligations, or carries a dated recorded decision that it deliberately does not. No lens is silently unreachable. Every pack closes on unit tests plus one run through the shipped surface — NOT on a harness plant hit, which is the withdrawn criterion. Wherever coverage is claimed on any surface, it carries its measured routing accuracy or an explicit unverified tag; asserted completeness is a defect. Rubrics for the new concerns pre-committed before judging; one stakeholder packet case per new concern recorded and accepted or rejected by Gerald. No cross-user claim anywhere.
notes:
2026-08-10 WAVE A CLOSED, WAVE B CODE LANDED. Gerald accepted the Phase 5 packet Case 1 and directed execution of all filed work, which is the dated amendment opening wave B; recorded here rather than inferred. Wave A: nmh, xhe, j5k closed. Wave B code: alo, gzw, sqx, xh7, phe landed with unit tests and verified routing, all five held open on the harness-plant criterion pending construct-pmn. Defects found and fixed along the way: ekv (punctuation and internal-stopword keywords could never fire; two shipped keywords were dead), 83y (lens ceiling never rendered into the dispatch). Defect found and filed, not fixed: oxc (postconditions declared on every brief and never validated). Measured cost of five new domains, recorded not waved off: labeled over-rate 0.143 to 0.250, held-out 0.140 to 0.229, miss rate unchanged at 0.027/0.026, targets 0.15 miss and 0.6 over. The labeled corpora predate every new domain, so no outcome carries their labels and every fire scores as an over-fire whether or not it was right — the number is an upper bound on the real over-rate, not a measurement of it.
2026-08-10 REFRAMED under the depth retirement (construct-1pj). This epic's title and success criteria were written on the premise that each concern would be 'deepened and measured', where deepened meant a lens reaching findings other lenses could not, and measured meant a clean-context harness run hitting a plant that lens owns. That premise is rejected on external evidence and the isolation criterion is withdrawn, not suspended: RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md sections 14-16, STRATEGY Phase 4 (fourth 2026-08-10 amendment) and Phase 5 (fourth amendment), docs/org-coverage-plan.md (second 2026-08-10 amendment). READ THIS BEFORE WORKING ANY CHILD: a session working top-down from bd ready must not restart depth work on the strength of an old title. The harness plant hit is NOT in any close path, so the wave-B hold on construct-pmn recorded in the entry above is lifted. Do not author replacement plants, do not re-run a discrimination sweep, do not describe any pack as at depth. What this epic now delivers is the surviving claim, which is smaller and fully checkable: each concern routes from wording that never names it, carries its obligations into the deliverable template as slots a checker can see, and is attributed in the work log — with routing quoted as a measured figure rather than asserted as completeness.

2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (open-but-named): commits name it because work under the base-coverage program landed; the epic's exit is coverage across every concern a cross-functional team owns, which no single commit completes. Stays open deliberately.
2026-08-20 Re-read under the recorded direction decision of 2026-08-20 (RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 22): base org coverage serves the kernel-as-backbone half of the program. Its three surviving jobs (routing, obligation, attribution) are unchanged; the skills wedge is a separate epic and does not depend on this one. The standing do-not-restart-depth instruction is unchanged.

title: construct watch accepts --root and ignores it: the Watch is hardcoded to Construct's own ground
description: Found by the grounded PRD run's own deliverable (run-20260810161440172): src/cli/index.ts:1758 builds the Watch as { id: 'construct', ground: CONSTRUCT_GROUND } regardless of the --root flag the command accepts, so watch --root=/some/other/repo gathers evidence from that root but reconciles it as findings about Construct's tracker and repo. Phase 3 scopes the shipped watch to Construct itself (external watches wait for Phase 4), so the fix is honesty, not breadth: either refuse --root pointing anywhere but this repo with a sentence citing the phase gate, or stop accepting the flag until external ground ships. A flag that is accepted and ignored is drift by construction.
acceptance_criteria: watch --root pointing at foreign ground either refuses with the phase-gate reason or the flag is gone; test covers the refusal; no external-watch capability is implied anywhere
close_reason: Fixed with a CLI test. --root was passed to evidence gathering but the Watch identity stayed hardcoded, so pointing it at another repository gathered that repository's evidence and recorded findings under Construct's own ground — a record naming ground the evidence did not come from. The watch reports drift between this project's strategy, tracker, and repo, so --root selects which CHECKOUT of Construct to inspect; a root that is not a Construct checkout is now refused by name, and the message says what the flag actually selects. Full gate green.

title: The claude adapter reports no model identity, so the tuned family is logged best-effort
description: Observed on the first grounded dogfood run (run-20260810161440172, 2026-08-10): dispatching on the claude host without --model logs 'model-untuned-best-effort ... model unknown: no tuning evidence for this family' even though claude is the tuned family (src/hosts/claude/adapter.ts sets no default model field and modelTuning gets undefined). The degradation note is doing its job — silence is not compliance — but the silence is the adapter's, not the model's: claude CLI resolves a default model the adapter could report (claude --version proves the binary answers; the invocation output envelope may carry the model id). Fix: surface the resolved model (or at least the family) from the adapter so tuning/tier notes state facts rather than unknowns.
acceptance_criteria: A claude-host dispatch with no --model records the resolved model or family in role-dispatched detail; the untuned note fires only for genuinely untuned families; test covers the adapter's model reporting
close_reason: The dispatch record now carries modelFamily and modelTuned resolved from the adapter, so a tuned run states its family instead of the family reaching the log only when tuning is absent. Tests cover both the tuned host and a host that will not say.

title: Ask the staff: a lightweight grounded question surface that answers without a four-role fan-out
description: Stakeholder requirement (Gerald, 2026-08-10, twice): a role 'can be asked questions' — operate as the team's PM you can turn to, not only a batch pipeline. Today a question must be phrased as an outcome and pays the full fan-out (multi-role dispatch, challenges, stance framing), which is the wrong weight for 'what does our roadmap say about X?'. Design sketch, to be validated not assumed: construct ask '<question>' runs the same spine with the namer choosing ONE primary domain, grounded material as construct work builds it, and a single dispatch whose deliverable is the answer with citations; no stance protocol, no conflict framing, challenges limited to claims-cited. Fail-open and host-agnostic like everything else. No new runtime, no new store shapes: a question is a run whose plan has one step. The behavioral north star holds: the user never types a role name.
acceptance_criteria: construct ask over a workspace with declared sources returns a cited answer from one grounded dispatch; the run is on the work log like any other; a question implicating a high-risk domain says so rather than silently answering; tests drive the CLI surface
notes: 2026-08-10 DISPATCH: Fable/Opus-class for design+implementation in one session; self-contained (spine commands in src/cli/index.ts, grounded dispatch in src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts, namer selection in src/kernel/run/outcome.ts). Close gate: full repo gate. Serves the end-state UX (STRATEGY r67.20 'asked questions' half) and Phase 5.
