title: The product-scoping deliverable is a product requirements document, not a padded memo
description: Stakeholder direction (Gerald, 2026-08-10): pointing Construct at a repo and asking for a PRD is the named first use. The product-scoping template ships as a 'scope memo' (in-scope/out-of-scope over the core slots), which is not the deliverable a PM hands a team. Deepen it into a product requirements document with checkable slots — users-and-problem, success-measures, phasing — and give program-sequencing a milestones slot, so 'thoughtful templates' is sufficiency a check can hold, not prose. Slots stay honest for small models: anything unknowable from the material is an [assumed]/[unverified] entry, never a reason to withhold.
acceptance_criteria: playbookFor('product-scoping') yields a product requirements document template whose slots cover users/problem, scope both ways, success measures, phasing; program-sequencing carries milestones; workProductDirective renders them; tests assert the shapes
close_reason: product-scoping deliverable is now 'product requirements document' with users-and-problem, in-scope, out-of-scope, success-measures required and phasing optional; program-sequencing gains milestones. Tests assert shapes; full suite green.

title: Requirements gathering as a first-class move: a role that lacks what it needs asks through the inbox instead of assuming everything
description: Stakeholder direction (Gerald, 2026-08-10 chat): operating as a TPM/PM means knowing when to gather requirements before executing on a strategy. Today the assignment tells roles to label gaps [assumed] and deliver — right for one-shot dispatches, wrong when the missing fact is genuinely the user's to give and cheap to ask. Design: a role may propose a requirements question as part of its deliverable; the kernel (never the role — commitment 14) turns qualifying questions into decision-inbox items shaped as commitment 11 contracts (what triggered it, the reversible default if unanswered, which role would normally have asked). The dispatch remains fail-open: an unanswered question never blocks the deliverable, it qualifies it. Guard against the failure mode where every run nags the user — asking is for facts that change the work, not coverage for the role's uncertainty.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatched role can surface a requirements question that arrives as an inbox decision with a reversible default; the deliverable ships regardless, labeled with the assumption; a test covers question -> inbox -> decide -> a later run consuming the answer
close_reason: ASK/ASSUMING protocol in every assignment; kernel parses at settle and raises at most one open ask per run (suppressions logged); frameAsk carries question + reversible default as the two positions; answeredAsksFor feeds later dispatches with '[cite:user answer]' discipline. Unit + real-settle-path e2e (ask -> inbox -> decide -> later dispatch consumes). Full gate green incl. smoke.

title: Codebase-scale grounding: the role reads beyond the listed cap through the host, and the record stays honest
description: The producer lists at most 40 documents per source (prose ranked first) and records the remainder as a partial read. For a PRD over a real codebase that is the right honesty but the wrong ceiling: the role's host can read anything in the tree, and the assignment already names the ground root via the partial row. What is missing is the design for reads the kernel did not list: either (a) the assignment licenses the role to read within declared source roots and cite by path, with the citation challenge validating cited paths fall inside a declared root (extending the fabricated-provenance gate), or (b) a richer survey (host-model-chosen relevant set). Option (a) is the fail-open, no-connector shape and the likely answer; decide with evidence from the first grounded dogfood run.
acceptance_criteria: A run over a large repository produces citations to documents beyond the listed cap that the provenance gate accepts iff they exist under a declared source root; the read record says what was licensed vs listed

title: The plan says 'grounded in N declared sources' from a field that only counts declarations
description:
Plan.sourcesConsulted is built in src/kernel/plan/planner.ts as input.sources.map(s => s.id) — every source declared on the workspace, whether or not anything read it. Nothing in src/ reads a declared source at all, so the field counts declarations and is named for consultation.

The CLI print hedges honestly enough ('grounded in 3 declared sources', src/cli/index.ts), but 'construct plan <run>' prints 'sources: <ids>' with no such qualifier, and the field name is what any future caller will trust. A field named for what it does not measure is how an overclaim gets inherited by the next reader.

Cheap and independent of the larger question of whether Construct should read sources itself: either rename the field to sourcesDeclared, or keep the name and populate it from recorded reads once those exist.
acceptance_criteria: The field's name matches what it holds; no shipped surface implies a source was read when only a declaration exists; test covers the wording

title: The notes-drop distractor discipline is harness-only: the product can record a decision the notes parked
description:
The org-harness notes pass carries an explicit paragraph forbidding a delta that records a parked or undecided item: 'Where the notes park something or say a question needs an owner, that is not yours to record as decided... if the words say "parking that", "needs an owner", "not deciding here", or anything of that shape, it is not a delta.' The answer key's distractorGate credits exactly that paragraph: 'five distractor-disciplined runs all clean; every run before the discipline paragraph violated at least one.'

That paragraph lives in scripts/org-harness-producer-prompt.mjs. The product's shipped producer prompt is src/hosts/contextloop.ts producerPrompt(), and it does not carry it — its nearest wording is 'never to invent, improve, or conclude beyond their words' and 'Do not reach', neither of which distinguishes a settled decision from a parked one. The two prompts also emit different shapes (product: deltas/proposals/observations; harness: proposals/deltas).

Recording a parked item as a settled delta is fabrication of agreement — a provenance-class failure the scorer gates rung 3 on, and the one thing the trust kernel forbids. The product is not undefended: challengerPrompt() runs an independent refutation pass and can refuse a delta that 'smuggles in a conclusion the line does not carry'. Whether it actually catches this class is unmeasured, and an unmeasured defense is what commitment 15 says not to count.
acceptance_criteria: Either the settled-vs-parked discipline ships in producerPrompt(), or the challenger is measured against planted parked items and shown to refuse them; the harness and the product state the same rule, verified by a test that reads both
close_reason: The settled-vs-parked rule is now a single exported constant (SETTLED_VS_PARKED_RULE in src/hosts/contextloop.ts) carried by the shipped producerPrompt, with the fixture-organization prompt importing it instead of holding a copy. Two tests assert both state it verbatim, so the product and the instrument cannot drift apart silently.

title: construct log hides the recorded reason on failure entries: namer-failed reads as a bare action
description:
Found during the stakeholder-acceptance runs (construct-9xq), on a real run through the shipped CLI: run-20260806032817359, host opencode, model ollama/qwen3.5:4b.

The store records the whole reason. The work_log row for namer-failed holds {"outcome":...,"host":"opencode","failure":"the host replied with malformed JSON","fellBackTo":"keywords"}. The CLI shows none of it: src/cli/index.ts log() prints seq, timestamp, role, action, and howInferred(detail) only, so the line reads 'construct namer-failed' with no reason and no fallback named. The reason was printed on stdout when the outcome was recorded, which means it survives only in the terminal that produced it — anyone reading the run afterwards sees that something failed and cannot see what.

This contradicts what docs/first-run.md promises of the log ('It records what was inferred and why, what was dispatched to which model, and what came back') and it defeats the point of an append-only record: the honest-degradation design writes the reason down and the reading surface drops it.

Fix direction: render the detail for entries whose detail carries a failure or degradation (namer-failed, model-untuned-best-effort, extraction-refused, voice-overridden are the known set) rather than adding a --verbose nobody will pass. Keep the one-line-per-entry shape; a reason clause on the entries that have one is enough. Do not widen this into a general detail dump.
acceptance_criteria: A run whose namer failed shows the failure reason and the fallback on the log line; the known degradation/refusal entry kinds each render their recorded reason; a test asserts the reason reaches stdout for at least namer-failed and model-untuned-best-effort; full repo gate green
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: minimum tier Sonnet-class or better. Self-contained: the renderer is log() in src/cli/index.ts around line 1362; howInferred() is the existing hint helper. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Fixed: reasonClause renders the stored detail on namer-failed, namer-retried, model-untuned-best-effort, model-floor-degraded, extraction-refused, role-failed, dispatch-halted, voice-overridden; end-to-end test proves the reason reaches stdout. Landed on main.

title: Distractor discipline: decide whether DX1/DX2 gate a rung
description:
The org-harness answer key plants two items the notes explicitly park or leave to an owner (note-1's unowned stage-branch promoter, note-2's undecided strategy-vs-PRD question). Writing either up as a memory delta records a resolution the organization never reached — fabricated agreement, which commitment 15 forbids. Until 2026-08-05 these lived in the key as prose and gated nothing, so three lens runs violated both while showing four rung passes. They are now encoded as distractorChecks DX1/DX2 in fixtures/org-harness/answer-key.json and reported by scripts/score-org-harness.mjs, deliberately non-gating so runs already recorded keep their as-run scores.

The open question is whether a distractor violation should FAIL a rung going forward — rung 3 is the context loop and is where memory deltas are scored, so that is the natural home. Arguments for: fabricating a decision is a rung-0-class provenance failure, not a style note, and a reported-only check is one nobody has to act on. Arguments against: the two distractors are keyword-matched like the plants, so a gate inherits the same vocabulary-artifact risk that has already produced four dated keyword amendments, and a false FAIL on the trust-kernel rung is expensive. Decide with the evidence of the distractor-disciplined runs (recorded 2026-08-05 onward) in hand: if the fixed prompt keeps DX1/DX2 clean across several runs, gating costs nothing and closes the hole.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on this bead with its reasoning: gate at rung 3, keep reported-only, or gate behind a run count. If gating, the scorer change ships with tests and the answer key records the date the gate began, leaving prior runs' as-run scores untouched.
notes:
2026-08-05 EVIDENCE UPDATE: distractor-disciplined evidence now stands at four clean runs — two single-pass (fable-lens-disciplined-run1/2) and two composed dispatch-shape runs (fable-composed-run1/2), all DX1:clean DX2:clean with the notes-drop discipline paragraph in the shipped prompt; a third composed run (run3, on the tuned program-lens question) is also clean. Every run recorded before the paragraph existed violated at least one distractor. The evidence supports gating: the discipline is prompt-carried and holds across both run shapes. Recommendation (Fable, this session): gate DX1/DX2 at rung 3 from the next answer-key date stamp forward, prior runs untouched. Awaiting Gerald's accept before the scorer change ships.

2026-08-05 DECISION (recommended by Fable this session, accepted by Gerald in chat): gate DX1/DX2 at rung 3 from the answer key's declared gate date (2026-08-05) forward; prior runs' as-run scores untouched (score files never regenerated). Shipped in commit 61623eb: scorer fails rung 3 on a violation when the key declares notesDrop.distractorGate; answer key stamped with the gate-start date and evidence note; tests updated (gated violation fails rung 3 and exits 1; a key without a declared gate stays report-only). title: The citation check does not see durations, statute references, or bare quantities
description:
Found while testing the spine challenge defaults (2026-08-05). findUntaggedClaims in src/kernel/verify/claims.ts flags amounts, percentages, and dates. It does not flag 'must be reported within 72 hours of awareness', 'Polish Labour Code art. 22 para 1(1)', or 'three of the five fields of exploitation'. Those are exactly the shapes the isolated first-run simulation produced: the contracts deliverable's statutory citations were entirely invisible to the checker, so claims-cited would have passed a deliverable made of unsourced statute references.

The check is honest about its own scope in its detail string, so this is a coverage gap rather than a false claim of assurance. Widening it is a judgment call with a real cost on both sides: too narrow and the challenge is theatre on legal work, too broad and every role learns to sprinkle [unverified] to get past a matcher.

What to decide: whether a statute-reference pattern and a duration pattern belong in the same checker, or whether legal-issue-spot is the right place for statute claims and this stays numeric.
acceptance_criteria: Either the checker covers statute references and durations with tests over real deliverable text, or the decision to leave them to the substantive pass is written down in claims.ts with its reason; full repo gate green.

title: Lesson admission is risk-weighted, and externally-sourced lessons never auto-admit
description:
Commitment 5: low-risk domain lessons auto-admit after an adversarial verification pass; high-risk domains, legal doctrine above all, require explicit human approval before a lesson goes operational. Commitment 6 adds the rule that overrides risk tier entirely: a lesson whose citation originates from an ingested external document can NEVER auto-admit, because verification by another LLM reading the same attacker-authored text cannot be trusted to catch injected instructions.

What: the admission gate over the lesson store — a per-domain risk tier, an adversarial verification pass for the low-risk path, and human review as the terminal state for high-risk and for anything externally sourced. The external-source rule is not a risk score input; it is a separate gate that runs first and cannot be outvoted.
acceptance_criteria: A low-risk lesson admits only after a recorded adversarial pass; a high-risk lesson cannot admit without a recorded human approval; an externally-sourced lesson lands in human review regardless of tier, proven by a test that gives it the lowest possible risk and still sees it held; every admission decision is recorded with its reason; full repo gate green.

title: A waiver is the user's alone, per deliverable and per challenge, and it is logged
description:
Commitment 13's last sentence: waivers are the user's alone, per deliverable, per challenge, and are logged — never a global off-switch. Nothing implements this today, so a challenge a deliverable cannot satisfy is a dead end with no stated way past it, which is the condition under which people disable checks wholesale.

What: a waiver record scoped to one task and one challenge id, recorded in the append-only work log with who waived it and why, and read by promotion so a waived challenge stops blocking that one deliverable and nothing else. No config key, no environment variable, no --skip-checks: a waiver that can be set once and forgotten is the global off-switch this commitment forbids, arriving by another name. A waived deliverable must be visibly waived wherever its state is reported.
acceptance_criteria: Waiving requires a task, a challenge id, and a stated reason; it is recorded in the append-only log; promotion treats a waived challenge as unblocking for that deliverable only; no global or persistent form of waiver exists; the reported state of a waived deliverable says it was waived and by whom; full repo gate green.
notes: 2026-08-05 DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Shipped. waiveChallenge in src/kernel/run/promotion.ts records the existing 'waived' verdict outcome through the one verdict path, requires a stated reason (unreasoned waivers refused and the refusal logged), and refuses a role waiving its own challenge. Promotion now reports waived challenges so a waived 'final' never reads like a survived one. CLI: construct waive --task --challenge --reason. No global form exists by construction. Full gate green (1493 tests, smoke pass).

title: SHORTLIST_K is 4 in code while the measurement that derives it says 8
description:
src/kernel/implication/escalate.ts:117 ships SHORTLIST_K = 4. The re-measurement of 2026-08-04 (RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md §5, run over all four corpora) reports the smallest k covering every keyword-missed label is now 8 (AUC 0.787), and the document itself flags the constant as a follow-up it cannot change on its own authority. As shipped, escalation under a live embedder narrows the namer to a candidate list measured NOT to cover the misses — the narrowed-and-therefore-wrong case the module header explicitly forbids.

The constant's own comment states the rule: re-derive, do not bump. Run
  node scripts/measure-decisions.mjs --embeddings --section 5.5
and set the value the script prints, updating the comment's derivation note (date, corpus set) so the next drift is visible the same way this one was.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read SHORTLIST_K at src/kernel/implication/escalate.ts:117 — it is 4.
2. Run node scripts/measure-decisions.mjs --embeddings --section 5.5 (needs local ollama with nomic-embed-text) and read the "smallest k covering every keyword-missed label" line — it prints 8 on the current corpora.
3. Any escalation with a live embedder therefore hands the namer a 4-domain shortlist that the measurement shows excludes known keyword-missed labels.
acceptance_criteria: SHORTLIST_K equals the value the section 5.5 script derives on the current corpora; the comment cites the re-derivation date and corpus set; escalate tests green; full repo gate green.

title: Measure the model-coder proxy against the stakeholder's own verdicts (single-annotator; the human floor is permanently unmeasured)
description:
Rewritten 2026-08-05 after Gerald's decision that the program recruits no external subjects. The original bead (Stage 2 of construct-2jb.3) was to recompute Krippendorff's alpha over HUMAN labels from >=2 human-labeled sources and so lift the permanent caveat on Stage 1's model-coder alpha of 0.7627. That is now unreachable by construction, not data-gated: inter-human alpha needs at least two humans and this program has exactly one. There is no human annotation floor to measure and no inter-human disagreement to compute, so the Stage 1 caveat (observed alpha is an upper bound on independent agreement; the derived floor a lower bound) is permanent WITHOUT qualification. Any wording anywhere that says the caveat holds 'until Stage 2 lands' is now a false promise and is corrected — RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 2 carries the dated amendment.

What one human CAN settle is narrower and still worth having: does the model-coder proxy track the stakeholder's own judgment? Measure agreement between Gerald's run-derived verdicts (inbox confirm/dismiss/missed decisions made in the course of real use — the harvest path from construct-2jb.13 already ships: append-only feedback store, verdict CLI, fixture-shaped export) and the model panel's labels on the same outcomes. Report it as single-annotator agreement against a model reference. It is NOT an inter-human floor and must never be quoted as one: a high figure licenses continuing to use the model panel as a labeling proxy; it does not raise the floor, because a floor is a statement about disagreement between independent humans.

Still gated on real usage producing verdicts — the recorded runs to date are simulations whose verdicts share an author with the system (corpus rule, construct-gsf). The stakeholder-acceptance packet (construct-9xq) is the first path that produces them.
acceptance_criteria: Agreement between Gerald's run-derived verdicts and the model-panel labels computed over the same outcomes with a bootstrap interval (per construct-eib), reported explicitly as single-annotator agreement against a model reference; a stated verdict on whether the model-coder proxy tracked the stakeholder's judgment well enough to keep using it; and an explicit statement that the human annotation floor remains unmeasured and permanently so under this program's design
notes:
2026-08-05 SCOPE CHANGE (Gerald's decision, in chat): no external subjects. Inter-human alpha is unreachable with one annotator; the bead is rewritten to the single-annotator proxy-tracking question and the Stage 1 caveat is now permanent. Do not quote any figure this bead produces as a human agreement floor. Prior NOTES below are kept as the record of what the bead was before this change.

2026-08-05 RELATED: construct-adf adds a cross-family MODEL panel to the 2jb.4 corpus. It does not substitute for the human floor and must not be quoted as if it did — every coder in that panel is still an LLM.
2026-08-05 PROTOCOL: per the stakeholder amendment in CLAUDE.md, this bead never schedules labeling work for Gerald. Its labels are verdicts he records in the course of using the product.

2026-08-13 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (open-but-named): commits landed the dependencies (construct-eib, construct-r67.10); the measurement itself is unrun. Reread under the 2026-08-05 stakeholder amendment: the acceptance wording assumes Gerald supplies verdicts, and no bead may depend on that, so the labels come from the strongest available model with the correlated-error caveat travelling with the numbers. Stays open.
2026-08-20 PRUNE: labelled human. The gate is real usage producing verdicts — Gerald's inbox confirm/dismiss/missed decisions in the course of real use. No session can produce them; the harvest path already ships. When enough exist, the measurement itself is dispatchable.

title: A hedged stance is flattened to an unqualified one: 'proceed with conditions' frames as 'proceed'
description:
Found in construct-185's discriminator run. parseStance() takes the first word of the STANCE line and ignores the rest:

  const word = /^([a-z-]+)/i.exec(raw)?.[1]?.toLowerCase();

So a role that declared "STANCE: proceed with conditions" is recorded as an unqualified "proceed". Observed live on run-20260804174150559, where the accessibility role wrote:

  STANCE: proceed with conditions
  BECAUSE: the outcome is valid but "usable by blind customers" requires specifying which assistive technologies to test with and what success criteria define "usable" before development begins.

and the framed decision reported "1 role(s) say hold, 2 say proceed", counting accessibility among the unqualified proceeds. The role's actual position is much closer to hold: it named a precondition that must be settled before development begins.

This contradicts the module's own stated design. conflicts.ts says it is "strict on the vocabulary and forgiving on the formatting: only the three declared words count" and that "a fourth word ... reads as no stance declared, which is the safe answer because it removes the role from the framing rather than putting a position in its mouth." First-word extraction is not strict on vocabulary; it is a prefix match, and it does exactly what the docstring says the design avoids: it puts a position in the role's mouth, and a more confident one than the role took.

The tolerance is not wrong in itself. It exists so "proceed." and "proceed --" parse, and the live-run decoration handling around it is well-earned. The defect is that the same rule cannot tell a punctuation tail from a semantic qualifier, and the two need different answers.
acceptance_criteria: A stance line carrying a qualifier after the stance word does not silently become the unqualified stance. Whichever way it is settled - treat it as no-stance-declared per the docstring, or carry the qualifier into the framed position so the user sees it - the framing never reports a role as taking a plainer position than it wrote, and the case is covered by a test using the observed 'proceed with conditions' text. Punctuation tails ('proceed.', 'proceed --') must keep parsing.
notes: 2026-08-04 filed from construct-185's live discriminator on ollama/qwen3.6:35b. The exact deliverable text is quoted in the description and is enough to write the test from. Note the tension worth deciding rather than patching: dropping the role entirely (the docstring's answer) LOSES a real position and could turn a genuine conflict into an empty inbox, which is the failure construct-185 exists to guard against; carrying the qualifier keeps the role in the framing but means "proceed" and "proceed with conditions" are no longer the same stance for isConflict(). DISPATCH: judgment, Sonnet-class or better - the choice above is the whole bead. Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: npm test silently runs against a stale gitignored dist/ for every subprocess test
description:
bin/construct.mjs prefers ../dist/cli/index.js over ../src/cli/index.ts whenever dist/ exists ('prefers the built dist/ (packaged install); falls back to src/ in a dev checkout'). dist/ is gitignored build output, and 'npm run smoke' creates it as a side effect of prepack and never removes it. So after any smoke run, a dev checkout permanently contains a dist/ that ages relative to src/.

Every test that spawns the CLI as a subprocess — tests/cli/roleserve.test.ts is the one that caught this — then exercises the STALE BUILD, while the same test's in-process fixture setup exercises src/. The two halves of one test can be running different builds of the codebase.

Found the hard way in construct-2fu: bumping SCHEMA_VERSION from 3 to 4 in src turned four roleserve tests red with 'no response before deadline'. The actual cause, only visible once the child's stderr was forwarded, was the child refusing the store: 'it was written by schema version 4, newer than this build understands (3)'. The test fixture (src, v4) wrote a store the spawned CLI (dist, v3) would not open. Deleting dist/ made all 1342 tests pass with no source change.

The failure mode that matters is the inverse of the one observed: here the stale build caused a false RED, which is loud. A stale dist that happens to be compatible causes a false GREEN — subprocess tests passing against code that is no longer the code under review — and nothing announces it.
acceptance_criteria: npm test gives the same result whether or not dist/ exists. Either the test entry point bypasses bin's dist preference, or the suite refuses to run against a dist/ older than src/, or smoke removes the dist/ it created — whichever is chosen, a test proves the stale-dist case is now detected rather than silently tolerated.
notes: 2026-08-04 filed from construct-2fu, which hit it while bumping the store schema. Reproduce: npm run smoke (creates dist/), edit any src file the CLI subprocess path depends on, npm test. DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better. The judgment is WHICH of the three fixes to take — bypassing bin in tests is smallest but leaves the packaged path untested, and testing the packaged path is exactly what bin's dist preference exists for. Self-contained. Close gate: full repo gate, run both with and without dist/ present.
close_reason: Closed

title: Work the 19 drifts the new tracker reconcile found
description:

title: Accept or reject the sequential phase-gate wording for STRATEGY.md
description:
construct-2jb.9 delivered the derivation and proposed wording for both phase gates (RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 9, commit a18c20b). STRATEGY.md was deliberately not edited: the epic rule is that Gerald decides its wording.

The decision, stated plainly so it can be made without rereading the research:

Phase 5 today reads 'three to five external users have each run a real outcome end to end'. As evidence that is 5/5, which licenses 'works more than about half the time' and ends at the first unlucky failure. The proposal replaces it with a sequential rule (bar 0.70, pass at 95 percent posterior, futility stop at 10 percent, budget 20 subjects) whose measured error rates are type-I 0.103 and power 0.73 against a true rate of 0.90. Those numbers are worse than a reader expects from a gate, and that is the honest cost of a twenty-user budget rather than a defect in the design.

Phase 5 accepted means the gate can now fail, can now cost up to twenty external users instead of five, and licenses a stated 70 percent claim instead of an unstated 'it works'.

Phase 2 keeps its composition quota verbatim (it is stratified sampling guarding a real failure mode) and adds that ten outcomes cannot reach any success-rate boundary, so Phase 2 exits on composition and evidence and makes no success-rate claim at all. That is a subtraction of a claim, not an addition of work.
acceptance_criteria: Gerald accepts, rejects, or amends each of the two proposed wordings; accepted wording is applied to STRATEGY.md and the change names this bead.
notes:
2026-08-04 DECIDED AND APPLIED. Gerald delegated this decision explicitly ('make realistic best practice decisions'). Both proposed wordings from RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 9 are ACCEPTED and now in STRATEGY.md.

PHASE 5: accepted as proposed. Reasoning recorded because the numbers look worse than what they replace and that must not be read as a regression. The old gate COULD NOT FAIL — 5/5 licenses only a one-sided 95% lower bound of 0.549 ('works more than about half the time') and terminates at the first unlucky subject with nothing to say. The sequential rule can fail, can cost up to twenty external users rather than five, and states what it proves. Type-I 0.103 is high for a gate; accepted deliberately as the price of a twenty-subject budget when external users are the program's scarcest resource, and written into STRATEGY as 0.10 rather than hidden.

PHASE 2: accepted as proposed. Pure subtraction of an unsupportable claim. The composition quota is kept verbatim and marked non-negotiable downward (it is stratified sampling guarding a named failure mode); the addition is that ten outcomes cannot reach the section 9 boundary, so Phase 2 exits on composition and evidence and makes NO success-rate claim. The r67.10 external-user probe is re-described in the same edit as first evidence rather than as a rate.

VERDICT: accepted. Decided by Fable, on Gerald's delegated authority 2026-08-04.
close_reason: Both wordings accepted and applied to STRATEGY.md on Gerald's delegated authority. Phase 5 now carries the sequential rule with its real error rates stated; Phase 2 keeps the quota and drops the success-rate claim it could never support.

title: Brief schema declares a minimum model capability tier; dispatcher satisfies or flags it
description:
Serves commitment 10 (briefs declare; a dispatcher satisfies) and the Phase 4 staggered model matrix. Today src/kernel/brief/schema.ts declares inputs, tool capabilities, and postconditions but says nothing about the model executing the task — zero model fields — so a brief whose work needs real judgment dispatches identically to a 4b local model and to Fable, and nothing in the record distinguishes the two.

Two findings make this a measured gap, not a preference. construct-185: the Phase 2 dogfood ran conflict-shaped outcomes on a 4b model and the decision inbox never fired; whether that is honest silence or a model too weak to stake opposing positions is currently undecidable, precisely because no capability floor was declared or recorded. And the opencode usage-blindness precedent: a host reporting cost 0 + steps 0 is unmeasured, not free — claims about what a run demonstrated must be qualified by what model actually ran.

Scope: (1) an optional capability-tier field on the brief schema — a small named ordinal scale (e.g. any / capable / frontier), family-agnostic, defined in GLOSSARY.md terms, never a vendor-model string; (2) satisfy.ts checks the requested host/model against the declared floor and either refuses or dispatches with an explicit degradation flag, per the Phase 4 best-effort-labeled pattern (STRATEGY commitment 3/4 language: stale-loudly, degrade-loudly); (3) the work log records the model identity actually used on every task, so any downstream claim about a run is tier-qualified. The tier-to-model mapping is host-adapter data, not kernel knowledge — the kernel compares ordinals, the adapter says which models it has at which tier.

## Success Criteria
See acceptance criteria.
design: Kernel stays host-agnostic: ordinal tiers in the schema, tier membership declared by each host adapter next to its pin. No vendor lock in kernel vocabulary (mirrors the DISPATCH protocol convention in CLAUDE.md, 2026-08-04).
acceptance_criteria: Brief schema carries an optional model capability floor; dispatching below it either refuses or records an explicit degradation flag in the work log (never silent); every task row records the concrete model identity that ran; construct-185's discriminator re-run can cite the recorded tier as evidence; full repo gate green.
notes:
2026-08-04 filed during beads alignment review; cites commitment 10 and the construct-185 finding. Cross-reference, not an edge: construct-185's discriminator benefits from the recorded tier but does not require this bead to run.
2026-08-04 DISPATCH: judgment (schema + degradation semantics) Sonnet-class or better; mechanical (work-log field, adapter tier tables) any tier. Self-contained: description names the files (src/kernel/brief/schema.ts, satisfy.ts, work log) and the constraint (kernel compares ordinals, adapters own tier membership). Close gate: full repo gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: Run-derived corpus: store and CLI wiring for implication verdicts
description:
Serves STRATEGY risk 1 and Phase 2 exit. The pure core exists (src/kernel/implication/harvest.ts): verdict records (confirmed/dismissed/missed per domain) fold into fixture-shaped corpus outcomes with provenance and negative labels, deterministically.

title: Wire the similarity shortlist into escalation: reach the misses silence cannot
description:
Serves commitment 1. The kernel seam exists and is measured (src/kernel/implication/similarity.ts, RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 5): AUC 0.750 on nomic-embed-text, and all six keyword-missed labels rank in the top 4 of 10 domains by similarity. Awaiting Gerald's call: accept as-is, or file follow-up to compute k from the corpus. Must be revisited when construct-2jb.4 grows the corpus.
2026-08-04 (beads alignment review): DECISION ACCEPTED per Gerald's recommend-and-accept direction — hardcoded SHORTLIST_K=4 with the documented manual re-derivation command is accepted as-is. The mandatory re-derivation when construct-2jb.4 grows the corpus stands (already required by these NOTES and 2jb.4's scope). Recommended by Fable, accepted by Gerald via plan approval 2026-08-04. Closing on that basis.
close_reason: Integration landed 6abd852 and re-measured (AUC 0.750, k=4); the open design question (hardcoded vs derived k) resolved by Gerald accepting hardcoded k with mandatory re-derivation under construct-2jb.4.

title: Phase-gate designs prove far less than they claim — propose sequential replacements
description:
Serves commitment 16 and every phase exit.

STRATEGY.md Phase 5 gates on 'three to five external users have each run a real outcome end to end without typing a role name'. As a statistical test, five successes out of five gives a 95 percent Clopper-Pearson lower bound on the true success rate of 0.478. A gate that reads as 'it works' licenses only the claim 'it works more than about half the time'. The Phase 2 gate (four non-engineering and two legal/compliance of the first ten outcomes) has the same shape — though its composition constraint is genuinely well designed, being stratified sampling that guards a real failure mode: a map tuned to the one distribution its author needs least.

For each gate, state what it currently proves at 95 percent, what n it would need to prove what it appears to claim, and a Bayesian sequential design that stops early on failure and continues until a credible interval reaches a target width. This matters concretely: external users are the scarcest resource in the program, and a sequential design spends them better than a fixed-n one at equal confidence.

Needs Gerald: STRATEGY.md is not edited without his decision.
acceptance_criteria: Per-gate: current proven bound, required n, and a proposed sequential stopping rule; proposed STRATEGY.md wording supplied but not applied.
notes:
2026-08-04 DISPATCH: tier=opus, needs Gerald. Judgment-heavy: proposed STRATEGY.md gate wording, sequential stopping rules, and the argument for each. The arithmetic is already in intervals.ts (clopperPearsonLowerBound) — do not re-derive it, cite the script.
2026-08-04 DISPATCH: pure judgment/research — Fable/Opus-class. Proposal-only: STRATEGY.md is not edited (epic rule); output is derivations + recommended sequential designs in RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md, numbers via the script only. Close gate: every proposed gate names its error rates and stopping rule; full gate.
2026-08-04: Delivered a18c20b. intervals.ts gains posteriorExceeds / credibleLowerBound / sequentialOperatingCharacteristics / sequentialPassBoundary (exact path-lattice enumeration, uniform Beta(1,1) prior chosen so the Beta CDF stays a binomial CDF; the prior's one-imaginary-success cost is stated, not hidden). RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md §9 now carries: per-gate proven bound, fixed-n equivalent (9 consecutive successes for >0.70), the proposed rule (bar 0.70, pass at 95% posterior, futility 10%, budget 20) with its OWN error rates printed by the script — type-I 0.103, power 0.73 at true 0.90, NOT 0.95 — the pass boundary as a table, and the fixed-vs-sequential comparison. Proposed STRATEGY.md wording for Phase 5 and Phase 2 supplied verbatim; STRATEGY.md unmodified per epic rule. Full gate green (lint, typecheck, 1325 tests, smoke). Remaining move is Gerald's accept/reject of the wording — filed separately.
close_reason: Proposal delivered with measured error rates (a18c20b); STRATEGY.md acceptance filed as a separate human-gated bead.

title: Fit and validate the confidence ramps instead of hand-setting them
description:
Serves commitment 15.

The intake ramp emits numbers that look like probabilities (0.55/0.72/0.82/0.92) and nothing checks that they behave like probabilities — that outcomes assigned 0.72 are correct about 72 percent of the time. An uncalibrated confidence is load-bearing here because the EVSI escalation rule consumes it directly.

Produce reliability diagrams, expected calibration error, and the Brier score decomposed into reliability / resolution / uncertainty. The decomposition is the point: it separates 'badly calibrated' from 'genuinely hard', which are different problems with different fixes. Fit with Platt scaling — isotonic regression overfits at current corpus size.
acceptance_criteria: Reliability diagram and ECE reported over the pooled corpus; Brier decomposition stated; ramp refit and the before/after ECE compared with an interval.
notes: 2026-08-04: §6 added to RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md. The ramp (classify.ts's calibratedBaseConfidence, 1/2/3/4+ hits -> 0.55/0.72/0.82/0.92, plus TITLE_LOCK_CONFIDENCE=0.9) belongs to the intake document-type classifier, not the domain-implication path the labeled/held-out/fresh/unspent corpora score -- those corpora label a different classifier entirely (dispatcher.ts/map.ts) that emits no confidence value. The only intake-classifier fixture, classify-golden.json, is a captured-behavior regression lock (predecessor's own output), not an independently adjudicated ground truth, so scoring against it is circular (always 100%). RESULT: no reliability diagram, ECE, Brier decomposition, or Platt refit computed -- none exists to compute, and none was fabricated from a proxy. What real calibration would need (per-bucket sample sizes, ~32-56 documents per hit-count bucket) is stated in RD.md §6 and printed by measure-decisions.mjs --section 6. Full gate green (lint/typecheck/test/smoke).
close_reason: §6 added: no ground truth exists to calibrate the intake ramp (0.55/0.72/0.82/0.92) against -- the only intake-classifier fixture is a captured-behavior lock, not adjudicated truth, and the labeled corpora score a different classifier. No reliability diagram/ECE/Brier/Platt refit computed; none fabricated. Collection cost stated instead (~32-56 docs per hit-count bucket).

title: Replace escalate-on-silence with an expected-value-of-information rule
description:
Serves commitment 1. Supersedes the remaining design scope of construct-2fu.

The current rule escalates iff the keyword pass is silent. Its known limitation, recorded in construct-4jq, is that a confidently-wrong keyword answer is never revisited: 'raffle' fires program-sequencing on the word 'before' and escalation never runs. Silence is the degenerate case of a general rule — escalate when the expected reduction in decision loss exceeds the cost of the call. The general rule also fires in the uncertain band, which is precisely the region the current rule cannot reach.

This needs a calibrated confidence per domain. src/kernel/intake/classify.ts already has that pattern (hit-count ramp 0.55/0.72/0.82/0.92, capped at 0.50 when the top two candidates are within 0.3). Reuse it once fitted rather than inventing a second confidence mechanism — that second mechanism is the drift commitment 16 exists to catch.
acceptance_criteria: Escalation decision expressed as EVSI > c_call using the loss ratio from the threshold bead; measured escalation frequency reported with a Wilson upper bound rather than as an absolute claim; no second confidence mechanism introduced.
notes: 2026-08-05 DRIFT RESOLVED (audit): closed by absorption. Escalate-on-silence itself was removed by the routing inversion (namer primary, keyword map as fallback), so the expected-value-of-information rule this bead proposed has no trigger left to replace. No escalateOnSilence remains in src/. Benign.
close_reason: Mooted by the construct-4jq acceptance (Gerald, 2026-08-05): escalate-on-silence ceases to be the shipped path, so an expected-value-of-information rule for when to break silence has no consumer. Force-closed past the 4jq dep: that edge encoded 'wait for the decision', and the decision fired; the implementation living on 4jq does not resurrect this bead's consumer.

title: Derive MIN_SIGNAL from an expected-loss minimization instead of asserting it
description:
Serves commitment 15.

MIN_SIGNAL=10 is asserted, and map.ts:22 says raising it 'trades recall for precision' without saying at what exchange rate the trade should be struck. The missing object is a loss function. The project already behaves as if it knows the errors are asymmetric — a 0.15 miss target against a 0.6 over target is a 4x asymmetry — but the asymmetry is asserted, never derived, and the two targets were chosen independently.

A miss means a domain is never consulted and the user is told their outcome touched no domain: unrecoverable within the run, and the confident-wrong-answer shape commitment 15 forbids. An over-inclusion means an extra role runs, costs one model call, and produces a visible deliverable the user can dismiss: recoverable and priced.

State c_miss/c_over explicitly as a project parameter, then read the threshold off the precision-recall curve. Report the width of the flat region honestly — if the curve is flat from 7 to 13, then 10 was a fine guess and should be left alone with that fact recorded.
acceptance_criteria: c_miss/c_over stated as an explicit assumption with a sensitivity analysis; PR curve over the pooled corpus; implied optimal threshold reported with the flat-region width; an explicit keep-or-change verdict on 10.
notes: 2026-08-05 Landed. PR curve, flat-region width (11 floor-units, 0-10, two adjacent plateaus at recall 0.637), sensitivity sweep over c_miss/c_over, and the map.ts:22 comment correction. VERDICT: KEEP MIN_SIGNAL=10 — optimal at every ratio >= 0.5; crossover against floor 11 is 0.263, so overturning it needs a judgment that over-inclusion costs ~3.8x MORE than a miss, which nobody here has argued. c_miss/c_over deliberately NOT picked: the table says which choices move the verdict and the choice stays Gerald's. Work was authored by a dispatched agent that was killed mid-session; the tree was verified, the crossover arithmetic re-derived independently, and the full gate re-run green before commit.
close_reason: Kept MIN_SIGNAL=10, for the measured reason rather than the asserted one. Flat plateau across [0,10] at recall 0.637, cliff at 11 (recall 0.304); optimal at every c_miss/c_over >= 0.5 with crossover 0.263 against floor 11. Ratio left open for Gerald. map.ts comment corrected.

title: Replace flat keyword scores with IDF weighting
description:
Serves commitment 1 (the map is the mechanism behind inferring invisible roles).

dispatcher.ts scores every keyword identically (0/3/7/10), so a domain's score rises with how many keywords its author happened to write — map.ts:88 already documents this as 'catalog verbosity into score'. The formalism it approximates is inverse document frequency: a term appearing across many domains or most outcomes carries little discriminative information.

The evidence this is the right frame: removing 'users' and 'customers' from product-scoping was a hand-rolled IDF correction. Both are high-frequency, low-discrimination terms — exactly what IDF suppresses automatically, without an author having to notice the problem first. Other keywords are likely over-weighted and uncaught; measure per-keyword IDF over the corpus to name them.

Keep the adjacency bonus, which is a real signal IDF does not capture.
acceptance_criteria: Per-keyword IDF measured and the over-weighted keywords named; weighted scoring implemented behind the same seam; non-regression on all corpora with intervals reported, not point estimates.
notes:
2026-08-05 REVERTED, on Gerald's decision, after the close. The weighting was implemented correctly and measured honestly; it is the RESULT that sent it back out, plus one defect in how it got there.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAID: every after-interval sat inside its own before-interval on all four corpora, and under the project's own asymmetric loss framing the pooled point estimate moved the wrong way (E[L] at 4:1, 1.704 -> 1.728; at 10:1, 3.882 -> 3.978). A change buying a generated weight table, a scoring multiply and a regeneration step, for no demonstrated effect and a slightly worse point estimate, is complexity nobody measured a reason for.

THE DEFECT, which matters more than the reversal: the weights were document frequency over outcome TEXT and read no labels, but the normalization pivot REFERENCE_FIRES=3 was chosen by observing that a pivot of 1 collapsed recall on the LABELED corpora — including unspent-outcomes.json, the only unspent one. That is one hyperparameter selected against ground truth while the code and the commit message both stated it was fitted to no label at all. Narrower than tuning a dictionary; the same shape; and the false claim was worse than the choice. This is precisely the circularity construct-gsf named and this epic exists to remove, appearing one level up in the stack, which is where it will keep appearing.

WHAT SURVIVES: scripts/measure-keyword-idf.mjs (renamed from generate-keyword-idf.mjs) prints per-keyword document frequency, IDF, and the weight an IDF scheme would apply. It imports into nothing. RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md section 3 carries the before/after table, the negative result, and the pivot defect. Any future weighting starts from that measurement and must derive its pivot from the frequency distribution alone, or declare it in-sample and spend the corpus it was chosen on.

The bead stays closed: its acceptance criteria asked for IDF measured, over-weighted keywords named, weighting implemented behind the existing seam, and non-regression reported with intervals. All four happened. 'Implemented' and 'kept' are different claims and only the first was promised.
close_reason: IDF weighting implemented behind the keywordScore seam, unsupervised (document frequency over outcome text, not the 83 labels). Non-regression on all 4 corpora: every after-interval sits inside its before-interval (held-out miss 0.026->0.053, over 0.140->0.122; unspent miss 0.663->0.675, over 0.404->0.357; pooled miss 0.363->0.375, over 0.252->0.228) - no statistically demonstrated effect, and pooled E[L] at the project's own 4:1/10:1 ratios is flat to slightly worse (1.704->1.728, 3.882->3.978). Honest negative result, not fitted further to force a win.

title: The decision inbox got zero exercise in the Phase 2 dogfood — determine whether that is correct or a dead path
description:
construct-r67.9's ten outcomes ran 22 tasks to completion across nine domains, including deliberately conflict-shaped pairings (commerce-tax + privacy on charging Europeans in euros; product-scoping + accessibility on blind customers; privacy + product-scoping on a schools pilot). The decision inbox stayed empty the whole time: 'decision inbox: empty. Nothing needs you right now.'

Two readings, and this bead exists because they are not distinguishable from the outside:

  1. Correct. These ten genuinely carry no cross-domain conflict worth a human's decision, and an empty inbox is the honest answer rather than a manufactured one. Inventing a decision would be the same class of failure as missing one.
  2. Dead path. Conflict framing depends on roles producing positions that actually disagree, and the dogfood ran on a local 4b model whose output is generic enough that no two roles ever staked opposing claims. On a stronger model the same ten might well produce decisions.

If (2), then the Phase 2 exit is about to be claimed on a spine whose decision half has never fired outside its own unit tests -- construct-r67.8 is closed and tested, but tested is not exercised, and the whole point of the dogfood is the difference.

Cheapest discriminator: re-run two or three of the conflict-shaped outcomes above on a stronger host (claude --host=claude, or a larger local model) and see whether the inbox populates. If it does, (2) is the answer and the dogfood's coverage claim needs the caveat. If it still does not, read the conflict-detection path against the actual deliverables and say which condition never held.
acceptance_criteria: It is settled which reading is correct, with evidence: either a live run in which the inbox populates and 'construct decide' resolves a real decision end to end, or a written finding naming the specific condition that never held and why an empty inbox is right for these outcomes. construct-r67.9's notes are corrected to match whichever it is.
notes:
2026-08-04 DISPATCH: judgment task, Sonnet-class or better for the analysis; the discriminator re-runs need a strong host model (claude host or a large local model) BY DESIGN — running the discriminator on a 4b model cannot distinguish the two readings, which is the bead's whole point. Self-contained: outcomes to re-run are named in the description. Close gate: the AC's evidence standard plus corrected r67.9 notes.
2026-08-04 cross-reference: construct-ap0 (brief-declared model floor + model identity recorded per task) was filed partly on this bead's finding; once it lands, the discriminator's evidence can cite the recorded tier instead of session memory.
close_reason:
Settled with a live run, the AC's strongest branch. The second reading is right: conflict framing fires; it did not fire on the 4b model. Discriminator: the three conflict-shaped outcomes from r67.9 re-run on ollama/qwen3.6:35b (free, local). All 11 deliverables across 4 runs declared a parseable STANCE line, so the stance-declaration condition holds on a stronger model. One run (blind customers) produced a genuine hold/proceed split, raised run-20260804174150559:stance, framed all three positions with citations, announced it at the end of 'construct work', and resolved end to end through 'construct decide' - after which the inbox was empty again and decision-raised was on the append-only log.

But the two readings were never mutually exclusive per outcome, which is what r67.9's caveat (c) got wrong. Two of the three (charging Europeans in euros; the schools pilot) correctly raised nothing on the 35b model too: every role said hold or unclear, and a unanimous hold is a report, not a decision. isConflict() requires hold AND proceed, and that is right.

So: the r67.8 path is live and correct, the dogfood's empty inbox was a model-capability artifact, and an empty inbox is still sometimes the honest answer. r67.9's caveat (c) is corrected on that bead with the evidence, and its standing limitation is preserved: r67.9 itself provides no live evidence for the inbox path, because a different bead on a different model produced it.

Two defects surfaced while establishing this, both filed rather than folded in: construct-xgi (framing is derived from the tasks settled in the current invocation, so a process dying between settlement and framing loses the decision permanently - observed live, and now an edge blocking r67.10) and construct-gf8 ('proceed with conditions' flattens to an unqualified 'proceed'). Gate: lint, typecheck, 1378/1378 tests.

title: A run killed by dispatcher misconfiguration is terminal with no stated way forward
description:
Found during construct-r67.9's dogfood. NOT a request for a retry policy -- kernel/store/tasks.ts is right that a failed task is terminal and that the host owns retries (commitment 1), and that reasoning should survive this bead intact.

The gap is narrower. The failure I hit was not host-transient: 'construct work --model=ollama/qwen3.5:4b' was dispatched with a model the host could not resolve because the ambient XDG_CONFIG_HOME had been isolated (construct-wl8). Every task in that run failed at once, settled terminally, and the next invocation said:

  nothing to work for run-20260804040423070. Its tasks are already settled.

That sentence is accurate and unhelpful. The outcome the user asked for was never worked, the reason was a flag the user can fix in five seconds, and the surface offers no next step -- not 'file the outcome again', not 'these tasks failed for reason X'. A host retry cannot help, because the host was never the problem. The user is left with a dead run id and no stated path.

Two failure classes are being collapsed into one terminal state: the task the host genuinely could not do, and the task that never reached a working host at all. Only the first is the kind commitment 1 is talking about. Distinguishing them does not require a retry policy -- it requires the surface to say which happened and what the person should do next.

Cheapest honest fix is probably at the CLI, not the store: when a run's tasks are all settled and all failed, say so and name the recourse, instead of reporting the run as settled in the same words used for a run that succeeded.
acceptance_criteria: A run whose tasks all failed reports that fact distinctly from a run that completed, names the recorded error, and states the recourse. The store's terminal-by-design semantics and the no-retry-policy note are unchanged. Covered by a test at whichever surface the fix lands on.
close_reason: Closed

title: Isolating a run's state with XDG_CONFIG_HOME also blinds the host to its own config
description:
Found while running construct-r67.9's dogfood. Pointing construct at an isolated state dir the documented way -- setting the XDG_* variables, exactly as scripts/smoke-packaged-install.sh does for all four -- also reroutes the HOST's configuration, because the adapter spawns the host binary with the ambient environment inherited.

Measured: with XDG_CONFIG_HOME pointed at a scratch dir, 'construct work --host=opencode --model=ollama/qwen3.5:4b' failed every task with 'Model not found: ollama/qwen3.5:4b. Did you mean: ollama-cloud?'. The model exists and 'opencode models' lists it. Isolating XDG_DATA_HOME alone (which is where construct's own store lives) works fine; isolating XDG_CONFIG_HOME is what breaks it, because opencode reads ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json for its provider registrations.

Two things collide in one namespace: construct's state and the host's configuration. A user isolating the first silently disables the second. The failure is at least legible rather than silent -- the task failed with the host's own message and the coordinator recorded it as a failed task, which is the designed behavior -- but the message points at the model name, which is correct, rather than at the environment, which is the cause.

Worth deciding rather than patching reflexively: the adapter could pass the host a deliberately-chosen environment instead of inheriting wholesale, which is also what hosts/claude/mcpconfig.ts already does for the role env (construct-r67.14) -- it puts the server's environment in the config rather than the ambient env. The same seam applies here. The alternative is documenting that only XDG_DATA_HOME should be isolated, which is cheaper but leaves the trap in place for anyone who isolates all four the way the smoke script does.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/scratch construct work --host=opencode --model=ollama/qwen3.5:4b -> every task fails 'Model not found: ollama/qwen3.5:4b. Did you mean: ollama-cloud?'
2. Unset XDG_CONFIG_HOME, keep XDG_DATA_HOME isolated -> the same command works.
3. Confirm the mechanism: 'opencode models' under each env in turn — 6 ollama models listed with ambient config, 0 with the scratch XDG_CONFIG_HOME, because opencode reads ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json for provider registrations.
acceptance_criteria: Isolating construct's state does not change which configuration the host reads, OR the collision is documented at the surface where a user would hit it and the smoke script stops modelling the trap. Either way a run with an isolated state dir reaches the same host configuration as a run without one, and that is covered by a test or the smoke script rather than asserted.
notes:
Reproduce: XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/scratch construct work --host=opencode --model=ollama/qwen3.5:4b -> 'Model not found'. Unset it, keep XDG_DATA_HOME isolated -> works. Diagnosed by running 'opencode models' under each env in turn (6 ollama models listed vs 0).
2026-08-04 DISPATCH: mechanical once the isolation approach is chosen; Sonnet-class sufficient. Self-contained: bug description carries the mechanism. Close gate: full repo gate plus the OpenCode probe (free, local model) proving the host sees its own config under an isolated run.
2026-08-04: while running this bead's gate, found main RED on lint from construct-2fu's commit — src/hosts/namer.ts shipped the retired term 'contract' because lint ran before git add and the linter walks tracked files only. Reworded here (it was English prose meaning a function's contract, not the domain term). That is the second occurrence of construct-fnn's class, so the MECHANISM is now filed as construct-2ua rather than fixed as another instance.
close_reason: Fixed at the seam rather than documented around it. Both adapters spawned their host inheriting process.env wholesale; they now build the environment deliberately (src/hosts/environment.ts), dropping all four XDG variables so the host resolves the configuration and credentials it would have read had construct never been isolated. All four rather than only CONFIG: OpenCode keeps provider auth under XDG_DATA_HOME, so the original 'DATA isolation is harmless' reading held only because it was measured on ollama, which needs no auth. CONSTRUCT_HOST_INHERIT_XDG is the supported way to put the host back under the isolation. Proven as a controlled pair on a real run, not asserted: under all four isolated, the exact command from the repro steps now settles 2/2 tasks; the same run with the escape hatch on fails 2/2 with the original 'Model not found: ollama/qwen3.5:4b'. The depended-on host behavior is now a named, probed expectation (provider-registry-follows-xdg-config-home) checked as a pair so it cannot pass vacuously on a machine with no providers; npm run probe:opencode reports 10 expectations hold. 8 unit tests cover the environment builder. The smoke script was left isolating all four on purpose — with the adapter fixed it no longer models a trap, and narrowing it would remove coverage for no gain. Gate: lint, typecheck, 1378/1378 tests, smoke all green.

title: Register role-serve in OpenCode's MCP config so the write surface is not Claude-only
description: construct-r67.14 wired the role write surface into ONE host (Claude), which satisfies host independence as a proof but not as a property: src/hosts/opencode/adapter.ts still accepts context.roleEnv and ignores it, so a run dispatched to OpenCode has no write surface at all. The shape to copy is src/hosts/claude/mcpconfig.ts -- config to a 0600 file in a 0700 per-invocation dir, the PATH on argv and never inline JSON, disposed on every exit path. What must NOT be copied is the flag vocabulary: OpenCode's MCP registration lives in opencode.json rather than a --mcp-config flag, its env delivery into the server process is unverified, and it may have no equivalent of --strict-mcp-config -- in which case a role would inherit whatever servers the operator has registered, and that is a finding to write down rather than a gap to paper over. Every depended-on behavior becomes a named expectation in src/hosts/opencode/pin.ts and is probed, per this repo's rule. OpenCode probes run on a local model, so unlike the Claude path re-verification is free.
acceptance_criteria: A model running inside OpenCode calls submit_draft and the draft lands in the store attributed to the role; the registration behavior is a named, probed expectation in opencode/pin.ts (including an explicit finding if server isolation cannot be achieved); the bearer appears in no OpenCode session store, argv, or log, verified by inspecting OpenCode's own state after the run.
notes:
2026-08-04 ACCEPTANCE CRITERION NOW MET — closing. construct-ghu's assignment instruction was the missing half, and with it a REAL dispatch exercises the OpenCode write surface end to end.

The run: run-20260804205800193, host opencode 1.15.4, model ollama/qwen3.6:35b, two roles (commerce-tax, contracts), driven through 'construct outcome' then 'construct work' with no hand-written instruction anywhere. Both roles called submit_draft through the registered server and both drafts landed in the store attributed to their roles — work log shows draft-submitted x2 alongside capability-issued x2. That is the AC's first clause: a model running inside OpenCode calls submit_draft and the draft lands attributed to the role.

Bearer leak inspection, the AC's third clause: after the run, ~/.local/share/opencode, ~/.config/opencode and ~/.cache/opencode contain no occurrence of CONSTRUCT_ROLE_TOKEN, CONSTRUCT_ROLE_RUN, or the bearer; the host's stdout and stderr were checked in an earlier probe and carried neither; and no per-invocation config directory survived any run (the one leftover found was a hand-made scratch probe using run-x/t-x and a throwaway secret, not an adapter dispatch — removed).

Second clause, the named probed expectation including the isolation finding: both 'mcp-registered-through-the-config-env-var' and 'no-strict-mcp-config-equivalent-so-servers-are-not-isolated' are in pin.ts and pass the live probe (12/12 hold).

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND MUST TRAVEL WITH ANY CLAIM ABOUT THIS HOST. Server isolation is not achievable here — both config seams merge with the operator's registrations — so a role dispatched to OpenCode can reach whatever MCP servers the operator has registered. Earlier in this session that was not theoretical: a probe model hunting for submit_draft called v2 construct's construct-mcp_find_tool instead, because v2's server is registered on this machine. Naming the tools explicitly in the assignment is what made the model reach the right server this time; it is not a guarantee, and the guarantee does not exist on this host. Removing v2's registration is part of construct-1we.2.
close_reason: Proven by a real dispatch: run-20260804205800193 on OpenCode/qwen3.6:35b, both roles called submit_draft with no hand-written instruction and both drafts landed attributed to their roles. Full gate green (lint, typecheck, 1417 tests, smoke) plus the live conformance probe at 12/12.

title: Register role-serve in a live host's MCP config so a real model can reach the write surface
description: construct-3sa built the whole chain — coordinator mints per dispatch, role env seam, 'construct role-serve' over MCP stdio — and proved it end to end across a real process boundary with a test acting as the host. What no host does yet is launch the server: the OpenCode adapter receives context.roleEnv and ignores it, because wiring it requires host-specific MCP registration (opencode.json mcp entries, env delivery into the server's process) whose behavior on the pinned 1.15.4 must be written as named expectations in pin.ts and probed, not assumed. The Claude Agent SDK path (construct-r67.4) has first-class MCP config and may be the easier first wiring. Until a host launches it, roles have no write surface, which is safe rather than broken.
acceptance_criteria: A model running inside at least one real host calls submit_draft and the draft lands in the store attributed to the role; the host-side registration behavior is a probed pin expectation, not an assumption; the bearer appears in no host transcript, argv, or log (verified by inspecting the host's own session store after the run).
notes:
2026-08-03 PRODUCTIZED AND CLOSED (e6eeea7). src/hosts/claude/mcpconfig.ts writes the MCP config to a 0600 file in a 0700 per-invocation dir; the adapter passes the PATH (never inline JSON -- argv is ps-visible) plus --strict-mcp-config and an allow-list of exactly ROLE_TOOL_NAMES, and disposes on every exit path including timeout. Four new pin expectations + `npm run probe:claude:mcp` (~$0.03/run, sterile XDG store, real HOME so the transcript grep is meaningful). Live probe: conformant on 2.1.216 -- draft landed attributed to privacy, bearer zero hits in ~/.claude/projects + stdout + argv.

TWO GUESSES CORRECTED BY PROBING. (1) The result envelope has NO mcp_servers key on the pinned version, so strict-mcp-config cannot be read from the host's own register; it is measured indirectly by asking the model to enumerate its tools, and pin.ts records that as the weaker check it is. (2) --mcp-config is VARIADIC: `--mcp-config m.json mcp list` failed with "config file not found: .../mcp" and ".../list". title: A store the CLI cannot open crashes with a Node stack instead of a diagnosis

Two defects in one: doctor calls a state dir healthy without ever checking it can be written, and every spine command (outcome, log, inbox, decide) inherits an unguarded openStore, so the user's first contact with a permissions or disk problem is a stack trace naming node:sqlite. Verified through the packaged install: chmod 500 the data dir, doctor now FAILs and outcome prints one sentence, no stack. Smoke covers the reproduction.

title: OpenCode's first-run database migration is not concurrency-safe
description: A live run of 'construct work --concurrency=2' against a fresh OpenCode data dir failed one of three tasks: the concurrent invocations raced OpenCode's own one-time sqlite migration ('Performing one time database migration, may take a few minutes...' then exit 1). The adapter declares the 'concurrent' capability, which is true for session state but not for the host's first-run migration. Options: warm the host once in init() before allowing concurrent invokes, or record the limitation as a named expectation in src/hosts/opencode/pin.ts so the conformance probe checks it. Found while landing construct-r67.5.
acceptance_criteria: A first run at concurrency>1 against a fresh OpenCode data dir does not fail any task, or the limitation is declared and probed rather than hit at runtime.
notes:
2026-08-03: reproduced twice, exact cause captured. stderr: 'Performing one time database migration, may take a few minutes...
sqlite-migration:done
Error: Unexpected error...
Failed to run the query PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL'. Two concurrent 'opencode run' processes race the same sqlite db on first use of a data dir; the loser exits 1 and the coordinator records a failed task. Warming the host with a single throwaway invocation in init() would close it.
close_reason: Fixed (d34816d). The report's premise was too narrow: measured on a fresh data dir, the first open of OpenCode's db can fail ALONE too (lost on CREATE TABLE project), not just concurrently (PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL). Concurrency amplifies, does not cause. Fix: init() warms the db with 'opencode stats' — same database, no model call, so no unmetered spend. Best-effort; when it does not confirm, a first-run gate arms so only one invocation meets a cold db. Gate is NOT armed when warming succeeded (would be pure loss). Verified live at pinned 1.15.4: before, cold dir + concurrency=2 failed 1 of 4 tasks; after, 4 of 4 done. Probe reports 9 expectations holding.

title: Phase 5: Surface + stakeholder-acceptance gate
description:
Outcome-in/decisions-out surface polish. No new roles, hosts, or platform investment until the surface passes stakeholder acceptance: real outcomes run end to end through the shipped surface without typing a role name, recorded as a reviewable packet, read and accepted or rejected by Gerald. Cites STRATEGY.md Program shape, Phase 5 as amended 2026-08-05; commitment 16 (standing scope-delta challenge on this repo's own tracker).

Amended 2026-08-05 (Gerald's decision, in chat): the external-user gate is removed. The program recruits no external subjects — not three to five, not the sequential up-to-twenty design of construct-fgo. What replaces it is a stakeholder-acceptance gate, and it licenses strictly less: nothing about anyone other than the author. The claim the retired design would have bought ('works for more than 70% of users', type-I 0.10, power 0.73 against a true rate of 0.90) is WITHDRAWN, not restated at lower confidence, because self-evaluation is not a sample from the population that claim is about. Any user-facing wording that implies a rate across users is a defect from here forward.

What keeps the measured claims intact without external subjects: measurement independence lives in the instruments, not in who reads the result. The corpora are authored by minds that never saw the catalog; the org-harness answer key is committed before any run and never edited to fit one; scoring is structural. Stakeholder acceptance sits on top of that evidence and is never itself cited as measurement.

## Success Criteria
Per STRATEGY Phase 5 as amended: the surface carries a real outcome end to end without the user typing a role name, recorded and accepted by the stakeholder. No new roles, hosts, or platform investment lands before that. No cross-user success-rate claim is made anywhere in the product, docs, or release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Surface work complete; a stakeholder-acceptance packet recorded and accepted per the construct-9xq pattern; no external-validity or cross-user rate claim appears in any shipped artifact (checked, not assumed)

2026-08-20 Phase 5 redefined by the 7t0 decision: the surface includes skills/ and acceptance is recorded real-work use (the use ledger in construct-54su's falsification test), claims licensed only for outcomes recorded. The no-external-subjects rule is unchanged.

title: The extraction ladder's remediation names 'construct install', a command that does not exist
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. construct install --with-docling
2. Observe: the CLI prints the top-level usage line and does nothing. 'install' is not in USAGE (src/cli/index.ts) and has no case in the command switch.

## What happens

src/kernel/extract/ladder.ts tells the user to run that command in three separate remediation paths (lines 144, 286, 307): the generic docling-unavailable message, the OCR path, and the office-document path. Every one of them is a dead end. A user who hits an unextractable PDF, a scanned image, or a .docx without mammoth is handed an instruction that silently does nothing.

## Why it matters

Remediation text is the one place a user is already stuck, and this project's rule is that a failure names the recourse. Naming a recourse that does not exist is worse than naming none: the user assumes they typed it wrong.

## What to decide

Either build 'construct install --with-docling', or rewrite the three strings to name what actually works today (installing docling directly, or setting DOCLING_SERVE_URL with CONSTRUCT_EXTRACTION_PRIVACY=remote-ok). The strings were ported from the predecessor along with the ladder; the predecessor had that command and this rewrite does not.
acceptance_criteria: Either 'construct install --with-docling' exists and is in USAGE, or no remediation string in src/kernel/extract/ladder.ts names a command this CLI does not implement. A test asserts that every command named in a remediation string is one the CLI dispatches.
notes: 2026-08-11: found while tracing how Construct ingests datasets. Verified by running the command against the installed 3.0.0-alpha.4: prints usage, exits without acting.
close_reason: Three dead remediation strings replaced with working recourse; guard test enforces no src/ string names an unimplemented subcommand

title: A denial flood is the system's own evidence of a role fighting its grants, and it is surfaced nowhere
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a role whose host retries a denied capability call (a record-verdict-shaped call, or repeated submit_draft past the cap).
2. construct log --run <id>; construct doctor

## What happens

Denials accumulate as append-only work log entries per src/cli/roleserve.ts. Neither construct log's run-state footer nor construct doctor reports a count. An operator finds a denial flood only by opening the raw work log and knowing to look for repeated denial entries.

## Why it matters

The denial record was built as evidence that a role is fighting its grants. Evidence nobody is shown is evidence that does not do its job — the same argument that put the limits label on the deliverable body rather than leaving it in the log.

## What to fix

A denial count in writeRunState's footer, or a doctor check, so a run with repeated denials reads differently from a clean one — the way a live lease already does.
acceptance_criteria: A run carrying denials reads differently from one that carries none, on a surface an operator already opens; a test drives it

title: The model-primary namer is unusable on 4b-class local models: record the capability floor instead of discovering it per run
description:
Found during the stakeholder-acceptance runs (construct-9xq): construct outcome --host=opencode --model=ollama/qwen3.5:4b returned malformed JSON from the namer on a plain outcome ('We want to hire a contractor in Poland to help with support'), so the run fell back to the keyword map. Run run-20260806032817359. The designed behavior worked exactly as intended — the failure is stated on screen, a namer-failed entry is written with the reason, and the keyword map answers rather than the run dying — so this is not a defect in the fallback. It is a missing statement of where the primary path actually works.

The matrix already has the vocabulary for this: src/hosts/tuning.ts records which families the producer prompts are validated against and every dispatch on an untuned family writes model-untuned-best-effort. Naming has no equivalent, so a user on a small local model discovers per outcome that the primary namer cannot hold the output contract, and pays a model call each time to find out.

Do the cheap honest thing: measure which local tiers can hold the namer's JSON contract (qwen3.5:4b, gpt-oss:20b, qwen3.6:35b are all installed locally, so this costs nothing but time), record the floor where the matrix stamp already lives, and say it in docs/first-run.md where --host is introduced. Do NOT paper over it with a retry loop or a JSON repair pass — a namer that needs its output repaired is not holding the contract, and hiding that would remove the signal this bead exists to record.

title: The deferred Phase 3 machinery has written data-volume triggers, not intentions
description:

No trigger is written down anywhere, so 'deferred' currently means 'not built yet', which is the same state as 'forgotten'. What: record each deferral in RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md with the number that unlocks it and the derivation for that number (how many lessons before retention pressure is real, how many runs before a heat baseline is learnable rather than fitted to noise, how many scenario evals before the suite can detect a regression at a stated power). Where a number cannot be derived from evidence the project has, say so and record what would have to be measured to derive it — a stated unknown is a deferral; an unstated one is an omission.

title: Review run coordination constants against queueing and timeout theory
description:
Serves commitment 1.

DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY=2, DEFAULT_LEASE_MS=15min, and a spend ceiling checked before dispatch. Lowest-value item in this epic and filed as such — included so the decision surface is covered, not because these constants are suspected wrong.

Concurrency is an M/M/c queue; with per-task service time and the domain-count distribution derivable from the corpora, the latency/cost frontier says whether 2 sits on it. The lease is a timeout against a service-time distribution where too short duplicates work and too long strands it, so the instrument is the hazard rate of task completion — the existing comment establishes only a correctness lower bound (must exceed OpenCode's 10-minute timeout), not a choice of value. The spend ceiling is a knapsack over which domains to dispatch when the budget binds; dispatching score-descending is optimal only if cost is uniform across domains, which is unverified.
acceptance_criteria: Service-time and domain-count distributions measured from the work log; keep-or-change verdict on each of the three constants with its derivation.
